long_description:
Glebe House is located in the picturesque village of Finghall near Leyburn, offering a tranquil and private setting. The property features a beautiful lawned area and a private patio courtyard with a 6-seater hot tub where you can relax and unwind. The ground floor boasts a fabulous open plan kitchen and dining space, well-equipped with everything you need for meal preparation. The dining area with a banquet table sets the stage for special meals with loved ones. After dining, the living area invites relaxation with its comfortable seating and cosy ambiance. For convenience, there is a separate ramped access to an en-suite downstairs bedroom, perfect for guests with restricted mobility.
The first floor houses a luxury master family bedroom with a kingsize four-poster bed and a day bed suitable for a child, the en-suite has a free-standing bath and double walk-in shower. Two more en-suite kingsize bedrooms can be found on this level, each featuring a Smart TV and luxurious amenities. The cosy second floor with vaulted ceilings has two kingsize bedrooms which one can be made up as twin if required. All bedrooms are en-suite and have the luxury of Smart TVs. Outside, a spacious garden with a flagged patio and lawned area provides a sunny spot to enjoy peace and tranquillity, whilst the hot tub is a wonderful addition for family entertainment and relaxation.
The village of Finghall is ideally located between the charming dales market towns of Leyburn and Bedale, making Glebe House a great choice for family holidays or special celebrations. The traditional village inn is within walking distance, offering wholesome food and local ales. The area is perfect for exploring attractions, walks, and cycle routes in Wensleydale. Nature enthusiasts will find numerous walks and cycle routes right from the doorstep, and Leyburn, a bustling market town, is just 5 miles away with interesting shops, restaurants, and a Friday market. The Georgian market town of Bedale, with its charming high street, is also nearby. The surroundings boast numerous castles, picturesque villages, stunning waterfalls at Aysgarth Falls, and the famous Wensleydale Creamery in Hawes. Historic Richmond with its stunning castle and riverside walks, Masham, Ripon, and Catterick Races are all within 30 minutes’ drive. Whether you seek relaxation or adventure, Glebe House’s contemporary design and nearby attractions make it the perfect base for a memorable holiday. Pub within 1 mile.

reviews.comment: Glebe House was difficult to find, possibly due to it being wrongly located on the map. However, once located the outside area and parking was great and the house is very spacious. Also the bedroom details are incorrect in the information provided.The bedrooms and bathrooms were spacious, clean and well appointed apart from all wall mirrors being way too high for the ladies and the pillows were very disappointing. One bedroom had no soap or toiletries. In the kitchen there was only a squeeze of washing up liquid so we had to buy more, also very little kitchen roll and no handwash which we had to buy.It was lovely having so much space for 12 adults and we all enjoyed the house. Some of the kitchen equipment seemed superfluous and yet only one small bowl for serving. Plenty of crockery, glasses and cutlery although short of teaspoons as always.The main gripe was being told to leave windows closed as the heating calibrated itself, it did not and we were all roasting and had to open windows and doors. The WiFi was disappointing in the sitting room and the router might have been better sited in there rather than the downstairs bedroom.We enjoyed exploring the local area and would all have come back happily once the issues are resolved.

We had a wonderful stay at Glebe house to celebrate my 50th Birthday with age ranges from 10 years to 84. The house was immaculate with so much space. We loved the games room and hot tub. We had a lovely Sunday lunch at the Queen’s Head. It was a shame it was closed Monday and Tuesday ( our stay was sat to wed) as we would have gone again. Would definitely recommend.

It was a fabulous stay in such a beautiful house celebrating my 50th with my family. Located in the outstanding Yorkshire Dales. Glebe Gouse far exceeded expectations it was huge and plenty of space for all members of my family. It had everything available that you need including dishwasher, microwave en-suites. Even books and games. Highly recommended for a large group. It was also set in a fabulous peaceful area but with plenty of activities, day trips out to choose from in the area and lovely walks on the doorstep.

Welcome to Welton House, an exquisite holiday let nestled in the charming village of Orby, just a stone’s throw away from the coastal town of Skegness. As part of our luxury collection, this stunning property offers a truly indulgent and memorable retreat for your getaway. Step inside Welton House and be prepared to be enchanted by its elegant interiors and exceptional amenities. The dining room provides a sophisticated space for communal meals, where you can gather and create lasting memories with your loved ones. The spacious living room, complete with a cosy gas fire and a Smart TV, offers a welcoming atmosphere where you can relax and unwind after a day of exploration.
The well-appointed kitchen provides all the necessary facilities and appliances to cater to your culinary desires. Whip up delicious meals and enjoy them in the dining room or take advantage of the outdoor space for al fresco dining during warmer months. For the ultimate entertainment experience, Welton House features a games room, where you can immerse yourself in having fun with the family. Additionally, a utility room equipped with a tumble dryer and washing machine ensures convenience during your stay. The property boasts a bathroom with a shower over the bath, providing a relaxing space for rejuvenation. In addition, there is a separate shower room with a convenient shower cubicle, offering flexibility for larger groups. Welton House offers six bedrooms, ensuring ample space for all guests. Every room is thoughtfully designed to provide comfort and relaxation, with each featuring a Smart TV for your entertainment. The bed sizes are tailored to accommodate various needs, ensuring a restful night’s sleep for everyone.
Surrounded by natural beauty, Orby and its nearby attractions offer a wealth of activities and experiences. Explore the stunning coastline of Skegness, with its golden sandy beaches and charming promenade. Discover the local wildlife reserves, where you can observe a diverse array of bird species or take scenic walks through picturesque nature trails.
Indulge in fresh seafood at nearby coastal restaurants or explore the charming village shops, offering unique crafts and local produce. Coming soon (2025) is an American Diner, serving up some classic delights for breakfast, lunch and dinner, with an ice cream parlour and village shop all located just behind the property! Welton House is the epitome of elegance and comfort, providing a memorable holiday experience. Whether you’re seeking relaxation, adventure, or a combination of both, this exquisite holiday let is the perfect base for your dream getaway.

reviews.comment: We stayed at Welton House for our annual family weekend away. There were 9 of us and 3 dogs, the house was very accommodating for large parties and the communal spaces allowed us all to be able to spend time together. The house had lots of extra touches which were amazing, the owners have thought of everything you would need to make the trip like home away from home. The house was very clean and smelled lovely, decorated beautifully and everything seemed in really good condition. The location is really private and the outdoor space was perfect for us and the dogs. At times the wifi wasn’t great and could be improved, but didn’t have a negative impact on our weekend. We would definitely return to Welton House in the future and had a great stay! It’s really hard to find accommodation to host larger families with pets but this place really was perfect!

We had a fantastic family holiday at Welton House. Everything you could possibly need was there. Such a great place to relax & have fun.Everyone enjoyed the games room & hot tub.Disappointed that the American diner wasnt up & running as advertised.Sad we are unable to book to return next summer as already booked up.Thank you Welton House

We had a really great time, and really enjoyed the hot tub, games room and surrounding area.There were just two problems- there was a lot of flys in the kitchen-I think they were coming from the drain. The other thing was the dish washer wasn’t cleaning dishes (after 4 washes they still were not clean)- so my brother in law spent a morning cleaning the filter and removing gunk from the arms.

long_description:
Harvel House Fam is an exceptional 8-bedroom holiday home set in the charming village of Meopham, near Gravesend, offering a truly memorable stay in a beautifully restored period property. This striking three-storey house blends historic character with refined, high-end finishes, creating a unique and luxurious retreat for larger groups. Inside, the home is full of personality, with quirky architectural features, generous living spaces, and elegant design throughout. The spacious layout allows guests to come together comfortably while still enjoying privacy across multiple floors. A cosy log burner adds warmth and atmosphere, perfect for relaxing evenings, while the outdoor space is equally impressive, featuring a private hot tub and a well-equipped children’s play park, making it ideal for families. Every detail has been carefully considered to deliver a 5-star experience, whether you’re gathering for a celebration, a family reunion, or a peaceful countryside escape.
The surrounding area of Meopham and Gravesend offers a wonderful mix of countryside charm and accessible attractions. Meopham itself is known for its picturesque scenery, traditional pubs, and relaxed village atmosphere, with plenty of walking routes through rolling Kent countryside right on your doorstep. For those who enjoy the outdoors, nearby Jeskyns Community Woodland provides miles of walking and cycling trails, picnic spots, and play areas for children.
A short drive brings you to Gravesend, a historic riverside town with links to Pocahontas and a vibrant waterfront. Here, you can enjoy riverside walks along the Thames, visit local cafés, or take a boat trip for a different perspective of the area. The nearby Cyclopark is a fantastic destination for families and active groups, offering cycling tracks, skate parks, and adventure play zones.
For day trips, the location is perfectly placed to explore more of Kent. Rochester, with its stunning cathedral and Dickensian heritage, is just a short drive away, while Bluewater Shopping Centre offers an extensive range of shops, restaurants, and entertainment options. If you’re looking for seaside charm, the Kent coast, including Whitstable and Margate, can be reached within an hour, offering beaches, seafood, and independent boutiques.
With its combination of luxurious accommodation, characterful design, and access to both countryside and attractions, Harvel House Fam is perfectly positioned for an unforgettable group getaway.

reviews.comment: Lovely comfortable space for a large family get together. Very accommodating and helpful contact. Would highly recommend.

We booked this property to celebrate our mum’s 80th birthday. We paid a substantial amount for our stay, so we were expecting a high-quality, well-maintained and properly prepared luxury property. Unfortunately, the reality was very different, and we feel the property fell significantly short of both the description and the standard we were entitled to expect for the price we paid.The property is marketed as a “luxury” five-star property, and we therefore expected it to be immaculately clean and fully prepared for our arrival. Instead, it appeared as though it had not been occupied or properly cleaned for some time.There were cobwebs throughout the property, including a particularly thick cobweb immediately above the Aga (food safety issue). There were also cobwebs in the kitchen cupboards, around doorways and in various other areas of the property. This was not an isolated issue or a minor oversight; it was immediately noticeable on arrival and gave the impression that the property had not been properly checked and prepared before we arrived.We appreciate it was an old farm house and we were in the countryside, but the cobwebs were thick and obviously had been there for a long time. The kitchen in particular was unacceptable, some of the cabinets were dirty inside, the floor was dirty, and we found dried, shrivelled food underneath the dining table and discarded food behind the bin. We ended up spending a significant part of the first day of our holiday cleaning the kitchen ourselves.This was particularly disappointing given the reason for our stay. We had travelled to celebrate our mum’s 80th birthday and had paid a substantial amount of money for what was supposed to be a special and relaxing family break. Instead of beginning the celebrations, we were having to clean the property.The cleanliness problems were also present in the bedrooms. A number of the drawers and cupboards were dirty and contained cobwebs, making them unsuitable for storing our clothes and belongings. To be fair, the bedding, towels and bathrooms were clean, which was one of the few positive aspects of the property. However, this does not make up for the general lack of cleanliness elsewhere.We also encountered a potentially serious electrical safety issue during our stay. The faceplate of an electrical socket in one of the bathrooms had come away from the wall and was lying loose. My husband had to refit the faceplate himself. We found this particularly concerning. An electrical socket with a loose or detached faceplate in a bathroom is not something we would expect to encounter in a property marketed as luxury, five-star accommodation. Had there been young children staying with us, we believe this could potentially have presented a serious health and safety hazard. At the very least, it raises concerns about the standard of inspection and maintenance carried out at the property before guests arrive.There was also a practical issue with the kitchen. For a property advertised as being able to accommodate a large group, there was only one large pan to cater adequately for our group of 13! This made preparing meals unnecessarily difficult and was another example of the property not being properly equipped for the number of guests it is intended to accommodate.We contacted the owner while we were staying at the property and made him aware of the problems. He offered to send a cleaner, which we declined, as by that point we had already cleaned the kitchen ourselves because we did not want to lose any more of our limited holiday time. We also did not want a stranger entering the property while our family was staying there, particularly during what was intended to be a private family celebration. We want to be clear that our refusal should not be interpreted as acceptance of the condition of the property or as meaning that the problem was resolved. The fact that a cleaner was offered after we had complained does not change the fact that the property should have been properly cleaned before our arrival.We regularly take staycations throughout the UK and have stayed in a wide range of holiday properties without any problems. In all our experience, this was by far the dirtiest property we have encountered — and, particularly disappointingly, as it was also the most expensive. There is a fundamental difference between a property being described as a luxury cottage and actually delivering a luxury experience. For a stay costing a substantial amount, we believe it is entirely reasonable to expect a property that is clean, properly prepared, safe and adequately equipped. Instead, we arrived at a property with cobwebs, dirty floors, old food debris, dirty cupboards and drawers, inadequate kitchen equipment and an electrical maintenance issue. We reiterate that taken together, these problems gave us the strong impression that the property had not been properly cleaned, inspected or prepared before our arrival.We feel that this represents a substantial discrepancy between the property as advertised and the property that was actually provided.This was supposed to be a very special occasion for our mum’s 80th birthday. Unfortunately, the condition of the property detracted from the start of our celebration and caused us considerable inconvenience, disappointment and frustration. We should not have had to spend part of the first day of a special family holiday cleaning a property that was advertised as luxury accommodation.We therefore do not believe that the price paid was justified by the standard of accommodation provided. To summarise we spent a significant amount of money for the accommodation, the property having been marketed as luxury/five-star accommodation. What we found on arrival was a poor standard of cleanliness (we had to spend time cleaning the property ourselves), electrical maintenance and potential safety issues and inadequate kitchen equipment. Not to mention the disappointment and inconvenience caused during what was intended to be an important family celebration.

We had a great time, and the location is ideal for exploring north Kent while also being quiet and rural. There was plenty of room for our family in the house and for the children to play outside.  The house is well equipped while retaining Iits character. We'd definitely return.

long_description:
Gather with extended family and friends, and celebrate a special occasion in style, where you can relax and unwind in the hot tub with a glass of Prosecco in hand.
Substantial and soaked in original features, this wonderful family home is ideal for social gatherings and any special occasion. Boasting a hot tub and large wrap-around landscaped gardens, this detached property is perfectly positioned to explore Norfolk’s amazing coastline, with its wide sandy beaches and famous Norfolk Broads, a natural haven and habitat for wildlife. Sleeping 14 guests and two well behaved dogs, it is an ideal retreat for all generations, benefiting from a ground floor bedroom suite with en-suite facilities.
There is a well-equipped kitchen with breakfast table, and a formal dining room, the perfect place to host any family celebration. The ground floor bedroom suite also has its own kitchenette, large bedroom with seating, and French doors opening onto the garden. The impressive sweeping staircase leads up to 6 further bedrooms, all beautifully presented.
The house is nestled within the village of Brundall, located along the River Yare. It is the centre for boat building and boat hire, and has its own railway station, post office, mini-market, hairdresser and local eateries. There are two good food serving pubs both within walking distance, one located at the riverside and the other within the village itself with a large garden.
Leave the car behind and walk down the hill to the train station, less than a half mile walk. Here you can jump on the train and visit the city of Norwich, or the traditional seaside towns of Great Yarmouth and Lowestoft. Norwich is only 8 miles away where guests can visit the cathedral, castle museum, theatre, excellent shopping and art galleries. Wroxham, only 7½ miles away, is known as the Capital of the Norfolk Broads, and has waterside shops, cafés, and daily boat hire with river trips available to explore the expanse of waterways. There is an RSPB reserve at Strumpshaw Fen, 1 mile.
Norfolk’s finest sandy beaches are within 14 miles and include Winterton-on-Sea, Waxham, Horsey and Sea Palling. For fun-filled family days out there is Thrigby Hall Wildlife Gardens with a renowned collection of Asian mammals including birds. Here you will also find reptiles in the pleasantly landscaped gardens. Close by, the village of Strumpsham has a steam museum, and Reedham offers Pettitt’s Animal Adventure Park. Beach 14 miles. Shop, pub and restaurant ½ mile.

long_description:
Gather with extended family and friends and celebrate a special occasion in style, where you can relax in the two hot tubs. A perfect choice for friends and family wanting to holiday together, but retain full privacy.
Tower Hill Grange’s living space is extremely spacious and boasts a 65” Smart TV with enough seating for your whole party, the kitchen is well-equipped and provides you with everything you will need to cater for a larger party. A light dining room is in the very heart of the house, with probably one of the largest dining tables you have ever seen, fantastic for a gathering of family and friends. In addition, you have two games rooms complete with a pool table, full size snooker table, darts board and large Smart TVs in both, a great place to socialise. The property also boasts a built-in sound system throughout the ground floor. The bedrooms are spread over the first floor and all boast en-suite facilities. There is a private enclosed garden to the front, a sun trap with seating furniture, perfect for al fresco eating and relaxation with a large, decked area to the side where the hot tubs are placed with outdoor speakers. The large, landscaped garden is perfect for younger children wanting to run around or play football. A wonderful holiday home ideal for social gatherings and any special occasion.
With the property set just outside the fantastic seaside town of Hornsea, you have instant access to a plethora of shops, pubs, restaurants, and cafés as well as the traditional amusement arcades. The promenade is popular with visitors and locals alike who enjoy a stroll while taking in the sea air. A visit to this area would not be complete without taking in Hornsea Mere, one of Yorkshires largest lakes, where you can enjoy various water sport activities, the bird watching is great too! A little further afield are the stately homes of Burton Agnes and Sledmere House as well as the RSPB reserve at Bempton Cliff. This wonderful Hornsea house is perfect for your family holiday on the East Coast of Yorkshire. Beach 3 miles.
These properties can be booked together to accommodate up to 27 guests.

long_description:
This historic, Grade II listed farmhouse, which is part of the Hawnby Estate, still retains many original features, giving this property real character. Built in the late 18th century, this detached property is steeped in history, which you will feel as you explore the spacious rooms possessing far reaching views over scenery which has changed very little over the centuries. Nature stretches out before you, with ancient woodland, fields, the meandering River Rye and heather moorland beyond. A haven for those who enjoy the great outdoors.
On arrival visitors are welcomed by a sweeping gravel driveway through the large enclosed garden and courtyard. There is a front and a back entrance for the property, one leading from the courtyard, the other from the front lawned garden. The property benefits from the security of automatic electric wooden gates. From the courtyard, enter into a stone flagged hall which leads through the property with the ground floor rooms branching off. The living room boasts a large Smart TV as well as the focal point - the crackling wood burner and club fender. Together you can all enjoy some evening entertainment on the large comfy sofas and armchairs. Perfect for unwinding after a long day of exploring the moors or coast. From the central hall you will also find the formal dining room, which is a great place for celebrating special occasions and enjoying home cooked evening meals in style. What could be more enjoyable than laughing and reminiscing while sharing a hearty meal with your family and friends?
They say the kitchen is the heart of the home, and what an incredible kitchen this is! This room oozes character and certainly has the WOW factor! With a beamed ceiling still retaining original meat hooks, handmade worktops and cupboards, five oven Aga, central island with electric oven and hob, American-style fridge/freezer as well as a large dining table, this social area will soon become the heart of your holiday experience.
Beyond the living room is the snug area with piano for those with musical inclinations. Separate from the main living room this is perfect for any members of the group to have some time to themselves, perhaps curling up on one of the cosy chairs to devour a good book. Younger family members may enjoy using this area to play board games together in an evening or enjoying a movie on the Smart TV. It has wonderful views over the outdoor dining and BBQ area. Also downstairs there is a separate toilet and spacious utility room, ideal for storing walking boots and coats.
Upstairs there are six generous bedrooms, each with its own character. All of the bedrooms are beautifully decorated and furnished, with deep pocket sprung mattresses and luxurious bed linen. You can guarantee that you will have a deep night’s sleep, waking refreshed and ready to explore the scenic Yorkshire Moors. There are three kingsize beds, one with en-suite facilities, and three with twin beds. Outside, relax in your very own hot tub in the privacy of an established orchard, as you are surrounded only by nature. Village pub and shop within 1 mile, with alternative pubs and restaurant within 5 miles.

long_description: This impressive Georgian country house offers extensive holiday accommodation and stands in it’s own gated grounds in the attractive, ancient market town of Appleby in Westmorland. The property has been totally refurbished to a very high standard retaining many of the original features, including an elegant staircase. The grounds are mainly laid to lawn with an outdoor eating/BBQ area and hot tub. Just a five minute walk takes you down to the town centre. Appleby is built in the curve of the River Eden and is a traditional medieval town with the castle at the top of the hill sloping gently downhill to the church. This is one of the prettiest market towns in England and despite once being the county town of Westmorland it retains a village atmosphere with a great deal of interest and charm. Situated in the beautiful Eden Valley the location is superb for exploring the highlights of the North of England as it separates the Lakes District fells from the Pennines and also gives easy access to the Yorkshire and Durham Dales.The scenic Carlisle to Settle railway route runs through Appleby and makes a great day out. Further afield, the Northumberland National Park along with Hadrian’s Wall and the Scottish Border are within an hours drive. Superb walking, cycling, golf and fishing are all available near by. A good selection of shops and pubs 500 yards. Ullswater is only a 20 minute drive away.

long_description:
Situated on a working farm in a beautiful rural environment, Dairy House Farm is a wonderfully unique Grade II listed 17th-century farmhouse, perfect for group gatherings and special occasions. Set out over three floors, each of the six good-sized bedrooms benefit from their own bathrooms, some with beautiful claw foot roll-top baths. Two of the bedrooms have superb four poster beds, and on the second floor two bedrooms share an interlinking door as well as their own private entrance. The property boasts many original and restored features throughout such as beams and exposed stone, and outside there’s ample private parking and a garden complete with private hot tub which offers the most spectacular far reaching countryside views.
Centrally located near to Rudyard Lake in rural Staffordshire Moorlands, just a few miles from the Peak District National Park, you’ll find many local walks and cycle routes. Rudyard Lake itself offers boating and fishing, and is also home to a café, bar and restaurant. The charming market town of Leek, with its cobbled market place, can be reached in around 10 minutes and provides ample shops, pubs and restaurants. The surrounding area holds many attractions within easy reach such as Britain’s premier theme park Alton Towers, World of Wedgewood or the Emma Bridgewater Factory, all around a 30-minute drive. Peak Wildlife Park is around 20 minutes or Trentham Gardens and Monkey Forest around 45 minutes. Shop 4 miles, pub and restaurant 2 miles.
Please note: There are open, steep, spiral or narrow stairs at the property.

long_description:
This beautiful, traditional stone-built farmhouse, dating back to the 18th century, stands in its own grounds boasting mature gardens and a stone-walled summerhouse. The building is spread over 5000 sq feet with a unique layout built in stages over the 300 years. The combination of oak floors, wooden beams, panelled walls and a particularly beautiful dining room with a French marble fireplace and log fire gives the building an abundance of character and charm. It makes the perfect location for weekend celebrations or getaways for the whole family revelling in its size and warmth and activities including local river walks and cycle tracks surrounding the farm, golf, fishing, horse riding or simply exploring. Furthermore, one of the stables has been converted into a small but well-stocked gym.
Etherley Dene Farm is located in Bishop Auckland, the official residence of the bishops of Durham since the 12th century. The town provides many interesting attractions, including Auckland Castle with its splendid marble and limestone chapel and stained-glass windows that relate to stories of early Christian saints. Durham with its cathedral is just 12 miles and there is seasonal access to the steam railway and the glorious Durham Dales from the local station; rail enthusiasts can also visit Shildon ‘The cradle of the railways’ and its railway museum, 2 miles. The Dales and Hamsterley Forest are a short drive with cycling and walking routes (cycle hire by arrangement). In winter there may even be the chance to ski or board on fresh snow in Weardale only 25 minutes away. Quaint Barnard Castle with its impressive French-style chateau housing the Bowes Musuem is 12 miles and Beamish open-air Victorian museum is 30 minutes’ drive. Newcastle, with St. James’ Park, The Metro Arena, The Playhouse and The Sage, is within easy reach and Gateshead’s Metrocentre is less than 3 miles. Visit the spectacular World Heritage Site of Hadrian’s Wall, the majestic Northumbrian coast which stretches for miles passing Alnwick Castle, Craster, Alnmouth, Seahouses, Bamburgh Castle and on to Holy Island (Lindisfarne). Supermarket home deliveries can be arranged but most supermarkets are within 1 mile. A garage shop is within ¼ mile. A family orientated pub serving meals is within ½ mile and a more traditional ‘drinking’ pub with TV sport is less than 100 yards.

long_description:
This 600 square foot Beach House at Whinthwaite is a fabulous seafront property with a hot tub in the coastal town of Seascale. Perfect for a family reunion, special celebration, or a large group holiday. With panoramic sea views, a train station nearby, easy access to the Lake District and the West Cumbrian Coast, you’ve got a perfect base for a memorable holiday with loved ones. It’s also perfect for walking or cycling groups. This stunning property sleeping up to eighteen guests features nine double bedrooms, a total of seven bathrooms, three kitchens, two living rooms, beautiful gardens, and some stunning original features. All the bedrooms are well furnished with comfortable beds, plenty of storage and hanging space, many come with sea views, seating, and vanity areas. Three bedrooms are on the ground floor, four on the first floor and two on the second floor. There’s a mixture of en-suite rooms and some floors have separate bathrooms. On the first floor you’ll find a comfortable games room with a pool table which converts into an air hockey table, along with table tennis which doubles over as a dining table! You’ll love the stunning dining room/conservatory with sea and garden views, but if you want the best views, head to the top of this stunning property, the sea views are amazing. The spacious, main living room on the ground floor is an excellent place to all get-together in front of the large open fire, it’s the dream on Christmas day to opening presents together and it’s a great social space to see the wine flowing while you catch up with your loved ones. There’s a kitchen on each floor, so you haven’t got to go far for a midnight snack or a cuppa and a utility room on the ground floor. At the rear you have an enclosed patio with outdoor furniture and private hot tub, perfect for soaking up the sun and enjoying a glass of wine or a cold beer after a day of adventure, along with large lawned gardens with amazing sea views.
The Beach House at Whinthwaite is on the Cumbrian coast near Gosforth in the West Lakes, this delightful village near to the Eskdale and Wasdale valleys offers an excellent shop and several pubs. From here you have easy access to some of most picturesque and dramatic scenery this Cumbrian hotspot has to offer. The highest mountain in England, Scafell Pike is a short drive through the countryside with beautiful lakes and walking routes nearby, while Drigg beach and Sand Dunes is about a mile away. You have an excellent links golf course at Seascale just walking distance from The Beach House at Whinthwaite. Muncaster Castle is a 10-minute drive where you can tour the haunted castle, take in the birds of prey show and enjoy the stunning gardens. La’al Ratty, a narrow-gauge steam railway from Dalegarth to Boot. You can also enjoy kayaking, paddle boarding and gyhll scrambling. Whether you’re looking for scenery, adventure or climbing, Whinthwaite is a great starting point. Beach 200 yards.

long_description:
The Parade in Bridlington is a spacious celebration home designed to host up to fifteen guests in style.
This impressive property features seven bedrooms, many with en-suite shower rooms, and each is equipped with a Smart TV. The open-plan ground floor includes a large living area, a cosy wood-burning stove, and a contemporary kitchen with a breakfast bar and an expansive dining table, perfect for large gatherings. An original bar adds a unique touch, while patio doors open onto an enclosed courtyard with a hot tub. A mere 100 yards from the beach, The Parade places guests right in the heart of Bridlington’s vibrant town centre. Bridlington offers endless entertainment and activities for all ages, ensuring a memorable stay year-round. Its sandy beaches stretch for miles, lined by a Victorian promenade, lively amusement arcades, and popular restaurants. Bridlington Spa, the town’s renowned venue, hosts live events and performances, while the indoor leisure centre with a swimming pool provides additional family fun. Nature lovers can explore the Bridlington Animal Park, go on boat rides, or visit the nearby RSPB Bempton Cliffs to witness incredible seabird colonies along the stunning Flamborough Heritage Coastline.
History and culture enthusiasts will enjoy nearby Burton Agnes Hall, Sledmere House, and the charming Old Town. From seaside strolls to historic attractions, Bridlington has something for everyone, making The Parade an ideal base for a fun-filled group getaway, perfect for guests who want to escape the hustle and bustle of working life by popping their feet up, or go out and take advantage of all the hidden gems this property and the area has to offer.

Inside this large, yet wonderfully laid out home, you have a beautiful entrance way with feature staircase and chandelier, a huge lounge with superb fireplace and woodburning stove, Smart TV and French doors leading to the garden. A second lounge/snug has a Smart TV and is a great space for the kids to have their own fun. The spacious Kitchen has a large Aga for cooking, electric hob, dishwasher and fridge as well as a breakfast area. Off the kitchen is the grand dining room with plenty of seating for everyone. From the kitchen you also have access to the utility room with large fridge/freezer and washing machine. On the ground floor is the downstairs suite complete with double bedroom, lounge and en-suite shower room, the perfect spot for the less mobile or for those who like a bit of their own space. Upstairs, you will find five more bedrooms. The rear facing bedrooms have wonderful views of Glastonbury Tor as does the principal bathroom, which features a spacious walk-in shower and fabulous bath, where you can relax and gaze out over the fields beyond.
Outside, you have a beautiful large garden, part of which is an orchard and a superb place to sit and relax under the shade of the apple trees on a hot day. The patio area has seating and a BBQ area, and there is also a fabulous lawn area for games. The crowning glory of course is the magnificent hot tub, perfectly situated to take in the views of the fields, the garden and the house while you sit back and relax with a glass of your favourite drink.
Crickledown is set in the village of High Ham, just 3 miles from Langport. The Somerset levels are easily accessible as are many of Somersets other attractions. The towns of Taunton, Yeovil and Glastonbury are reached in under 30 minutes by car, with the latter being of note for its ancient historical links and of course the Tor which can be seen from Crickledowns windows. National Trust properties abound nearby and a fun day out for the family can be had on the West Somerset Steam Railway which runs from Bishops Lydeard to the seaside town of Minehead. Pub within a mile.

long_description:
Nestled on the Welsh borders in hundreds of acres of rolling countryside, this superb holiday cottage complete with hot tub combines bright contemporary style with rural charm. The Woodlands Farmhouse is surrounded by the most beautiful countryside for as far as the eye can see and being set on a working farm, offers a unique insight into everyday rural life.
Spaciously set out over one level, means the property is perfect for generations of family and those special group occasions, with each of the six individually designed bedrooms boasting en-suite facilities. Outside in the enclosed gardens, those with children and four legged friends can truly relax and take in the peaceful and tranquil surroundings.
At night you can also discover a world of wildlife in the darkness, with visitors ranging from foxes and badgers, to owls and bats. The lanes around the property are perfect for gentle strolls and bike rides with circular routes ranging from 3 to 5 miles and beyond. For those wanting to explore the surrounding area, the location is perfect for discovering the hidden beauty of Shropshire, Cheshire and the Welsh borders. The farmhouse itself lies just on the Welsh side of the border, however the brook on the adjoining farm takes you into Cheshire, and the county of Shropshire is just a few miles away.
For lovers of the great outdoors the Clywdian Range, Offa’s Dyke, Ceiriog Valley and the Coed Llandegla Forest are all accessible within an hour. An abundance of towns, villages and attractions are also readily available, to name but a few: Ellesmere (25mins), Hawkstone Park Follies & Beeston Castle (30mins), Llangollen, Chester & Chester Zoo (40mins) and Shrewsbury (55mins). There really is something for everyone.

reviews.comment: We had a lovely family holiday. The farmhouse was spotlessly clean, very well equipped and comfortable with plenty of seating for everyone inside and out. We enjoyed walks from the doorstep and we also visited Whitchurch, Chester Zoo, The Blue Planet Aquarium, Llangollen for ice cream and a hike up the hill to the castle ruins, the Pontcysyllte Aqueduct and some of the family enjoyed forest Segway. I would also recommend The Horse & Jockey Pub for excellent service and good quality food, catering for allergies, vegans and they accept dogs.

We had a fantastic stay at this beautiful farmhouse, celebrating a group of old school friends coming together for their 40th birthdays.Tina was absolutely fantastic and went above and beyond to make our stay extra special. I was able to send decorations a few days before we arrived, and she kindly put everything up for us, even added her own little treats to help make our celebrations even more special.She kept in touch throughout our stay to make sure we had everything we needed, but despite living next door, we barely saw her, which gave us such a lovely sense of privacy and trust. She was like a little fairy who magically appeared to empty the recycling, top up the hot tub and keep everything running smoothly!The farmhouse is in a beautiful countryside setting, with lovely walks right on the doorstep. Everything we needed was provided, and having an ensuite in every bedroom was a huge bonus.The hot tub was definitely a favourite and got plenty of use throughout our stay! We had an absolutely brilliant time and couldn't have asked for a better place to celebrate. Highly recommended.

Excellent accommodation. Tina and Ian were very hospitable with great comms, friendly greeting and helpful information. Having all en-suite Bedrooms was great and worked really well for us. A well stocked games cupboard, well stocked kitchen utensils and a hot tub meant we had everything we needed for a family vacation of 12 of us. Plenty to do in the local area - parks, pubs (you need a car).Highly recommended for any group looking for a relaxing, quiet and private break.

Underfloor central heating (on ground floor), electricity, bed linen, towels and Wi-Fi included. Initial logs for wood burner included. Travel cot and highchair available on request. Welcome pack. Shared laundry facilities on-site. Courtyard with garden furniture and barbecue. Landscaped grounds with sitting-out area and garden furniture (shared with other properties on-site). Private parking. Located in Lincolnshire Wolds (AONB)
Private coarse fishing lake

These delightful barn conversions (refs 25589, 26477, 26718, 26724, 26726 and 29579) maintain many original features and are set in the heart of The Lincolnshire Wolds, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. The properties (except 29579) have all received a Green Tourism Business Scheme Gold Award. Within the grounds of the farm, these holiday properties offer coarse fishing on the farm lake, as well as many excellent walks and fantastic views across the countryside.
On the edge of the village of North Willingham, the barns provide an excellent base for exploring. Just 3½ miles from Market Rasen with its world famous racecourse, excellent range of restaurants, pubs, shops and market. Horncastle is renowned for its antique shops and is only a short drive, as is the unspoilt Georgian town of Louth with two busy market days a week. A visit to the sandy beaches at Mablethorpe or Skegness are always worth a day out, as is a visit to Lincoln Cathedral and the Bailgate area used in the filming of the ‘Da Vinci Code’. Shops, pub and restaurant 4 miles.

reviews.comment: We have just got home from a wonderful stay at Wagonner's Barn for my husband's 60th birthday celebrations with 14 other family members. We had the best time, the accommodation is supplied with absolutely everything you need to make the stay enjoyable and comfortable. The layout of the bedrooms suited us perfectly, impeccably clean throughout and lovely friendly hosts. A perfect stay and we will definitely be back again. Our guests particularly liked the hot tub and the games room.

It has been a wonderful week staying at the Waggoners barn.We were celebrating a family Golden anniversary, so age ranges were from 74 - 5. There was plenty of room for everyone. Family enjoyed using the games room, hot tub and outside areas to relax. It was a great base to explore the local areas.Lovely touch of fresh cake, tea & coffee on arrival.

We stayed as a party of thirteen with no children and we have had a wonderful time! We were greeted on arrival, the house had just been cleaned and was in excellent condition, with a bonus little tray of chocolates on the dining table. Cleaners are in every day to use the laundry facility, but they were all polite and called good morning to us whilst we had breakfast outdoors. In addition, the hot tub is serviced daily by a very pleasant gentleman, which keeps it clean and fresh.We were in a heatwave whilst we were staying, but the barn remained cool. By propping the doors open all the way from the stables double bedroom to the main room, you can get quite a significant breeze through, which keeps things fresh. Unfortunately, you can't do a huge amount about upstairs as, with an open stairway, it gets quite warm up there. Same with the games room; it gets the sun most of the day, which turns it into a bit of a greenhouse. This is only an issue in the height of summer of course.The kitchens are well furnished with appliances, utensils, and even a proper carton of milk on arrival (rather than little pots of UHT milk) with tea and coffee.The bedrooms aren't enormous, but they function perfectly for the house, as the main facility is the large communal spaces. We loved the multiple options to seat our large group for meals etc.The surrounding area is gorgeous. We only had to walk a short ways up into a field to have a beautiful view of the solar eclipse. There are also plenty of routes to take a hike into the Wolds, including to the nearby ice cream parlour, which is also fabulous.Overall, we had a wonderful stay and would recommend it to other large groups.

long_description:
Paradise is in the town of Cinderford in the Forest of Dean and is ideal for larger families or friends wanting to explore the area. Only 23 miles from Cheltenham Racecourse, it’s perfect for large groups to stay. The property comprises a large living room, a large dining room with a table that seats 16 guests, a kitchen with an island and a Ninja Foodi 9.5L Dual-Zone Air Fryer has also been added to the kitchen to make cooking faster, meaning you can have dinner on the table quicker and enjoy more quality time with family and friends. There are also patio doors leading to the rear decked area with a private hot tub and cycle storage. There are three double bedrooms on the ground floor, one with a super king-size bed, one with a double bed and one with two ¾ double beds, all of which have en-suite facilities. To the first floor are a further three bedrooms, one with four poster super king-size bed, one with four poster double bed and one with twin beds, all with en-suite facilities.
There is an outbuilding to the rear of the property where you will find the washing machine, a tumble dryer and enough room for the safe storage of bikes, there is a collection of ride-on toys for young visitors to use.
This excellent position allows guests to venture out and explore Gloucestershire, Monmouthshire and Worcestershire. For those looking for an adventure, Paradise has easy access to the Forest Adventure Outdoor Centre, Puzzlewood, Clearwell Caves and the Soldiers of Gloucestershire Museum. Alternatively, visit the English Heritage’s Goodrich Castle, National Trust Round House and Naval Temple, and Norchard Railway Station Museum on the Dean Forest Railway. Monmouth, with its castle, wide high street and a good range of shops, and Chepstow Castle and racecourse, are well worth a visit. There are also walks, golf and mountain biking opportunities available nearby. Shop, pub and restaurant ¼ mile.

reviews.comment: Front downstairs bedroom needed a wardrobe and the ensuite was small with a minute washbasin. The remaining bedrooms all had spacious ensuites. Access to the wardrobe in the upstairs twin bedroom was difficult, being so close to one of the beds. It was not possible to hang coats in the hall cupboard as it was full of various items of equipment. We felt that the lighting in the kitchen was inadequate for cooking and also lacked suitable lights above the kitchen island. The low level leather sofas would not suit all generations. It would have been helpful if all of the keys were labelled. Up to date information about local eateries would be helpful.The welcome gift was a nice touch.

We had a most comfortable stay at Paradise for my husband's 75th birthday celebrations.  The parking out front was enough for us to get 4 cars parked facing the house without overhanging the road, which was fine.  There are 3 downstairs bedrooms all with en-suite bathrooms which were great for those with babies and younger children. Plus a further 3 huge luxury  bedrooms upstairs, all with large en-suites and two with four poster beds and lovely old fashioned quirky furniture.  The weather was great until the day before we left, and after a day out in the Forest of Dean, the hot tub was a great way to wind down.  It was pleasant sitting out the front watching the sun go down and there was plenty of room for 9 adults and 3 children.  Weston Super Mare is great for a beach day out, also the Cotswolds Country Park & Beach was a fun day out.  We cooked breakfast most mornings and there is plenty of seating for everyone at a huge dining table or perched on a stool at the kitchen island. Kitchen facilities are very good, plenty of equipment, even a modern airfryer.  Huge larder fridge, but only a 3 drawer freezer so initially, dont buy too much frozen stuff as space is limited !  Everyone enjoyed their stay at Paradise, the owner lives next door, but never bothered us and allowed us to just get on and have a great family time.

We had a great time staying at Paradise.  Plenty of room for the 11 of us. Everything you needed to ensure a good holiday.  Extremely friendly owners.  We all were very sad to leave. Would recommend to anyone looking for a place to stay in the area

The entrance hallway features a cocktail arcade machine, and the ground floor offers contemporary living with a large living room and a spacious, well-equipped kitchen/dining room leading to a games room which overlooks the garden. There are also two bedrooms on the ground floor, one with an en-suite shower room. There is also an additional downstairs toilet. There are a further four bedrooms on the first floor, all of which have a Smart TV. The master bedroom also has its own dressing room and en-suite bathroom. Enjoy a BBQ in the large, enclosed garden, complete with a private hot tub and cycle store. There is an electric vehicle charging point available free of charge.
Thanks to its proximity to the road network and with so much to see and do within easy driving distance, this property makes the ideal touring base. It is conveniently located close to the Fylde Coast and just 5 miles from the popular seaside resort of Blackpool. Poulton-le-Fylde is just 1½ miles away which has a good selection of shops, bars and restaurants. There are also lots of family friendly pubs in the area as well as play centres for the children. Activities available locally include golf, fishing and horse riding, as well as plenty of opportunities for walking and cycling.
Blackpool, whose many attractions include the famous Blackpool Tower, Pleasure Beach, Sea Life Centre, Madame Tussauds, Blackpool Zoo and Sandcastle Water Park, is just 5 miles away. For a more laid-back seaside experience, Cleveleys, 5 miles, has an award-winning seafront, and the cosmopolitan town of Lytham St Annes, 13 miles, is famous for its 5 championship golf courses and annual Proms. Other places within easy driving distance include Preston, 15 miles, and Lancaster, 20 miles. Lancashire’s beautiful Ribble Valley, the Lake District, Yorkshire Dales National Park and the Forest of Bowland, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, are all within an hour’s drive. For those who prefer to leave their car behind, there is a good public transport network in the area with buses from the main road into Blackpool. Alternatively, trains run from Poulton-le-Fylde to Blackpool, Manchester and Preston. Beach 5 miles. Shop 50 yards, pub 1 mile and restaurant 1½ mile.

long_description:
Nestled within the quiet village of Gimingham, but under 2 miles from the coast, Hall Farm Barns have been thoughtfully furnished and equipped to ensure guests have everything they need for a great stay. Light and airy throughout, these semi-detached barns can be booked individually or as a group for those wishing to accommodate large numbers while still retaining some privacy. The largest of the barns, The Great South Barn (UKC2527), sleeps twelve and benefits from four bathrooms, three of which are en-suite. Just as impressive, The Great North Barn (ref UKC2526), sleeps ten and has a glass ceiling area that is just perfect for gazing at blue skies and stars alike. The smaller, but perfectly formed Courtyard Barn (ref UKC2525), sleeps six and offers integrated ceiling speakers and retains an air of spaciousness, making it a great place in which to relax and unwind.
Close by lies the seaside village of Mundesley which offers a lovely sandy beach, a firm favourite with the locals but something of an undiscovered gem compared to its larger neighbour Cromer. Do make time to visit Cromer though, as here you will find a celebrated Edwardian seafront, a long promenade to stroll along and a famous pier, which often offers end of pier shows. Both seaside resorts also offer lots of places where you can eat and drink, and Cromer also has a cinema and Amazonia Zoo.
Close by also lies the gateway to the Norfolk Broads, Wroxham, which offers lots of attractions, including the opportunity to hire a day boat or join a charter as it glides through these famous waterways. There is so much to do in the area that whichever barn you choose, you will book to come again, just to fit everything in. Beach 2 miles. Shop, pub and restaurant 1 mile.
These properties can be booked together to accommodate up to 26 guests.

reviews.comment: The view from the property is incredible, you are so close to the sea that you can lay in bed and listen to the waves. So relaxing. The house has everything you need and was very clean when we arrived. I know that the house has been sold and there is going to be updates made at the property. The beds are very small and the mattresses definitely need updating, but having said that it didn’t impinge too much on our wonderful family holiday. Thank you.

We seem to have been unfortunate to have our holiday the week the receivers completed the sale to new owners. The internet was lost on the Sunday morning (probably because the bill had not been paid) and, despite daily contact with the manager and a conversation with the receivers, the internet was never restored. With the poor local mobile phone signal that required being outside the apartment in order to connect, this was a major issue. Hopefully, the new owners will have the internet reconnected and address the long list of other issues to avoid yet more negative feedback. I suggest the new owners stay in the apartment for a while and try to cook and serve a meal for 12 people and experience the inadequate kitchen and multiple other problems. The kitchen is badly under-equipped. Two separate extendable tables without their leaves made eating as a family very difficult. One bedroom was shared with the sauna, projection system, and hot water heater and was unsuitable as a private bedroom.Despite the problems, the apartment has many positive features including the view, the ten-minute walk to the beach and railway station, and the hot tub. You’ll get a lot of exercise climbing up and down the internal staircases and outside steps.

The property listing and photos need to be updated — they do not accurately reflect the current condition of the property.Unfortunately, the condition of the property did not match the expectations created by the listing, particularly given the price paid.The first issue we noticed was the main bathroom. There was an awful smell throughout our entire stay. No cleaning products were provided for the toilet, so I actually purchased toilet cleaner myself. I then noticed faeces on the toilet brush holder, which was extremely unpleasant.The shower drain is blocked and fills up very quickly when the shower is being used.I also found cobwebs and spiders in several rooms, which gave the impression that the property had not been thoroughly cleaned or maintained.The hot tub room was also a concern from a safety and comfort perspective. There was a tiled table in the corner which appeared to have been cut to fit into the space. The photos show three outdoor wooden loungers, but there was only one when we arrived. This meant that only one adult could sit comfortably with the children while they were using the hot tub.The outdoor area is extremely overgrown, with weeds everywhere. The wooden balcony is very run down, and the windows had a considerable amount of bird faeces on them.Overall, it appears that the property has not been updated since the photos and description were originally added. The listing refers to a refurbishment in 2020, the property doesn’t appear to have been updated since then. One suggestion would be to install non-slip mats or suitable non-slip flooring on the stairs leading from the hot tub area to the bedroom containing the sauna, as these could become very slippery and present a safety risk.There was also a strange layout in one of the rooms, with the sauna, bed and projector all located in the same room. This was not what we expected from the listing.The kitchen tap is a significant health and safety concern. The water comes out extremely hot and there is currently no warning sticker. A clear “VERY HOT WATER” warning should be added immediately. Thankfully, we did not allow any of the children to use the tap, as they could easily have been scalded.The main living area has window seating with very uncomfortable cushions, and the pool table is extremely old and tired.We visited during peak summer, yet the beds had very thick duvets with no alternative lighter bedding available. The listing photos show thinner blankets on some of the beds in the loft room, so we expected these to be available.There are, however, some positives. The location is excellent, being around five minutes from the beach, and Tesco is only a few minutes’ drive away.The train station being very close and a lovely walk into St Ives. One thing future guests should be made aware of is that the bar on the beach hosts wedding events. There were two weddings taking place during our stay, and if you are sleeping in the loft room, the music was very loud and continued until around midnight. This is particularly important for families or anyone expecting a quiet night’s sleep.Overall, the price paid for this booking does not reflect the current condition of the property. The listing needs to be updated so that the photos, description and claims about the property’s condition accurately represent what guests will actually find on arrival.Sadly, based on our experience, I would not recommend this property and would not book it again.

long_description:
Mole Hall is a beautiful, detached, thatched 18th-century barn conversion, in the heart of the Devon countryside. The property takes advantage of far reaching rural views from many rooms and is only a 20-minute drive from the thriving market town of Bideford.
Internally, the property is cosy with traditional features whilst having a modern touch. The open plan kitchen/dining area has access to the garden through French doors that fill the room with light. The living room is on the first floor offering exposed beam ceilings and a seating area with a desk to relax and unwind. Externally, the property has a lawned garden and patio with garden furniture, perfect for enjoying the afternoon sun. There is a lake on-site which is stocked with carp perfect for any keen fishermen.
North Devon holds many interesting attractions for all ages. RHS Rosemoor is approximately a 10-minute drive away from the property, and is an internationally renowned collection of gardens. The Tarka Trail is also nearby which features a series of footpaths and cycle paths that go around north Devon following the route taken by Tarka the Otter in the book of that name. The Milky Way Adventure Park is also only a half hour drive from the property and is a great family day out. Home of north Devon’s biggest indoor adventure play area with assault courses and slides built for adults and children along with shows and displays to enjoy too.
Only an hours drive away is Exmoor National Park offering an amazing variety of landscapes within its 267 square miles. A unique landscape of moorland, woodland, valleys and farmland; shaped by people and nature over thousands of years. Where high cliffs plunge into the Bristol Channel, and cosy pubs and tearooms offer delicious local produce.

long_description:
The Cottage has commanding, stunning views across the English Channel. This attractive, spacious, family home for all seasons is the ideal property for a relaxing holiday with both friends or relatives.
The property has plenty of space for the entire family to spread out and enjoy, including a stunning living room with wooden flooring and large windows letting in plenty of light. Relax after a brisk winter walk in front of a glowing log burner in the cosy living room, overlooking the frothing waves. The kitchen is well-equipped with everything you need to whip of fantastic feasts including and Rangemaster gas cooker with 5 hobs and 2 ovens, a raclette and sandwich toaster, enjoy your meals seated in the kitchen, or alternately in the formal dining room. Stunning French doors open out from each end of the kitchen, one leading to a seaside balcony and herb garden with the other end opening onto the garden patio and outside seating area. A decked terrace runs the length of the property, an ideal spot for soaking up the sun or four of the six bedrooms have sea views and the other two have attractive garden views.
There is a private hot tub at The Cottage, and the property offers two games rooms, one in the house with children’s toys, a library, games and two table football tables. There is a large, second games room in the garage next to the house which offers several activities including: table tennis, pool table, darts, bows and arrows, basketball (outside the garage). These games rooms also feature a kitchenette with a fridge, and seating area with a large sofa, ideal for all ages. Please note this games room is not heated.
The white chalk cliff above St Margaret’s Bay is said to be the first place the sun reaches each morning on mainland Britain! The beach is famous for being the closest point to France and is the spot where Channel swimmers begin their marathon 21 mile swim.
The village itself offers good pubs, restaurants and local shop within walking distance. The coastal path leads to the famous White Cliffs of Dover, gateway to England and now one of the UK’s protected Heritage coasts offering some of the best cliff coastal walking in the country. The lighthouse is the place where Marconi transmitted his first radio broadcast to France. Closer to France than London, bring a passport, catch a ferry from Dover and visit the French markets in Calais and Boulogne for the day.
Visit Dover, Deal and Walmer Castle, Pines Garden and Metropole Galleries Folkestone. Canterbury 17 miles. Golf, sailing, cycling, horse riding locally. Shops and pubs 500 yards.
Please note: There are open, steep, spiral or narrow stairs at the property.

reviews.comment: We were a group of 9 adults staying and we had a fantastic weekend.  The Cottage is charming with lots of rooms and different garden areas on different levels.  It is very spacious and has everything you could need.  The bedrooms are big with very comfortable beds and plenty of storage areas and 4 of the bedrooms have sea views - as do the living areas and kitchen.  There is also a beautiful balcony (with hot tub) overlooking the sea. The location is very peaceful - yet is only a short walk to the beach, local shop, pubs, tearoom etc. and there was no issue having food delivered.  It is only 10 - 15 minute drive to Deal or Dover.   We also enjoyed the games room in the garage (although it is fair to say the pool table won't suit a serious player!)  The communication from the host was excellent both before and during our stay and we felt welcome in their family home.

10 of our family had a lovely stay at the cottage to celebrate 80th birthdays. The accommodation was just right for us. We were lucky to have beautiful weather and it was a joy to sit on the decking and take in the wonderful views across the English Channel with France so clear on the horizon. The only disadvantage is the Cottage is built on a very steep hill, but if you are able to cope with lot of steps then it is worth it for the stunning views.

Had an amazing week loved the cottage and incredible views and walks. Kitchen could do with updating had everything we needed just odd layout. Found dishwasher hard to use as unable to see program dial. Beds really comfortable, bathrooms excellent and enjoyed the hot tub. Would love to go back!

long_description:
Welcome to the luxurious Jorvik Villas in York, an exceptional celebration home that combines stunning interior design with original charm. This exquisite property features six individually styled and named bedrooms, each with its own unique character, and six bathrooms spread across three floors. Complete with a private sauna and a large hot tub in a secluded courtyard, Jorvik Villas is the ultimate retreat for relaxation and luxury.
The ground floor boasts a kingsize bedroom with an en-suite shower room, a Smart TV, and an original feature fireplace, creating a cosy and elegant ambiance. The spacious living room offers plenty of seating and a Smart TV, perfect for unwinding after a day of exploring York. Two steps down lead into the Shaker-style kitchen, equipped with a gas range cooker, dishwasher, washing machine, and coffee machine. French doors open out to an enclosed patio, ideal for al fresco dining and gatherings. Adjacent to the kitchen is a stylish dining room featuring a large dining table and a breakfast bar option. French doors from the dining room also lead to the enclosed patio, ensuring a seamless indoor-outdoor living experience. Two steps down from the dining area, you’ll find the house bathroom, which includes a bath with a shower over it and a heated towel rail for added comfort.
The upper floors house five more uniquely decorated bedrooms, each with a Smart TV and many with original feature fireplaces. The master bedroom is particularly enchanting, featuring a freestanding slipper bath in the main room. All bedrooms have en-suite shower rooms, except for the two on the top floor, which share a bathroom with a large shower cubicle. Jorvik Villas is packed with original features that blend historic charm with modern luxury. The private courtyard, complete with a sauna and hot tub, offers a serene space for unwinding.
The villa is ideally located just minutes from the historic City Walls and York’s vibrant city centre, with its iconic attractions such as York Minster, the Jorvik Viking Centre, Castle Museum, and York’s Chocolate Story. Enjoy boat trips, explore cobbled streets, and meander down The Shambles, York’s most famous street. With a choice of pubs nearby and a host of events throughout the year, including York Races and one of Europe’s best Christmas markets, Jorvik Villas is the perfect house for families to come together and celebrate special moments in life. Family groups only.

reviews.comment: We found the property difficult to find and the information given about accessing the property via key safe was inaccurate and out dated which caused some unnecessary stress after a long journey. Once inside the property comfortably accommodated our party of 12. The kitchen was well equipped with main appliances but lacked a few basic utensils such as kitchen scissors and oven gloves. More general information about the house and local area would of been helpful. The children's play area was enjoyed by the younger members of the group but this does need some attention. Overall it was an enjoyable week and a nice base for a large family holiday

The property itself was lovely. It was very spacious and the outdoor area, including the field behind, was super for playing games together as a family. The  table outside was big  enough for everyone and the hot tub was also well  used by us. The indoor kitchen facilities were great, plenty of fridge space and kitchen cupboards. The pool table was definitely a family  favourite. A second key would have  made life easier for us as the gates only opened via the  key fob, so if only a  few  of you went out you couldn't take it as the others  would have been locked in. Consequently it meant you had  to phone someone to open the gate on  your arrival back and not everyone carries  there phone with them all of the time!! Overall, we had a  great time as a family, this is definitely  the  most spacious accomodation we have ever booked.

Meadow View is not worth the money. The pictures must have been taken quite a while ago. It's extremely tired. There were no basic items left out for us. Like, bin liners, dish washer tablets, washing up liquid. The special hot water tap wasn't hot enough to brew up with. The kettle was too small for 13 people. There was no electric kettle. The tea towels looked like floor cloths.To much water was wasted in the showers waiting for hot water to come through. We had to empty the kitchen bins into the outside bin loose due to lack of bin bags. The hot tub was good and the views were good.

long_description:
The Old Rectory is a fantastic celebratory home located within the buzzing town of Leek in Staffordshire, known as the ’Queen of the Moorlands’ and ’Gateway to the Peak District’. It oozes style but remains comfortable and cosy. As soon as you enter the grand hallway you will instantly feel at home.
The house has a stunning kitchen with an island and stools, all the equipment you should need, and is kitted out to cater to a house full with plenty of fridge space, wine fridge and two dishwashers. The kitchen is open plan to a relaxed dining area with bench seating and log burner, and there is a utility area off from the kitchen where you can store your walking boots and coats plus a washing machine. There is a large living room with ample, comfortable seating, large TV and a wood burner, a games room with a pool table and an array of board games to choose from, as well as a more formal dining room overlooking the garden. Upstairs on the first floor are four comfortable bedrooms, the master is incredibly spacious with dual aspect views and an impressive en-suite with a roll-top stand-alone bath and double shower. The other rooms on the first floor all are bright and spacious with en-suite bathrooms plus a toilet, all rooms have been named making it easy to know what is where. On the second floor are the remaining four bedrooms, the difference on the second floor is that the bedrooms Tittlesworth and Dovedale share a bathroom and there is an interconnecting door, perfect for a small family, there is also the addition of an extra single bed in the Tittlesworth. The manicured garden offers a private and relaxing outdoor area where lawn games can be played, a barbecue, and a long table with chairs to seat all guests, plus a 7-seater hydrotherapy spa pool to relax in at the end of the day.
The town of Leek sits in Staffordshire where you can explore its scenic moorlands, there are great walks such as The Roaches or Hartington Dales, and aside from walks, there are many other activities for you all to enjoy such as Alton Towers theme park being a short drive away as well as Water World. Trentham makes for a fantastic day out also, not only is it great for shopping at Trentham Shopping Village but you can also walk around Monkey Forest where there are over 140 monkeys.
Also nearby is the Peak Wildlife Park, RSPB Coombes Valley Nature Reserve and Tittlesworth Reservoir (for stand-up paddleboarding). There is something for everyone in this location, and knowing you have The Old Rectory to retreat back to at the end of the day makes your holiday even sweeter.

long_description:
Psalter Farmhouse stands detached on the edge of the Lincolnshire Wolds, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, in a rural location. Just over a mile away is the local pub (with bar and restaurant) at Skendleby Psalter. The Farmhouse offers plenty of space for all the family with two living rooms, one with an ornamental open fire, a large traditional conservatory/games room and large garden, which is perfect to retire to after a long day exploring the area.
The coastal resort of Skegness is just 10 miles away, with its sandy beaches and traditional amusements. For those wishing to explore the area, there are great walks and cycle routes straight from the door, as well as many good country pubs for refreshments along the way. Local market towns include Alford, Spilsby, Louth and Horncastle, famous for its many antique and collectable shops, are also only a short drive. The Battle of Britain Memorial Flight and Visitor Centre is based at Coningsby, only a 20-minute drive away, or visit East Kirkby Airfield, with its Lancaster Bomber, just 15-minute drive away and a must for WWII enthusiasts. Lincoln, famous for its cathedral, castle and Magna Carta Visitor Centre is only 40 minutes away. Beach 10 miles. Shop 2 miles, pub and restaurant 1¼ miles.

reviews.comment: What a wonderful holiday!  Sophie and the team were really attentive to our needs.  We had a really relaxing week!

Booked this property for my 30th birthday and it was a huge disappointment. Upon arrival we discovered that the hot tub was not working and despite this being raised with management, it could not be fixed at any point during our stay. This was particularly disappointing as the hot tub was one of the key facilities we had paid for and was a big part of why we chose the property. Whilst I appreciate that this is a farmhouse and some insects are to be expected, the overall cleanliness was not up to an acceptable standard. My bedroom alone had over 10 large spiders, there were lots of flies throughout the property, and the outside furniture was covered in bird droppings and appeared not to have been cleaned for some time. The BBQ had also clearly not been cleaned after the previous guests with leftover food still inside and a bun left on the grill when we arrived. We also encountered a number of other issues including a leaking fridge, lights that did not work in the games room, and problems with the toilet flushing. On several occasions, we had to use a bucket of water to help flush it properly. Unfortunately, the number of issues significantly affected what was supposed to be a special birthday stay. We requested a partial refund due to the hot tub being unavailable for the entirety of our stay, given that it was one of the advertised facilities we had paid for. However, the owner refused our request outright. Based on our experience, I would not recommend staying here. It was incredibly disappointing to feel that despite raising multiple issues, there was very little effort to resolve them or acknowledge the impact they had on our stay. I would give 0 stars if that were an option.

We had an excellent stay at the farmhouse with three families. The space was superb and exactly what we needed. I'd highly recommend it to anyone looking for a getaway with a larger group – fantastic value for money too! The hosts were very responsive whenever we had any questions or issues. Thanks so much for a wonderful stay!

Welcome to your dream holiday escape in the heart of the picturesque village of Barham, Suffolk. The beautiful property is located in a VERY QUIET residential area. This charming six -bedroom house that’s perfect for. family get togethers, invites you to experience the epitome of relaxation with a ten-person hot tub, your stay promises to be a perfect blend of tranquillity and indulgence.
As you step into this beautifully appointed residence, you are greeted by an atmosphere of comfort. The spacious living/dining and kitchen area is perfect for you all to be together, whilst the dining room is perfect for family get-togethers with a feast cooked in the spacious kitchen The six bedrooms are tastefully decorated, each providing a cosy retreat after a day of exploration. The master suite exudes sophistication with its dressing area and en-suite bathroom. The remaining bedrooms are equally inviting, providing a comfortable haven for a good night’s rest. There is also a large downstairs bedroom and bathroom. The Yes highlight of this holiday home is undoubtedly the garden with its ten-person hot tub, unwind after a day of adventure as the bubbles soothe your senses and the starlit sky provides a breathtaking backdrop.
It’s the ideal setting for creating lasting memories with family and friends.The private patio is the perfect spot for al fresco dining or simply enjoying a morning coffee as the sun rises. While the house itself offers a haven of relaxation, the surrounding area is brimming with activities to suit every taste.
Take a stroll through the charming village of Barham, where you’ll discover quaint shops and friendly locals. An extremely popular and family-run pub “Sorrell Horse” is a stone’s throw away with great food and drinks available Baylham House Rare Breeds farm is nearby, a working livestock farm, that specialises in native rare breeds. Needham Lake and Needham market town is a short drive away.
Walk around the lake and nature reserve with picnic and play facilities. A coffee shop is located at the park. Explore Ed Sheeran’s favourite places during your stay.For history enthusiasts, a visit to the nearby medieval Framlingham Castle is a must, offering a glimpse into the past and panoramic views of the Suffolk countryside. Wander through the grounds and explore the castle where Mary Tudor was proclaimed the Queen of England. If you are an English Heritage member, you can visit the castle for free.
Nature lovers will find themselves in paradise with the stunning landscapes of Dedham Vale and Constable Country just a short drive away. Explore the scenic trails, enjoy a boat ride along the River Stour, or simply bask in the beauty of the rolling hills. Foodies will delight in the local culinary scene, with quaint pubs and restaurants serving up delicious Suffolk specialities. Indulge in fresh seafood, artisan cheeses, and locally produced wines for a Yes taste of the region. A day at the Suffolk coast is a must and the towns of Aldeburgh, Thorpeness, Southwold and Woodbridge are only 40 minutes away. The desired temperature of the hot tub might not be available on your arrival , due to same day check out / check in .
