long_description:
All properties: Electric heating, electricity, bed linen and Wi-Fi included. Towel hire £2per person. Travel cot and highchair available on request. Grounds (shared with other guests on-site). Barbecue. Indoor heated swimming pool with shower and changing facilities (shared, 12m x 6m, depth 1.6m, open 8.30am-9pm all year). Hot tub (shared with other guests on-site. All weather tennis court, small gym, games room with table tennis and table football, indoor skittle alley and children’s play area (shared with other guests on-site). Karaoke machine with on screen graphics for hire. Beauty therapist available by arrangement with the owner. Fishing (rods for hire). No smoking. Please note: There are ponds in the grounds.

Sherrill Farm Holiday Cottages is a complex of 13 delightful self catering cottages (refs UKC1427 to UKC1439), converted from the original 300 year old barns and farmhouse set within 16 acres of Devon farmland. Clustered around the central courtyard, the properties retain many original features and are charmingly furnished and decorated, with well-equipped kitchens. (Some properties are adjoining, whilst others occupy either the ground floor or the first floor of the same cottage). Located near Dartmoor and midway between Tavistock and Launceston on the Devon/Cornwall border, in wonderful rolling countryside.
Approached by its own private driveway, Sherrill Farm is a perfect spot to relax and unwind or to use as a base for exploring north and south Devon, and Cornwall.
This farm complex is a superb place for the entire family, and all guests have use of the large indoor heated swimming pool, Jacuzzi, gymnasium, bowling alley and games room. This leisure complex is open daily until 9pm. After an energetic swim you can step out onto the surrounding sun terrace and enjoy the stunning south-facing views, whilst the children keep themselves entertained in their own play area. There is also an all-weather tennis court available and rackets can be hired on site; a picnic area and a summerhouse along the banks of the ponds. This really is a beautiful area offering perfect family accommodation, peace and tranquillity.
There are three ponds within the grounds, one has been especially created to encourage wildlife and is set in beautiful surroundings. The other 2 ponds have been stocked with fish for those wishing to try their hand at this relaxing pastime (rods can be hired on site). Many bird species can be seen in the area as it is so quiet here and foxes and badgers are often seen on a summer’s evening.
A short drive away is the beautiful Tamar Valley dividing Devon and Cornwall, with picturesque and historical riverside villages including Morewellham. Within minutes you can be venturing out onto the Dartmoor National Park with over 250,000 acres of wild rugged open moorland, a haven for hikers or dog walkers. There are many exciting places to visit including Morwellham Quay and the National Trust properties of Cotehele, Buckland Abbey and Lydford Gorge with its White Lady Waterfall.
The historic market town of Tavistock is just 6 miles away and is a popular town with indoor pannier market and local shops selling locally produced foods. Horse riding is also available locally, as is trout fishing. Why not try canoeing on the River Tamar, or perhaps cycling on the Plym Valley track? The north and south coasts of both Devon and Cornwall are within easy reach by car and offer an amazing choice of splendid sandy beaches, a variety of water sports, cliff top walks, swimming, surfing and other seaside activities. The owners can also recommend local caterers, and guests can contact Lifton Farm Shop to organise a hog roast. Beach 20 miles. Shop 4½ miles, pub 1 mile and restaurant 1¼ miles.

long_description:
Just 2 miles from the sea, this enchanting period detached holiday property is surrounded by its own large lawned garden and is a perfect choice at any time of year for large families and discerning groups wishing to holiday together. Beautifully furnished to a high standard and well-equipped throughout, it boasts a wood-burning stove in the living room, seating for 12 in the dining room and sheltered decked terrace overlooking the garden - a perfect spot for enjoying outdoor dining or just simply relaxing. The property provides ground floor sleeping accommodation with twin bedrooms and a bathroom for guests wishing to avoid stairs. The area of North Norfolk is a haven for wildlife, with excellent walking and bird watching amid the nearby salt marshes and sand dunes, a must for any enthusiast. Lavender Cottage is centrally located to explore Norfolk’s amazing coastline and attractions and the popular seaside town of Wells-next-the-Sea is 2 miles with an excellent wide sandy beach, picturesque fishing port (great for crabbing, fresh shell fish) and town centre with many excellent bistro inns, cafes, restaurants and shops. Holkham Hall and an excellent sandy beach backed by pine trees are 6 miles. Boat trips are available to the seal colony, RSPB and nature reserves at Morson Harbour. Bustling villages including Blakeney Quay, the historical market town of Holt, and Burnham Market are an easy drive. The medieval village of Walsingham (2 miles) is rich in archaeological treasures, historical and religious interests whilst Wells and Walsingham light railway is well worth a visit. The Norfolk Coastal Path offers excellent rambling opportunities, and is an invigorating way to see Norfolk’s smooth green belt. Shops 2 miles and pub 330 yards.
Please note: There are steep stairs at the property.

Thatched Cottage is a spacious detached six bedroom property for 12 guests and is suitable for a large family or a group of friends. It is a beautifully furnished converted restaurant set within the town of Kingsteignton, 2 miles from Newton Abbot and 1 mile from Newton Abbot racecourse. Spend some time unwinding in the open plan living and dining area on the ground floor which is light, airy and has plenty of room and home comforts for everyone to spread out. Perfect for a relaxing evening indoors when you’re not out exploring the delights of the local area. Next door, the kitchen is well equipped to prepare a family dinner. It is perfect for socialising whilst cooking a home-cooked meal. From the living room three steps lead down to a separate games room area which houses a pool table, a bar with stools, a gaming fruit machine (which is free to use with no prizes), a dart board, a 40” Smart TV with Freeview and Netflix. Upstairs are 6 bedrooms each with a Freeview Smart TV with Netflix. The enclosed walled garden is great for pets and it features a 5-seater hot tub, a barbecue, 2 picnic benches on the lawn plus a small patio area with a bench, great for enjoying your morning coffee.
Kingsteignton has a choice of shops, pubs, a variety of eateries and sporting facilities, and the nearby towns and villages offer a variety of attractions. Nearby Newton Abbott can be reached from the doorstep along the walking and cycling path which takes you through the Hackney Marshes nature reserve. The ancient market town offers plenty of local shops, high street chains and supermarkets. There’s also a racecourse where National Hunt racing takes place from spring until autumn, with craft fairs during the winter.
There are a number of beaches within easy driving distance including Teignmouth, Torquay and Paignton, which also has a zoo. Spend a day on the beach building sand castles and walk the impressive Victorian Pier at Teignmouth. Enjoy the stunning beaches around Torquay and the many hidden coves such as Meadfoot, Oddicombe, and further afield, the pretty Ness Cove. And of course, the South West Coast Path provides stunning seascapes across the bay, with a popular stretch from Torquay Harbour to Daddyhole Plain.
The Dartmoor National Park is nearby with rugged and stunning scenery where you can enjoy walking, cycling, horse riding, climbing and canoeing. You can see the ponies, walk the Tors or simply stop off in one of the many villages for a Devon cream tea. For the children, there is Crealy Adventure Park or Go Ape in Haldon. There are many cycle ways off road, including Powderham Castle where there is a cycle track along the estuary. Other memorable days out include the Round Robin Bus Trip, Paignton Zoo, Woodlands Adventure Park, Babbacombe Model Village and Kents Cavern. Beach 3 miles. Shop and pub ¼ mile, restaurant 1 mile
Please note: There are open, steep, spiral or narrow stairs at the property.

long_description:
Canal View House (ref UK39363) and The Gallery Barn (ref UK39368) are wonderful properties that are ideal for any special occasion. Gather with extended family and friends and relax in your own private hot tub. Nestled alongside Dilham Canal, boasting waterside views, this quiet waterway, approximately 9 miles long, runs onto the market town of North Walsham. As well as private hot tubs, both properties feature a fantastic games room. In Canal View House (ref UK39363), cosy nights in can be enjoyed snuggled up by the wood burner, and the well-equipped kitchen offers the opportunity to dine in. There is also a private enclosed garden, perfect for al fresco eating and relaxation.
This is a great location to explore or simply relax and unwind on the comfy sofas, or maybe even enjoy a tranquil evening under the stars relaxing in the hot tub. There are opportunities for great walking and cycling to enjoy direct from the doorstep, having miles of footpaths and trails to explore, including local woods, footpaths, North Walsham, and in part, alongside the Dilham Canal.
Explore the excellent sandy beaches of the North Norfolk Coast or the Norfolk Broads. The seaside village of Mundesley, 4 miles, has an excellent sandy beach, and the seaside resorts of Cromer and Sheringham also house glorious sandy beaches and are host to many attractions. Cromer boasts a pier, with a carnival week which is held in August and, weather permitting, a spectacular New Year’s Day celebration, complete with fireworks. Sheringham is home to the North Norfolk Steam Railway, Splash fun pool and Sheringham Gardens. There are numerous bird sanctuaries, salt marshes and wildlife centres that punctuate the region.
Wroxham, 12 miles, is known as capital of the Norfolk Broads and has daily boat hires and river trips available, riverside cafés, pubs and shops. The market town of North Walsham, 2 miles, is perfect for guests to visit the supermarkets, shops, cafés, library and bank, as well as the vast bistro and gourmet eating establishments in the surrounding area. Enjoy a trip to the city of Norwich, 16 miles, where there is a fantastic castle museum, cathedral, excellent shopping, theatre, art galleries, cafés, pubs and restaurants.
Places of historical interest and stately homes can be found within easy driving distance, and Blickling Hall boasts open air concerts during the summer season. Perfect for entertaining the younger generations, these properties are also close to Banham Zoo, Wroxham Barns craft centre and play park, Dinosaur Adventure Park at Lenwade and BeWILDerwood at Horning. There are also many places within driving distance, ideal for walking your four-legged friends, including Blickling Park, where you can also enjoy lunch afterwards at the local pub. Beach 4 miles. Shop, pub and restaurant 2 miles.
Canal View House (ref UK39363) can be booked together with The Gallery Barn (ref UK39368) to accommodate up to 24 guests.

long_description:
Set in the prestigious and leafy neighbourhood of Emerson Park, this impressive six-bedroom, five-bathroom house offers the perfect balance of luxury, space and location. Designed for memorable stays with family or friends, the property combines generous indoor living with standout outdoor entertainment features, making it ideal for both relaxed retreats and celebratory get-togethers.
The house itself is spacious, modern and beautifully laid out. With six well-appointed bedrooms and five bathrooms, there is ample room for larger groups to spread out comfortably while still enjoying time together. The heart of the home opens out to the garden, where an outdoor heated swimming pool takes centre stage, perfect for warm summer days and leisurely evenings alike. A private hot tub adds an extra layer of indulgence, ideal for unwinding after a day of exploring. The separate summer house creates a fantastic social hub, complete with a pool table and bar area — a great spot for friendly competition, drinks, and relaxed nights without ever needing to leave the property. The luxurious cinema/games room is perfect for family entertainment. Every element has been designed with comfort, entertainment and ease in mind.
Beyond the front door, Emerson Park offers a highly sought after setting known for its peaceful atmosphere, tree lined streets and elegant homes. This is an area that feels calm and exclusive, yet remains exceptionally well connected, making it a superb base for exploring both the local surroundings and greater London. Guests can enjoy the best of suburban tranquillity while still having easy access to vibrant town centres, cultural attractions and transport links into the city.
The local area is rich in green spaces, perfect for morning walks, jogging, or relaxed afternoons outdoors. Well-maintained parks and open spaces provide a refreshing contrast to urban life and are ideal for families and groups looking to enjoy fresh air during their stay. Nearby, you’ll find a wide choice of cafés, restaurants and traditional pubs, offering everything from casual brunches to refined dining experiences. Explore history at the RAF Hornchurch Heritage Centre and relax in Hornchurch Country Park. Other top activities include visiting Hopefield Animal Sanctuary, strolling through Langtons House gardens, and golfing at Upminster Golf Club.
Shopping options are plentiful, with a mix of independent boutiques, high-street favourites and larger shopping centres just a short drive away. For those wanting to explore further afield, excellent transport connections make day trips into central London straightforward, opening world class museums, theatres, the popular Covent Garden or Soho and varied nightlife.
Whether you’re planning a summer escape, a celebratory break or a relaxed gathering with friends and family, Emerson Park Villa offers a rare combination of luxury living and an outstanding location. It’s a place where you can truly switch off, enjoy your surroundings, and create unforgettable memories all from the comfort of an exceptional home in one of the area’s most desirable neighbourhoods.

long_description:
Mouthlock Chapel is a spacious converted chapel dating back to the early 1900’s. This charming, detached stone property with self-contained annexe, sits amidst its own private garden, complete with patio and garden furniture, perfect for dining al fresco. This stylish holiday home has tremendous views that change by the minute and weather permitting can stretch up to 30 miles along the beautiful Eden Valley, and never disappoints.
The chapel is equipped to a good standard with a lovely mix of contemporary and antique furniture. The spacious living room features a wood burner for cosy evenings by the fire, while the conservatory provides an extra sociable space for guests to relax. There are six comfortable bedrooms, comfortably accommodating large family get-togethers or groups.
Situated in the east of the county in an enviable rural location, the property is ideally placed for exploring the highlights of the north of England. This detached holiday home is sandwiched between the Lakes and Dales National Parks, both within a 40-minute drive and sure to make for a great day out. During your stay you could visit Northumberland, Hadrian’s Wall, the Pennines (an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty), Teesdale, where you can visit the most spectacular waterfall in England, and the Scottish Borders, all within an easy scenic drive, making this a perfect holiday base. Tan Hill, the highest pub in England, is romantically set in a wild, moorland landscape, five miles away, and there is a good selection of pubs, restaurants and galleries in Brough and Kirkby Stephen, six miles away. A 15 mile drive will take you to the market town of Barnard Castle hosting an array of shops, pubs and restaurants.

reviews.comment: This accommodation is tricky to review and explain.  It is a more like a conference centre than a holiday let.  It is well equipped (including a great hot tub), but none of the fixtures are 4 or 5 star.  What was cleaned was done well, but some of the area was clearly not cleaned before our visit. Ignore the low score for local amenities, the whole point is that this place is in the middle of nowhere!
Very beautiful location and the place contained all necessities with a wide array of things to do. Would definitely recommend!

Situated in a quiet part of Cadeleigh, these beautiful, detached, barn conversions overlook the ponds and the deer with amazing views across the rolling hills of Devon. Set 100 yards apart within the owner’s 40-acre deer farm, nestled next to the ponds, the properties are accessed by an unmade track and provide beautiful, spacious accommodation. Perfect for friends to get together, celebrations or a family holiday.
The Otters (ref UKC3930) has been decorated and furnished to a good standard, each bedroom has en-suite facilities, and there is a spacious open plan living area with underfloor heating.
The Linhay (ref UKC1290) has a kitchen/dining room with large picture windows offering lovely views down the valley; the living room has a wood burner, ideal for those cosy nights in throughout the winter, and most of the bedrooms have en-suite facilities.
Kingfishers Lodge (ref UK36063) is a luxurious and spacious three-bedroom barn conversion, showcasing open plan living, underfloor heating, a private hot tub and bi-fold doors.
Deer Park (ref UK36064) is a luxurious and spacious three-bedroom barn conversion, showcasing open plan living, underfloor heating and bi fold doors seamlessly blending the living spaces with the outdoor landscape. The kitchen is fully equipped and there is also a utility with a washing machine.
All of the properties have their own private garden and on balmy summer evenings, is the ideal spot to relax with the prossecco which the thoughtful owners will leave for your arrival. All of the properties have a private hot tub, so don’t forget your towels!
With these properties being located on a deer farm, red deer and amazing stags can be seen close up, and there are sometimes otters in the ponds. Although the ponds are unfenced, the properties gardens are fenced, so there is some barrier between the garden and ponds.
The village of Cadeleigh lies just 9 miles from Exeter, with its magnificent cathedral and many shops and canalside pubs. Tiverton is just 6 miles away, and Bickleigh Mill with its lovely river walks, small fun railway, shop and café, is nearby. Spend a day exploring tranquil moorland and winding rivers in the Exmoor National Park, as well as the breathtaking coastline full of secluded bays and spectacular cliffs. Exmoor is sprinkled with quaint villages, attractive towns and charming harbours. Enjoy a day out at Tiverton Canal, walk with the horse drawn canal boat or enjoy a boat trip. Alternatively, take a trip to the north Devon coast and explore the dramatic coastlines and sandy beaches. Beach 24 miles. Shop 6 miles, pub and restaurant ½ mile.
These properties can be booked together to accommodate up to 40 guests.

long_description:
Nestled in the beautiful Cumbrian countryside Blaithwaite Estate is surrounded by 80 acres of estate grounds made up of 30 acres of gardens and grounds and 50 acres of woodland. Blaithwaite Stables (ref UKC1359) is the old stable building for the Blaithwaite Estate and has been carefully renovated to a very good standard, while keeping characterful original features such as the old range, but don’t worry, guests have all the modern conveniences to cook with! Twenty people can be comfortably accommodated in eight rooms, all but one room are en-suite, and two of the ground floor bedrooms are wheelchair friendly. The Stables overlook the superb old courtyard with access to the beautiful orchard, miniature golf and garden chess set.
On the estate there are two play areas, mini-golf, football fields, woodland walks and laser tag is available (must be pre-booked. Please check the what’s on section of our website for further details). The woodland is made up of rare specialist trees and fascinating wetlands which you can explore for hours in peace. If you fancy exploring the area, the estate is set midway between Keswick and Carlisle where you can find a great range of shops, restaurants and bars, plus museums and activities to suit a wide range of tastes and interests. Beach 10 miles. Shop 1½ miles, pub 2 miles and restaurant 5 miles.
These properties can be booked together to accommodate larger groups.

This former barn used by the farm for storing the apples from the orchard next to it for generations now provides spacious modern holiday accommodation for families and friends to get together and enjoy. Be welcomed into the large open plan living with views to the front flow into the kitchen with breakfast bar and also the galleried hallway. This is the heart of the property with an inviting atmosphere and comfortable ambience, creating the perfect place not only to enjoy homely meals rustled up in the well-equipped kitchen, but enjoying them and cosying to reminisce over the day’s adventures as it draws to an end.
To the rear of the property is a huge games and cinema room with bi-fold doors opening out onto the terrace and rear garden ensuring entertainment options for all, while the lawned garden is ideal for a family football competition with grounds and the nearby woods to explore, or simply kicking back and enjoying a meal al-fresco on the BBQ with a glass of your favourite tipple, or a morning coffee to plan the adventures the next day holds. Why not take advantage of enjoying a night under the stars? All while enjoying the warmth of the hot tub bubbling away.
Situated in a small village, 6 miles from the town of Sleaford where you can catch the train for a day out in Skegness or even London. There are lovely walks through the surrounding countryside and cycle routes straight from your accommodation. An abundance of wildlife surrounds you and you may be lucky enough to see the deer in the paddock next door. Shop and pub serving food 1.5 miles

reviews.comment: We really enjoyed our stay overall. The property itself is in a beautiful area and is very spacious, making it a comfortable place to stay for large groups. However, there were a few areas that could be improved. The overall cleanliness of the property needs attention, as it did not feel as clean as we would have expected. We also experienced an issue with drain flies in the bathroom, which was unpleasant and something that should ideally be addressed between guests.We also found the property lacked some basic essentials, such as tea towels, oven gloves and cleaning products.We had an issue trying to work out how to use the EV charger. When we contacted the maintenance number for assistance, we were advised to contact the owner. Unfortunately, when we did so, the response was that dealing with the issue was an inconvenience at the time. This was disappointing, as we were simply looking for some guidance with the equipment provided at the property.The listing also advertised a welcome pack, but unfortunately there wasn't one provided during our stay.Overall, the property has a lot going for it  particularly its beautiful location, the hot tub and spaciousness. With improvements to the overall cleanliness, better provision of basic essentials, attention to the bathroom issue, and better support for guests using the facilities, the experience could be considerably better.
Outdoor space amazing, furniture could do with repair. Bedrooms slightly apart from master bedroom. Need more clothing space . Lovely big house and garden

Disappointed to find no car charging point despite advertising as available. Outside furniture whilst usable had seen better days. Good size kitchen with plenty of utensils glasses and crockery. Large cinema room was used and enjoyed. A couple of minor issues were quickly sorted. Summing up we all had a great time in this holiday home.

long_description:
Nestling in the pretty Norfolk countryside close to the heart of the Norfolk Broads, Willow Barn (ref CZB) and single-storey Beech Barn (ref CZU) and Alderfen Barn (ref UK30458) are detached holiday properties dating back to the 1700s, situated in the grounds of the owner’s home. Providing a perfect retreat for discerning larger family groups, these converted barns offer spacious and comfortable accommodation boasting beamed interiors, wood-burning stoves and enclosed separate gardens with private hot tubs, and for a special meal or family celebration gourmet meals can be arranged with the owner.
For Beech Barn (ref CZU), between Easter and the 16th July, and the 1st September-1st November, for 7 night bookings the owner is offering free boat hire for one day.
Beech Farm Barns are ideally located for all the family and for nature lovers there is an abundance of bird life. Within walking distance is Alderfen Broad, which is situated in The Broads National Park, a bird watcher’s delight. For the children there is BeWILDerwood Adventure Park with its treehouses, zip wires, jungle bridges and boat trips, which all combined makes a great day out. Nearby is the attractive Broads village of Horning with its selection of tea shops, restaurants and pubs. A day boat can be hired directly from the owner, or book a trip on the Mississippi steamer. The sandy beaches of the North Norfolk Coast are only 10 miles away. Alternatively spend a day in the fine city of Norwich with its magnificent cathedrals, castle, museums, theatres, market and vast array of cafes and shops. There is a wealth of National Trust properties to visit in the area which include Felbrigg Hall, Garden and Park (one of the finest 17th-century country Jacobean houses in East Anglia), Blickling Hall (a magnificent house with woodlands and lakeside walks) and Sheringham Park (beautifully landscaped and renowned for its spectacular displays of azaleas and rhododendrons in late spring). Shops and pub 1½ miles.
Beech Barn (CZU), Willow Barn (CZB), Alderfen Barn (UK30458) and Kings Lodge (UK39013) can be booked together to accommodate up to 36 guests

long_description:
A delightful detached cottage situated next to a working farm in the village of Llanyblodwel near to Oswestry in Shropshire. Well-furnished throughout to provide ample accommodation for families or groups of friends who wish to spend time together in this beautiful part of Shropshire.
With parts of the cottage dating back to the medieval period, there are many traditional features prevalent in the older sections, such as exposed beams and low doors. The ground floor has a large, fitted kitchen with plenty of space to cook for large numbers, this leads to a spacious dining room with seating for all of the guests. After dinner, guests can retreat to the sitting room and relax by the wood burning stove or enjoy an evening in front of the TV. For those who prefer to watch something different, or simply want some peace and quiet, there is an additional snug with comfortable sofas and a TV located in the older portion of the cottage. There is a games room with a pool table and football table to keep children or adults alike entertained. On warmer evenings, guests can enjoy a refreshing drink in the hot tub overlooking to stunning countryside landscape. Outside is a front patio area where guests can plan the day’s activities, leading to an extra paddock which is great for the kids to enjoy.
The rural village of Llanyblodwel offers beautiful countryside. Just one mile from the Welsh border and close to the Berwyn Mountain Range, there is an abundance of scenic walks and cycle trails to explore. The town of Oswestry is just a short drive away where there are a variety of shops and restaurants to try. Close to a number of tourist attractions, Garth Ucha can be enjoyed throughout the year. Car essential. Pub and restaurant 2½ miles.

long_description:
Perfect for a family get-together, reunion, or a special occasion, this celebration house is set in an eighty-acre private estate, surrounded by woodland walks, and open views, and offers easy access to The Northern Fells and the Lake District National Park.
On the first floor, you’ll find five bedrooms with a range of beds to sleep up to ten guests suited to adults and children. From the windows, you have views of the surrounding farmland and fields and the garden at the rear. All bedrooms are well-equipped with comfortable beds hanging space, storage, and beamed ceilings. There’s a shower room too. Downstairs is where the fun begins, the piano bar comes with cool neon lights and a pool table where you can challenge your friends while sipping a cocktail. There’s a large family room to sleep up to four guests in a double and two singles. Leading to a conservatory with views of the garden and direct access to the hot tub. There’s a family bathroom with Jack and Jill doors, one from the family bedroom and the other side to the hallway. The showstopper is the huge open-plan living room/kitchen/diner. The perfect space to spend time with loved ones. Firstly, wow, what a view! With floor-to-ceiling glass on two sides, these bi-fold doors open to the garden and decking where you’ll find garden furniture, great views, and the hot tub for a dip after a day of adventure. The kitchen features an aga and all the mod cons, there’s a utility with additional appliances and a boot room, and a separate walk-in shower. This house is full of surprises. This cosy property features underfloor heating on the ground floor and plenty of easy seating where you can relax and enjoy the large screen Smart TV to round off the day with a drink in hand, surrounded by your favourite people. Nestled in the beautiful Cumbrian countryside, Blaithwaite Estate is surrounded by 80 acres of estate grounds made up of thirty acres of gardens and grounds and 50 acres of woodland. Guests can enjoy the old courtyard with access to the beautiful orchard, miniature golf, and garden chess set.
The estate has two play areas, mini-golf, football fields, woodland walks, and laser tag is available (must be pre-booked). The woodland is made up of rare specialist trees and fascinating wetlands which you can explore for hours in peace. If you fancy exploring the area, the estate is set midway between Keswick and Carlisle where you can find a great range of shops, restaurants, and bars, plus museums and activities to suit a wide range of tastes and interests.
These properties can be booked together for larger groups.

reviews.comment: We had a wonderful three days break to celebrate  my wife's 80th. birthday. All the family were there including young grand children. Ten of us in total. The bedroom arrangement suited us all and were spotless, quaint and warm. Our favourite room was the open plan lounge and kitchen. Spacious and comfortable with great views, The kitchen has a huge long table which we all sat around for our meals. We all loved the Aga! cooker! The games room was a bonus and the pool table well used. As was the hot tub which was in constant demand. This is checked every morning. The decking patio was excellent and I already miss the view of the Solway.  The garden and grounds were perfect but some sections closed because of a private event. There is not much to do in the area surrounding the estate but we were happy spending our evenings at the house. The bottle of bubbly left on the table on our arrival was a nice touch. I would definitely recommend The Coach House and will certainly consider booking it again.
Excellent family holiday in a beautiful location, staff all friendly and helpful, definitely be going back

We moved the coffee table and underneath was a biscuit and loads of crumbs also a tee shirt pushed into a corner in the kitchen.The AGA was hot at all times and  was not to be adjusted which was a bit of a safety risk for young children .Just had to be mindful of that. However we would return as everyone in our party loved it and the panoramic views were beautiful

long_description:
Nestled in the picturesque countryside near Sudbury, Lime Tree House , a six bedroom holiday home in the charming village of Bulmer, offers a luxurious and spacious retreat for families, groups, or anyone seeking a relaxing getaway. Whether you’re planning a weekend escape or a longer stay, this modern property is designed with comfort and style in mind, providing everything you need for a memorable stay. Lime Tree House has been designed to create a warm and welcoming atmosphere. The open living areas are perfect for unwinding after a day of exploration, watching a movie or to sit around and chat. The spacious dining area is ideal for gathering around for meals and the fully equipped kitchen, central island and walk in pantry is perfect for preparing everything from a quick breakfast to a family dinner.
Each of the six kingsize bedrooms in this stunning home comes with its own en-suite bathroom, offering total privacy and convenience. The bedrooms are generously sized, elegantly decorated with soothing tones, and furnished with comfortable beds, ensuring a restful night’s sleep for all guests. The en-suites are equipped with high-end fixtures and fittings and walk in showers. There is a ground floor bedroom and bathroom for the less able, making every bathroom experience a pampering one. The expansive landing has amazing views across the countryside. Large windows throughout the property allow natural light to flood the interior, enhancing the open and airy feel of the space. Outside, the property boasts a garden, perfect for enjoying the peaceful surroundings or simply soaking up the fresh countryside air. Whether you’re relaxing on the patio with a drink in hand, enjoying a meal al fresco, or letting the kids run around, the outdoor space offers ample room for all guests to enjoy.
Located in the quiet village of Bulmer, just a short drive from the historic town of Sudbury, this property offers a perfect base for exploring the Suffolk countryside. The house is in easy reach if Bury St Edmunds, Colchester, Cambridge, Braintree and Chelmsford, and close enough for a day trip to the Suffolk Coast. You can even go by train from Sudbury to London in less than one and a half hours! Sudbury is home to a variety of local shops, cafes, and restaurants, as well as the renowned Gainsborough House, the birthplace of the famous artist Thomas Gainsborough. Sit at The Mill Hotel with its waterwheel and look out across the Water Meadows, or walk or cycle the old railway line. Go for a drink or arrange a Brewery and Distillery Tour at the local Nethergate Brewery. For those who enjoy outdoor activities, the nearby area provides plenty of opportunities for walking, cycling, and exploring scenic landscapes.
With its combination of modern amenities, stylish décor, and idyllic location, Lime Tree House in Bulmer offers the ultimate countryside retreat. Whether you’re here for relaxation or adventure, this beautiful home will ensure your stay is truly unforgettable.
This property can be booked together with UK50450 and UK49479 to accommodate up to 16 guests.

long_description:
This stunning Grade II listed Georgian property offers an exceptional and luxurious space for large groups to relax, celebrate and enjoy the beauty of the surrounding countryside. The property is well equipped to ensure a comfortable stay including fuel for the open fire and a welcome pack on arrival. Set within extensive grounds, the house boasts wonderful views across the landscaped gardens and rolling land beyond, providing a truly impressive setting for a memorable stay.
Formerly operated as a hotel, the property offers generous living accommodation throughout, with every bedroom benefiting from its own luxury en-suite facilities. Elegant period features are complemented by modern comforts, creating a refined yet welcoming atmosphere. Guests can gather in the impressive dining room, where a large table comfortably seats up to 30 people, making it ideal for celebrations, special occasions or group meals.
On the ground floor, a spacious cloakroom area provides excellent facilities, including two cubicles for ladies, a cubicle and two urinals for gents, along with an additional accessible toilet designed for ease of use by all guests.
Outside, guests have access to private gardens with lawned areas, patio space and garden furniture, perfect for enjoying the peaceful surroundings. An outdoor swimming pool (10m x 5m, depth 0.8m to 1.3m) is available daily from 9:00am to 9:00pm between April and September, while a private hot tub for four offers a relaxing place to unwind during the warmer months. The grounds also provide ample private parking for up to 20 cars.
Ideally located close to the Wye Valley, the house is within easy driving distance of the cathedral cities of Hereford, Worcester and Gloucester. The area offers a wealth of activities for all interests, from kayaking and canoeing along the River Wye to scenic walks and guided tours of historic landmarks such as Goodrich Castle and Symonds Yat Rock. Golf enthusiasts are well catered for with several nearby courses, including the picturesque Rolls of Monmouth and Ross-on-Wye golf clubs.
Combining elegant accommodation, excellent facilities and a superb location, this remarkable Georgian property provides the perfect setting for an unforgettable group getaway.

long_description:
Set on the owners’ non-working farm in Horbling village, this detached farmhouse, with its own swimming pool and hot tub, lies in the heart of the Fens, an ideal touring base for visiting the area’s wealth of historic attractions. Providing comfortable holiday accommodation for families, it retains many original features, including exposed woodwork, an ornate cornice in the dining room and a traditional farmhouse-style kitchen. There is a second sitting room, well-stocked library and video and DVD collection (including latest releases). There are also five family bathrooms, providing luxury towels for an added touch of comfort. Outside is a large, private, rear lawned garden with apple, pear, plum trees and gooseberries which guests are welcome to pick in season, and a large patio with garden furniture and barbecue. There is also the added bonus of a private hot tub.
As this property is located within a designated conservation area, the owner kindly request that all noise and music be kept to a minimum during the evening hours, particularly from 11PM onwards to minimalise any potential noise pollution, keeping this preserved area protected.
The fenlands make ideal walking and cycling country, an excellent way to view the landscape with its rich farmlands, huge skies and wonderful sunsets; walks can be enjoyed from the doorstep; facilities can be found nearby for golf, fishing or horse riding. Close by are a wealth of interesting places, including the old towns of Uppingham, Oakham and Stamford, full of beautiful stone buildings, alongside Burleigh House, one of England’s greatest Elizabethan houses. Nearby Spalding is an attractive, Dutch-influenced town and centre of the flower-bulb industry, where the Springfields show gardens and the annual flower festival in May are popular. Tattershall Castle (NT), Belton House and Coningsby, noted for its huge one-handed church clock, and the home of the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight. One of the landmarks of the Fens is the octagonal lantern tower of St Botolph’s Church in Boston. Shop and good pub with food ½ mile in Billingborough, or village pub 300 yards.

long_description:
Endeavour is a beautifully restored detached farmhouse located at Woodhouse Farm, just steps away from the estate’s indoor swimming pool, games room and other shared facilities. Perfect for families or groups, each property is maintained to the highest standards, and this elegant home has retained many original charms retained, such as oak-beamed ceilings and wood or tiled floors, blending traditional style and country charm with modern luxury.
The heart of the house is a generous open-plan living and dining space, featuring deep leather sofas around a large Smart TV with Bluetooth speaker, alongside two log-burning stoves with logs provided to create a warm, inviting atmosphere all year round (logs provided). The dining area flows into a spacious kitchen, equipped with an oil-fired AGA, an electric oven, a microwave, an American-style fridge/freezer, a dishwasher, and washing machine for home-from-home convenience for the ideal relaxed self-catering stay.
The house has a private sauna room found in the rear utility room, offering a tranquil space to unwind after a day exploring the Devon countryside, and also on the ground floor there is a comfortable double bedroom with its own en-suite bathroom, along with a separate downstairs cloakroom.
Upstairs, guests will find six additional bedrooms, each designed with comfort and practicality in mind. Every comfort has been thoughtfully considered at Endeavour Farmhouse to ensure a seamless and relaxing stay. Enjoy electric heating, superfast Wi-Fi, and the inclusion of all electricity, bed linen, and towels. Families are also well catered for, with added convenience in the way of a cot and highchair available on request, and there’s even a shared outdoor playground is on site.
For convenience, a payphone is located in the foyer of the indoor swimming pool building. Outside, guests can unwind in the enclosed garden and patio, complete with outdoor furniture and a barbecue for relaxed dining in the fresh country air. Private Parking is available for this property, with electric vehicle charging also available at this site. The indoor swimming pool complex is at this site, each property has scheduled private access on a rota provided by the owners prior to arrival. Our cottages are designed for comfort and practicality, with a wide range of Devon attractions right on your doorstep.
Sleeping from 6 to 28 guests, the cottages can be combined to accommodate larger groups. For an extra touch, you can even book an in-house chef to handle your catering.
Set in the heart of the rolling Devon countryside, the privately owned Ashcombe Country Estate nestles in a quiet, beautiful valley, surrounded by endless things to do and just a short drive from the sandy beaches of Dawlish and Torquay too. Enjoy peaceful walks through the estate’s hills and woodlands. Just under a mile down the lane lies the Ashcombe Shooting Ground, offering clay pigeon shooting, quad bike safaris, and archery (available at extra cost for ages 14+). Also on the estate, A Touch of the Wild runs exciting forest activity camps where children can enjoy bushcraft, campfire cooking, bug hunting, and woodland adventures, a wonderful way to spark a lifelong love of the outdoors.
In the evenings, join the friendly locals at the local pub, open on various nights with inexpensive local beer and Ashcombe Cider, summer fêtes, and community events. Guests can also book guided foraging walks to discover the simple pleasure of finding wild foods in the Devon countryside. Both Dartmoor National Park and the historic city of Exeter are just a 20-minute drive away, while the South Devon Coast and its sandy beaches are only 3 miles. Nearby, you’ll find Exeter and Newton Abbot Racecourses, golf courses, family theme parks, zoos, sailing, and fishing, as well as Devon’s famous pubs and restaurants. Walk the wild beauty of Dartmoor, visit nearby National Trust properties (including Agatha Christie’s Greenway), or enjoy a steam train journey from Kingswear to Paignton or Totnes to Buckfastleigh. Explore historic Dartmouth with its harbour, castle, galleries, and the spectacular Regatta Week and Air Show. Salcombe, Blackpool Sands, Slapton, and Dittisham are all within easy reach, while East Cornwall and the Eden Project are less than an hour’s drive away. Adventurers can also try Rock Solid Coasteering along the Jurassic Coastline.
All major supermarkets deliver directly to your cottage. Main shops are 3 miles away. All in all, Ashcombe is the perfect base to explore, experience, and enjoy the very best of Devon, “The Cream of Devon.”

long_description:
Fairwinds is a luxurious six-bedroom, four-bathroom coastal retreat set in the highly sought-after village of St Mawes, offering generous space, refined comfort, and breathtaking sea views. Thoughtfully designed for families and larger groups, the property provides a welcoming balance of elegance and practicality, ensuring a relaxing and memorable stay by the coast. The first floor accommodates all six beautifully appointed bedrooms along with the bathrooms, creating a peaceful and private sleeping area where guests can unwind after a day of exploration.
On the ground floor, Fairwinds continues to impress with a spacious lounge is a standout feature, boasting stunning sea views and a relaxed atmosphere perfect for socialising or quiet evenings in. From here, guests have direct access to the large garden, an inviting outdoor space ideal for children to play or for enjoying the fresh coastal air. There is also an additional convenient shower room, ideal for returning from the beach or coastal walks. A separate dining room provides an excellent setting for shared meals and special occasions, while the well-equipped kitchen includes everything needed to make your stay as comfortable and effortless as possible. Whether preparing a relaxed family breakfast or hosting a leisurely dinner, the kitchen has been designed with convenience in mind. After a busy day exploring the Roseland Peninsula, guests can truly unwind by sinking into the hot tub under the stars, enjoying peaceful evenings in a serene coastal setting.
The owners are happy to accept one well-behaved dog, making Fairwinds a wonderful option for guests travelling with a canine companion. St Mawes is a notably dog-friendly destination, with many local pubs, cafés, restaurants, and shops welcoming dogs. Coastal paths, countryside trails, and nearby beaches offer endless opportunities for scenic walks, ensuring every member of the family can enjoy the holiday.
St Mawes itself is a charming coastal village located within an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty on the Roseland Peninsula. It is particularly popular with families, nature lovers, walkers, and water enthusiasts, thanks to its unspoilt landscapes and crystal-clear waters. Within easy walking distance are two lovely sandy beaches, Summers Beach and Tavern Beach, both ideal for families with safe swimming, rockpools to explore, and picturesque harbour views.
Just over five miles away are the long sandy beaches of Towan and Pendower, known for their wide-open spaces, excellent swimming conditions, and convenient parking. Water sports enthusiasts can also enjoy boating, paddleboarding, kayaking, and sailing in the sheltered waters of the Carrick Roads.
St Mawes offers plenty to explore, from ferry trips across the water to Falmouth to scenic sightseeing boat tours along the coastline. History lovers will enjoy visiting the impressive St Mawes Castle, one of Henry VIII’s best-preserved coastal fortresses, while the village’s independent shops, galleries, cafés, and restaurants provide a relaxed and welcoming atmosphere. For a memorable day out, take the King Harry Ferry to Feock, Falmouth, or continue on to the city of Truro, where cobbled streets, a striking Gothic-style cathedral, and guided walking tours reveal the city’s rich and fascinating history.

long_description:
Enjoying uninterrupted views of the award-winning Mawgan Porth beach, this fantastic beach house is surrounded by a third of an acre of beautifully kept gardens with a large, sea facing, sun trap decking area, overlooking gently sloping lawns and a pretty stream that trickles down to the sea below. Solar panels help heat the house and water while providing free electrical car charging for our guests’ electric vehicle.
Over the past year (2022), the house has been renovated to the highest standards by one of the country’s leading interior designers and offers plenty of living space all benefitting from exceptional sea views and floor to ceiling sliding doors leading to a large decking area. The large circular fireplace makes for cosy evenings during the Autumn and Winter months. The brand-new handmade kitchen is well supplied with all creature comforts from a juicer to a selection of coffee machines, including a Nespresso. A door leads into a separate TV room with a big corner sofa, both with fabulous sea views and door to the terrace. Three ground floor bedrooms, ome with chandelier, two with those stunning views. A beautiful glass and oak staircase leads from the entrance hall up to the first floor where you will find three more bedrooms; a double bedroom with en-suite shower room; a large twin bedroom with large en-suite shower room, and one with a TV and sofa bed which enjoys the best views of all.
The beach is just a 5-minute walk away from the garden gate. Off the drive, there is a lawned area and to the side of the house a heated outdoor shower for when you return from the beach. The equipment store has a range of children’s wetsuits and storage for boards. Once cleaned off, you can luxuriate in the state-of-the-art Aspen and Spruce spa with a sauna, experiential shower plus cold water bucket for the brave. Situated mid-way between Padstow and Newquay, Mawgan Porth offers you a beautiful west facing beach, stunning scenery, wondrous walks, superb surfing, an amazing variety of restaurants to suit everyone’s taste and pocket, including a cosy pub, seafood restaurant, cafés, and takeaways all within walking distance of Blue Seas. Beach less than a 5 minute walk.

Belper is a charming market town offering a mix of independent shops, cafés, and traditional pubs. Take a leisurely stroll along the River Derwent or explore the town’s industrial heritage at the North Mill and Belper Mill. Nature lovers will appreciate the town’s proximity to the Peak District National Park, with numerous walking and hiking opportunities. The nearby Chevin Hill provides panoramic views of Belper and the surrounding countryside, perfect for a scenic walk or hike. Belper’s excellent train connections make it easy to visit nearby cities such as Derby and Nottingham, both offering a variety of shopping, dining, and cultural experiences. Matlock Bath, just a short drive away, is a picturesque village known for its Victorian charm and hot springs, while Matlock offers additional attractions like the Heights of Abraham and Gulliver’s Kingdom theme park.
Whether you’re seeking outdoor adventure, cultural exploration, or simply a peaceful retreat, Chevin View’s central location provides easy access to all that Belper, and the surrounding area have to offer. From scenic walks to nearby towns and attractions, there’s something for everyone to enjoy. Please note: This property does not accept stag parties, and the house is located in a residential area so respect to neighbours is required.

long_description:
An ideal holiday retreat for larger families or groups, offering plenty of space to relax, unwind and enjoy quality time together. Set amidst the breathtaking beauty of Exmoor, the property boasts stunning views across the surrounding countryside, providing a peaceful and picturesque setting for your stay.

Timed oil central heating, gas, electricity, bed linen, towels and Starlink 40 Wi-Fi included. Initial logs for wood burner included. Travel cot and highchair available on request. Lawned raised terrace garden with sitting-out area, garden furniture and barbecue. 10-acre natural grounds (shared with owner, restrictions apply at certain times of year). Hot tub for 8 (private). Stabling available. Private parking for 4 cars. No smoking. Please note: The property has a natural water supply from a spring and there is a fenced pond in the grounds, 150 yards away. Fireworks and drones are not allowed in the garden or grounds of this property due to livestock.

Brambley Meadow is set at the foot of Exmoor as it rises from the stunning coastline, in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty with origins dating back to the Magna Carta, and offers families or a group of friends the ideal place to escape to for a countryside holiday, or somewhere to spend the weekend celebrating a special occasion. There is a lot of living space for everyone to enjoy in the house. Outside the farmhouse is a large patio area ideal for a morning coffee or a soak in the hot tub after a day at the beach.
Spend your days exploring the spectacular landscapes, charming villages and attractions of Exmoor, then return home to relax and soak away the day in the private hot tub while taking in the beautiful views. The perfect base for discovering Exmoor and creating unforgettable memories together.
Guest are invited to explore the farm and meet the animals who call it home. There are 10 acres of fields and natural landscape to enjoy and great walks directly from the cottage into the surrounding countryside.
The seaside village of Combe Martin is nearby. As well as good local amenities, the beach is great for rock pooling at low tide or for hiring a kayak and exploring the coastline. Ilfracombe, just around the corner, has a wider range of amenities and a bustling harbour at its centre.
There are numerous attractions within easy reach of the properties including the Combe Martin Wildlife and Dinosaur Park, Watermouth Castle and the Lynton to Lynmouth cliff railway. At Croyde and Woolacombe you will find some of the best and cleanest surf beaches in the country, as well as many smaller coves and bays. Exmoor is a short distance away and on a clear day, the views can be spectacular. There are National Trust properties at Arlington and Knightshayes and the RHS Gardens at Rosemoor, Great Torrington. You really are surrounded by the best Devon has to offer. Beach 5 miles. Shop, pub and restaurant 2 miles.

reviews.comment: very rural location with beautiful views, single track roads to get to property. Our grandchildren loved being able to feed the horses and visiting the ducks and chickens. Really big table outside which we were lucky enough with the weather to have a few meals outside to enjoy the views from the patio.Some of the pictures are inaccurate, the dining table is no longer in the kitchen /living space enjoying the great view, but down 7 steps to another room. In its place is a pool table which was very much enjoyed by everyone. Lots of different sitting areas all with tv's but no nintendo or CD player(as suggested in the listing).The owners were very responsive to any requests.We loved the hot tub with its great views.The beams into the upper bedrooms are low. A great place to be with our family

Thought it needed a bit of a clean on arrival. Thought liquid hand soap would be a basic requirement to be left for visitors on hygiene grounds so had to nip out to get some. Promised welcome pack, as described in details, never arrived. Husband hit his head on low beams ( he was warned !). Needed to wash his pillow case as a result and was very disappointed with the stained pillow protectors. The snooker table was enjoyed by the youngsters but there was no outdoor area for them to play games, completely gravelled. We enjoyed the hot tub and the area.

Good isolated location which is what we wanted. However we were disappointed with the interior. It clearly needs some renovation. That aside it hadn't been properly cleaned when we arrived, there were crumbs on the table and floor. The furniture was somewhat dilapidated with splits in the leather. There were cobwebs in some of the corners. Some crockery was badly chipped. Our children were looking forward to the working farm. There isn't one! The photos in the advertising literature give a rosy view of the interior which disappoints when you actually see it for real.

long_description:
The Loft is the ultimate choice for large family gatherings or group outings, offering a tranquil setting on a small holiday cottage complex surrounded by paddocks and woodland. With ample space and impressive features, this detached accommodation is designed for comfort and relaxation. The first floor boasts an open-plan living area with bi-folding doors leading to a balcony overlooking the picturesque countryside. The contemporary and well-equipped kitchen is thoughtfully planned for catering to larger groups. Spread across both floors, the bedrooms all feature en-suite facilities.
The Loft comes complete with two private hot tubs and access to shared on-site facilities, including a games room. The Loft will soon enjoy a private TV lounge and games room facility which is currently under development and expected to be completed by Aug/Sept 2026. Enjoy a private, enclosed, lawned garden and take advantage of the shared 2-acre paddock for exercising dogs. Additionally, explore 10 acres of unspoiled shared grounds, ideal for picnics and outdoor activities. Located 4 miles away, Brandesburton village provides a general store, fish and chip shop, pizzeria, and a choice of pubs.
Hainsworth Park Golf Club is nearby, welcoming visitors for pay-as-you-go golf, and there are facilities for fishing, clay shooting, and jet skiing. A short drive takes you to the coastal resorts of Hornsea, Bridlington, and Filey, each offering miles of sandy beaches, colourful promenades, and a variety of inns and tearooms. Bird lovers can visit Hornsea Mere and RSPB Bempton, while the charming market town of Beverley boasts a 13th-century minster and a renowned racecourse. Explore stately homes and halls at Burton Constable, Sewerby, Burton Agnes, and Sledmere. For outdoor enthusiasts, walking and cycling tracks surround The Loft, providing easy access to the scenic Yorkshire Wolds that inspired the famous Hockney paintings.
The property can be booked together with other accommodations on the complex to accommodate larger groups, making it the perfect base for unforgettable gatherings.

long_description:
Kilburn House is a large Victorian town house just a short stroll from the centre of Bridlington on the beautiful North Yorkshire coastline. Once known as a popular bed and breakfast, it has once again been transformed into a very welcoming home. With private hot tub, spacious social areas and two private courtyards, this holiday home is perfect for large family groups to come together and celebrate whilst enjoying this vibrant harbour town.
The spacious open plan living/dining area offers a large bay window which floods the room with natural light. Huge sofas, handmade for the property, offer plenty of seating and are ideally placed to enjoy a family night in front of the 65” Smart TV, whilst the bespoke dining table can accommodate the whole group, whether that be for a hearty breakfast before heading out for the day or for coming together to enjoy a delicious home cooked evening meal. This holiday home also offers a café room with bar; just perfect for a social cuppa before heading out for the day. The chef in the group will be delighted with the kitchen which offers a host of appliances including a huge range, triple slow cooker, and a large grill. There is a separate utility room with fridge/freezer, washing machine and dryer. A cosy ‘quiet’ room sits to the back of the house and here you can relax in one of two armchairs to read a book or enjoy one of the board games provided. A second sitting room offers more seating and access out to one of two private courtyards. This offers a private seven-seater hot tub and additional seating. Enjoy a soak surrounded by bubbles in the mid-day sun or enjoy a spot of star gazing with your friends on an evening. Kilburn House offers two ground floor bedrooms, one of which has en-suite shower facilities, for those who can’t manage the stairs. Access to the second courtyard is via the café’ room. This outside area offers a covered seating area should the weather be a little inclement.
This fabulous holiday home offers nine further bedrooms spread over two floors, the majority of which have en suite bathrooms. There is a mixture of double, super king-size zip and link and a bunk room, and all of them are beautifully presented with Freeview TV’s. The deep filled mattresses and cosy soft furnishings will guarantee a great night’s sleep after a busy day. A bonus too are the six private car park spaces – two to the front and four to the rear of the property.
On the doorstep is a plethora of tea rooms, restaurants, amusements and convenience stores. Bridlington also offers two beautiful sandy beaches, a promenade for relaxing seafront walks and a thriving spa and theatre offering a packed events programme throughout the summer months. Sewerby Hall and Gardens, Burton Agnes Hall and Sledmere House and Gardens are all within a short drive of the property, and a little further along the coast is Filey and the pretty village of Flamborough with its working lighthouse. For bird watchers, a visit to RSPB Bempton Cliffs is a must. With miles of walking and cycling routes do not forget to bring your bikes. With a choice of golf courses and miles of walking and cycling opportunities on the Yorkshire Wolds and along the Flamborough Heritage Coast there is something for everyone. Whether you are staying to celebrate a special occasion or to just enjoy spending time with friends and family, make Kilburn House the base for your Bridlington holiday.

reviews.comment: A last minute change to here due to the property we booked having a boiler issue. The lady at Cottages.com couldn’t have been more helpful and Sandra who manages the property and wasn’t expecting anyone that week rallied the team and made sure everything was perfect and welcoming for us. Just a short walk from the beach and plenty for children to do there along with Sandra’s knowledge of places to eat made it a fantastic base for the week and easy to travel to other places each day. The home comforts at the property and the amount of en-suite shower rooms meant it was more than enough for our party of 9. Thank you Leah at Cottages.com and Sandra and her team for making this a memorable holiday for us all.

So much space!! Lots of ensuite bedrooms and plenty of living space. The hot tub was great and all set up. Location just a short walk from a lovely sandy beach. Owners very friendly and quick to help. We had a lovely family break. The car spaces were a real bonus.

We had 14 family members stay here for my daughters 21st birthday. The location is great, the size of the property was great. I have deducted a star as there was a couple a niggly things that could be improved. Firstly, you get 1 big bunch if keyes with no indication what each key is for, it took a while for us to work out. Only 1 set of keys, so if we went out separately we had to plan to meet up if anyone wanted to go back. The  next thing is, it is advertised as pet friendly, but what you are not told prior to booking / arriving is that pets are not allowed on the furniture at all, and cannot be left unsupervised. Personally I dont consider this to be pet friendly, when you have a pet that goes on the sofa at home, it is very difficult to keep them off the furniture, making the whole trip quite stressful. Finally, the fire alarm went off on Saturday night, the housekeeper came and checked the property, it was unclear what set this off and it was put down to my daughter using a hair dryer so we were asked not to use a hair dryer in that room, I thought it was a little strange that a hair dryer would do that. You are also asked to strip beds before leaving, not something i expect to have to do when on holiday, Ultimately we did have a great time, but I do think some improvements could be made.

long_description:
With so much space, The Dower House is ideal for large families and groups of friends wishing to holiday together. It is an impressive and spacious Grade II listed, detached farmhouse with large lawned gardens and its very own hot tub. This well-appointed property offers a games room with a table tennis table and table football, and guests can also enjoy shared use of the owner’s hard tennis court.
The Dower House is set in countryside, with a network of quiet lanes offering good walking and cycling from the door. There is much of interest locally, including the highly acclaimed Church Farm Stow Bardolph Rare Breeds Centre with its petting animals, adventure playground, tea room and shop. Stow Hall Gardens provide an opportunity to walk around beautiful gardens and enjoy tea with homemade cakes, whilst Denver Windmill serves excellent beverages, homemade cakes, and light lunches. There is also a pay and play golf course and Welney Wildfowl Trust wetland paradise brimming with nature. You can also enjoy easy access to the lovely sandy beaches, and RSPB nature and bird reserves along the North Norfolk Coast. The local pub is just 100 yards away.
The market town of Downham Market, 2 miles, has Friday and Saturday markets, a supermarket, shops, bank, restaurants and boasts a direct rail link to Ely, Cambridge and London (in an hour and twenty minutes). The medieval town of Kings Lynn, 10 miles, is complete with handsome waterfront offering an array of good shops, inns, restaurants, a theatre, cinema, bowling alley and a sports centre. Both west and north Norfolk have an expanse of sandy beaches and salt marshes along the coastline, as well as nature reserves to protect the birds and plants which thrive here. The coastal road passes through many pretty rural villages, with popular tea rooms serving wonderful local food.
For those who enjoy a visit to the beach whilst on holiday, Snettisham Beach is the closest at 30 minutes’ drive. Further along the coast road are the traditional seaside resorts of Hunstanton and Heacham, which boast beaches and an array of traditional seaside activities and attractions for all ages. Hunstanton, 24 miles, has a pier with lively seasonal entertainment, a Sea Life Centre and cliff-top golf course. Heacham, 22 miles, is home to Norfolk Lavender and visitors may participate in guided tours of the expanse of lavender fields to observe the harvesting. Sandringham Estate,- the Queen’s country residence, with its Jacobean-style house, museum, superb gardens and park, are open to the public when the Royal Family is not in residence. To the south lies Ely Cathedral, known as the Ship of the Fens. This small city has an excellent Saturday market and a good variety of gift shops, as well as a pretty waterfront and boat hire.
The historic city of Cambridge is easily accessible for the day, and well worth a visit. One of the nicest ways to explore the city is by punt, which meanders through the city and passes many of the stunning university grounds. There are also many shops, pubs, restaurants, and theatres. Norwich, famous for its cathedral, is also within easy reach, and not to be missed. Don’t miss the famous mustard shop there as well, with many new and old varieties of mustard that can be purchased. We are opposie the award winning pub The Hare Arms/ this is a delightful village pub with great food and superb beer, booking is recommended for large groups to eat. Beach 21 miles. Shops 2 miles and pub 100 yards.

Gas central heating (underfloor on ground floor), electricity, bed linen, towels and Wi-Fi included. Initial logs for wood burner included. Welcome pack. Table football and football goals. Games room with pool table, dartboard and table football (shared). Catering available by direct arrangement with owner (at cost). Large meadow to front. Please note: There are 2 steps in the garden. Children are not permitted in the hot tub, for Health and safety purposes. This property has a security deposit of £500.

The Barn (UK31813) is a converted barn for up to six people provides excellent accommodation for families and friends who are looking to enjoy a break and get away from it all. The house has a large meadow outside, perfect for a game of football, plus your enclosed garden with a hot tub at the back. Inside, it has been decorated and equipped to a very high standard. It has two king size bedrooms, one with an en-suite and there is also a family bathroom, a wonderful well-equipped kitchen, a spacious living and dining room with large TV. There is a comfortable sofa bed in the living room which is suitable for two adults.
Farmhouse (UKC1891) which has six bedrooms, three with en-suite facilities, two lovely reception rooms, a wonderful well-equipped kitchen, a spacious dining room with large TV, and a fantastic bright family room with stunning floor-to-ceiling doors that overlook the garden.
To make your stay that bit more special, the owners offer an in-house dining experience. Perhaps treat yourself and arrange the chef to come and cook you a delicious meal? The experience can be tailored to suit your needs, please arrange this direct with the owner. If you are not dining al fresco in the garden or in the hot tub relaxing, then there is a wealth of attractions for families to enjoy.
Within an easy drive is Longleat House and Safari Park a great day out for all. Guests can also spend some time at Stourhead House and Gardens and heading just to the other side of the abbey town of Sherborne, a favourite with everyone is the Yeovilton Fleet Air Arm Museum, with its feature aircraft carrier deck. For lovers of vintage classic cars of a bygone day, then the Haynes Motor Museum is well worth a visit to see an array of superb classic car collections. Further inland into south Somerset, you can spend days out taking in the ever-popular Clarks Factory Village, Glastonbury and on to Cheddar Gorge and Caves. Wander into the quaint town of Shaftesbury with its famous Gold Hill, Sherborne with its wonderful shops and abbeys, or go south towards Dorchester the county town, Weymouth with its award-winning beach and seaside atmosphere and the famous Jurassic Coast World Heritage Site. There are country walks locally, beautiful scenery, village pubs to wine and dine in, golf and many historic houses in the area, and on your return, relax and unwind in the hot tub, have a barbecue or amble down to the nearby village pub. Shop ½ mile, pub and restaurant 1 mile.
These properties can be booked together to accommodate 22 guests.

long_description:
The spacious Grade II listed Brookbank Farm is set in the rolling Cheshire countryside. Sleeping up to eighteen guests in seven bedrooms with seven bathrooms, this superb house is perfect for family getaways, group holidays and celebration weekends. Due to the age of the property, you’ll find low doorways, beams and uneven stairs, however, it offers wonderful natural character set out over three floors, and although large is beautifully traditional.
As soon as you step inside you’ll find original oak doors and heavily beamed walls and ceilings. The kitchen boasts an oiled fired Aga (switched off Jun–Sep) and a wood burner is set pride of place within an inglenook fireplace in the cosy living room. Outside in the enclosed rear garden is a hot tub positioned under a timber-framed veranda. From the front lawn, far reaching views stretch over the Jodrell Bank Observatory, which is within easy walking distance. Finally, Brookbank Farm also has four of its own fishing lakes shared with the local angling club, so day tickets can be arranged.
Situated in stunning surroundings, the location of the farmhouse is perfect for those who love the outdoors, and for exploring the beautiful Cheshire countryside. You only have to step outside to find numerous walking routes and if you prefer, there are also some fantastic cycle paths with some of the best cycling in the country found on the Cheshire Cycleway. If you fancy a drink the nearest pub is just a 15-minute walk away and the friendly owners can suggest a range of activities to book, including boot camps, spa treatments, catering and cocktail making classes (charges apply). Pub and restaurant 1 mile.
Please note: There are open, steep, spiral or narrow stairs at the property.

long_description:
Sitting pretty in the outskirts of the small North Norfolk village of Swanton Novers, Bell House and the Stables at Bell House have everything you need for the perfect getaway whether you are seeking something large and impressive or something small and perfectly formed. Formerly an inn, imposing Bell House would be best described as a manor house property and accommodates up to twelve guests in six bedrooms and boasts an impressive three bathrooms, one of which has a spa bath. This makes this a great escape for couples travelling together, two or three families wanting to relax with company or indeed three generations planning an escape to remember. There is much to love about this house, not least of all the Jacuzzi in the private garden, which is the largest one available and offers somewhere special to relax. With a small snug, which has the TV in it and a large sitting room, with quirky bespoke made metal elephant heads on the wall, this impressive property also has a formal dining room, which is perfect to gather around and raise a toast to old memories while making new ones. The outside is just as special with two and a half acres of private land featuring a small orchard, a wild flower garden, croquet, boules and other outside games. This has been the owner’s much-loved family home and it shows. It is lived-in luxury, which means that everything is set up for a comfortable and enjoyable stay.
Set within the grounds but still enjoying a degree of privacy, The Stables at Bell House is a brand-new renovation, created by the owners and, like Bell House, it offers feature beds. Sleeping four, both the bedrooms are en-suite and one even has a spa bath. It also offers open-plan living and outside you will find an Indian sandstone patio. In fact, you can be sure that no expense has been spared to make this the perfect escape for two couples of a small family. You will be tempted to stay on-site, socialise or relax and unwind but should you venture out you will find yourself within easy reach of the stunning Norfolk Coastline, the famous Norfolk Broads and the fine city of Norwich and so much history and wildlife too. So, a perfect location and great properties. Good choice. Now enjoy!
The Stables at Bell House (UK41789) and Bell House (UK41790) can be booked together to accommodate up to 16 guests.

long_description:
Bridlington Old Town House offers a wonderfully quirky base from which to explore one of Yorkshire’s most charming coastal towns. This large, historic property retains an abundance of period character, with stone floors, wood panelling, and even its own original pub bar – guests can ring the bell to order food and drinks from the neighbouring pub, a truly unique feature! The house includes eight en suite bedrooms, a roof terrace with hot tub, spacious living areas with the kitchen and dining area on the 2nd floor! Parking for three cars. Three dogs are also welcome, making it ideal for group stays.
Nestled in the heart of Bridlington’s Old Town, this location captures the essence of old-world Yorkshire charm. The cobbled streets are lined with Georgian and Victorian architecture, independent shops, and cosy tea rooms, creating a delightful step back in time. Visitors can enjoy the town’s many annual festivals celebrating food, art, and heritage. Just a short drive to two award-winning beaches, offering everything from classic seaside fun to peaceful coastal walks. Bridlington Spa hosts concerts and theatre performances year-round, while nature lovers can head to the nearby RSPB Bempton Cliffs to spot puffins and gannets. Sewerby Hall and Gardens offer family-friendly attractions and sea views, and golfers will find excellent courses dotted across the Yorkshire Wolds. Whether you’re exploring the dramatic cliffs of Flamborough Head or relaxing in a seaside café, Bridlington blends history, culture, and coastal beauty – the perfect destination for a memorable group getaway.

reviews.comment: Absolutely perfect.Nothing could be improved.Will definitely be back, and recommending to everyone

This is a unique property with lots of positives and a great deal of potential. The 8 ensuite rooms are all of a good size and meant that everyone in our large group were able to have their own space.  The upstairs kitchen and lounge was decorated well and was a good place to come together and relax. The downstairs bar area and outside courtyards are also good features with plenty of space. We didn't use the hot tub but it looked clean and well-kept. As the property is adjacent to the pub, it can be quite loud in some of the rooms in the evening. This wasn't too much of a problem for us as the music stopped around 11 but it would be something to consider if you have small children.The communication with the property wasn't great and we we didn't receive the code for the front door by the allocated check-in time. I tried the number on the booking information email a couple of times but wasn't able to get hold of anyone, despite leaving a message. Thankfully the staff in the pub were very helpful and helped us to gain access.All the rooms had towels, bedding and a TV. However, some of the rooms hadn't been cleaned very thoroughly when we arrived, particularly the ensuite shower/ bathrooms. The property has a good-sized range oven and a fridge freezer. There are lots of plates and cups but not really enough cooking pots and pans for a large group. Thankfully the pub staff came to our rescue again and were able to loan us what we needed. Thanks guys! There is no dishwasher or washing machine in the property...there is however a nice, reasonably priced laundrette about a 15 minute walk away. The property is located in the 'old town' area of Bridlington, about a 25 minute walk from the town and sea front. There are lots of pubs and a couple of decent cafes close to the property and we had a good time walking around and exploring! It was a good springboard to enable us to explore the wider area.

Amazing property. Very quirky old style pub with the bar features. Bedrooms were spacious and clean… on suite in everyone. Towels in every room. Upstairs kitchen was clean and spacious too. We were lucky to come when brilliant weather too so could enjoy the roof terrace and the undercover outside area. The pub next door had music on til late but that didn’t bother us as we were all up late. The hot tub was clean and ready for use.  Definitely would go again!!
