long_description: This superb wing of Grade II listed Islington Hall, which is adjacent to the owner’s home, has been refurbished for 2018 and benefits from a large garden and a private hot tub to sit back and relax in after a day spent exploring the area. There is plenty for all the family to see and do, from Her Majesty’s country retreat at Sandringham, 20 minutes by car, and the sandy beaches of Heacham and Hunstanton to the medieval town of King’s Lynn, which is just a short drive away. Hunstanton is a traditional seaside resort and offers good days out for all the family, as does Heacham, which has been a seaside resort for over 150 years. For children there is Church Farm, 10 miles south of King’s Lynn, where you can meet the animals and enjoy refreshment in the farm café/restaurant. Snettisham is great for spotting the birdlife that inhabits this stretch of the Norfolk coastline and you can often see thousands of wading birds in the spring, or sit and watch the birds on the lagoon islands. Beach 17 miles. Nearby there is horse-riding, golf, fishing and roller skating. Shop, pub and restaurant 3 miles.

long_description:
Grey Gables is a grand and imposing Victorian vicarage, perfect for large family gatherings and celebrations, set in the historic hamlet of Old Quarrington, offering luxurious accommodations and easy access to Durham’s attractions.

Welcome to Grey Gables, an imposing and grand old vicarage dating back to 1870, nestled in the historic hamlet of Old Quarrington, once the capital of medieval Queringdonshire. This magnificent property provides the perfect setting for large family gatherings and celebrations with friends, offering a unique blend of Victorian charm and modern amenities.
As you approach Grey Gables up the sweeping gravel driveway, take a moment to appreciate the grandeur of this impressive building. Inside, the ground floor welcomes you with a large living room featuring sumptuous sofas, a cosy and intimate room for relaxation. The spacious kitchen is well-equipped with everything you need to create family feasts, complete with a dining table for casual meals and a separate dining room for larger group events. A games room with a pool table provides entertainment for all ages, while a utility room and boot room add practicality to your stay. Upstairs on the first floor, three beautifully furnished bedrooms await, three doubles and a super king bedroom, with its own walk-in wardrobe, each exquisitely decorated with chandeliers hanging from the vast high ceilings. The expansive bathroom offers both a freestanding bath and a large walk-in shower, as well as his and her sinks for added convenience. Ascending to the second floor, you’ll discover a surprise, a spacious hallway transformed into an incredible spaceship-themed games room, complete with a gaming console and a sofa. This is a top floor is sure to inspire the imagination of younger family members. There are also two double bedrooms with themed murals, one with a Marvel superhero theme and the other featuring a Formula 1 racing car, and a single bedroom with a feminine, pink theme. A bathroom completes this floor.
Outside Grey Gables boasts a hot tub that accommodates six people and a huge 2-acre garden ideal for outdoor activities and enjoying the beautiful surroundings. The owners also provide stabling for horses by prior arrangement and for a small cost, should you want to bring your own horse with you. Nearby, walking trails and cycle paths offer opportunities to explore the countryside, while the vibrant city of Durham is just 5 miles away. Durham itself is a city rich in history and culture. Visitors can explore Durham Castle and Cathedral, both UNESCO World Heritage sites, offering breathtaking architecture and stunning views of the city and river. The Cathedral is renowned for its Romanesque architecture and the Shrine of St Cuthbert, making it a must-visit for history enthusiasts.
In summary, Grey Gables offers not only a historic stay in a grand Victorian vicarage but also a gateway to exploring the rich history and cultural heritage of County Durham. Whether you’re planning a family reunion, celebrating a special occasion, or simply enjoying a break with friends, Grey Gables promises an unforgettable experience in Old Quarrington. Please note dogs are to be kept downstairs in the large kitchen and boot room.

long_description:
Nestled in the shadow of Holme Moss on the northern edge of the Peak District National Park, this high-quality listed cottage offers stunning panoramic views over the surrounding scenic Holme Valley. What was once three terraced weavers’ cottages, has been completely renovated to one spacious, luxury holiday cottage boasting seven en-suite bedrooms.
Once inside you’ll find unique features that reflect the age of the property have been wonderfully blended with modern day touches. The wood burner for instance is complemented by underfloor heating on the ground floor, a claw foot bath has been paired with walk-in showers and one bedroom even including an award winning king size study bed as featured on George Clarke’s amazing spaces. Once outside the views are simply unrivalled. Pride of place in the garden you’ll find a hot tub giving you ample opportunity to sit back, relax and enjoy the rolling countryside away from the hustle and bustle of everyday life.
Goosander Cottage is around ½ mile from Holme village where you’ll find a cosy pub serving food and being set in the rolling hills of the Peak District there are walks straight from the door. Keen cyclists can also recreate routes from the Tour de France 2014 including the iconic Holme Moss which is literally a stone’s throw away. Holmfirth is around 3 miles from the cottage, and anyone familiar with the TV comedy ’Last of the Summer Wine’ may recognise the area as the backdrop from this. In Holmfirth you’ll find a wide selection of cafés, bars, pubs and restaurants to suit the majority of tastes, together with a century old picture house and live music venue, and also a vineyard. Huddersfield is around 8 miles away and home to the UK’s first eco-spa, and a whole host of Peak District towns, villages and attractions are within easy reach to explore.

reviews.comment: The property was a little small for our party. We are not massive 6ft 3, the biggest and not overweight, but the bedrooms were very small and this was highlighted by the showers which were so small as to make them almost unusable, there were no shelved in them and it was very hard to bend down without banging the glass. The living areas were nice but cramped for our party of 11. The views outside were beautiful and it was lovely in the hot tub looking out into the countryside, however we had a toddler with us and there was a8ft plus drop from the property into the field below which was a bit dodgy and also the patio was stoned which was a bit uncomfy on the feet. A nice pub about a hundred yards down the road, and the hosts were very accommodating, but it just seemed a bit overpriced for the size to me

The cottage is in a beautiful rural setting, very peaceful and quiet with a wonderful pub just a few minutes walk away.It is well appointed with everything you may need, home from home, except for a few fundamental things that are missing, hence only leaving 4 stars.There is a washing machine, (great) but only a tiny airer to dry clothes. For a properly that can accommodate 15 people, the airer was totally inappropriate. There isn’t a washing line or rotary line outside either. I ended up buying 2 airers locally just so we could get the washing hung up to dry.Outside the hot tub was well used, but the outside furniture was not very comfortable to sit on for any length of time (sitting on metal chairs with no cushions). The outside furniture didn’t match the ones shown in the photographs, much less inspiring to sit on. We were lucky in that we had 2 glorious weeks of sunshine, but there was no shade. No outdoor umbrella, so even if we had wanted to sit outside and enjoy the view for any length of time, we couldn’t. I get that the back is open, I’m sure it can be windy, but an umbrella and a note to say if it’s damaged it comes out of your security deposit, would surely suffice.We would certainly go back.

Lovely cottage with everything you could need for a short break with friends. Some lovely extra touches with the named ducks, Molton Brown products, robes and slippers and a fabulous hamper of fruit. The house is immaculately clean with comfortable beds and modern en-suites in every bedroom . The location is perfect for walks right from the door, a short stroll to the local pub and just a few minutes drive from Holmfirth. Highly recommended.

long_description:
This fabulous large barn conversion, nestled on the edge of the gorgeous Peak District National Park, offers beautiful scenery on the doorstep as well as several excellent pubs and restaurants nearby. Accommodating up to 14 guests, this lovely barn conversion makes a perfect base for family get-togethers. A hot tub is available by arrangement (with a recommended company, at cost). Its thoughtfully decorated interior and comfy seating area make it the perfect getaway for groups, families and friends looking for that ideal retreat. Beautifully furnished to provide spacious accommodation, Valley View Barn has fabulous features, with oak beams, stone walls and a wonderful open plan living area.
You will find an abundance of walks from the door of this detached barn, as well as a fabulous selection of pretty villages, market towns and visitor attractions. Take a drive to nearby Ashbourne, visit Carsington Water, or even spend a day at Alton Towers. Dovedale and Ilam Estate are only a 5-minute drive from the property, and they offer guests the chance to walk around stunning countryside, explore caves, limestone hillsides and stroll alongside the River Dove to reach Milldale.
The cottage is located on the Tissington Trail and is perfectly situated to cycle directly from your doorstep and take in the breathtaking scenery around the cottage! Chatsworth Estate, Haddon Hall and Bakewell are only a 25-minute drive from Valley View Barn and therefore the location is the perfect place to explore the Peak National Park. Located half a mile from Bradbourne, the village stands high on a ridge between the valleys of Bradbourne Brook and Havenhill. Just a few miles up the road, the famous Peaks village of Tissington makes a wonderful afternoon out. Famous for its well dressings, Tissington invites everyone to come along and soak up the atmosphere of this pretty village, complete with duck pond, church, tea rooms and an impressive old hall.
The market town of Ashbourne has all the amenities you may require, as well as a variety of walks, climbing opportunities and cycle routes. Golf can also be found nearby. After a busy day exploring, what better place to relax in than the beautiful Valley View Barn? Shop, pub and restaurant 2 miles.

long_description:
Situated along a private road, this Victorian home was formerly the summer residence of the Countess Cowley, a member of Queen Victoria’s entourage. Located to maximise the sea views it is set within a beautiful 9-acre estate surrounded by woodland and the coast. Here you can enjoy the peaceful surroundings - and you may even spot one of the island’s famous red squirrels. Bodwen has been designed with large families and groups in mind with carefully co-ordinated interiors and contemporary furnishings. The property also has the added bonus of an outdoor tap, perfect for washing off walking boots and bikes.
A children’s playground has been created, complete with a dragon tunnel, walk-the-plank, hopscotch, picnic area, swings and much more. Both adults and children are able to make use of the sports equipment available, such as cricket, badminton, croquet and boules sets, along with football. On the front terrace, which looks onto the lawn and the Solent, you can enjoy lazing on the rattan patio furniture and table. You will also find a patio on the beach, with an oak table and benches along with a BBQ area; a perfect shady spot for reading, relaxing and watching the kids on the beach. A Scandinavian, 7ft cedar, wood-fired hot tub is the ideal place to lie back and watch the stars.
The Victorian fountain in the grounds has been beautifully restored and looks amazing, especially at night, giving you the feel of driving into a stately home.
Just 4 miles away is the seaside town of Ryde with its good selection of individual shops, restaurants, bars, tea shops and large sandy beach. There is also an abundance of attractions to visit which include the Isle of Wight steam railway and Museum of Havenstreet, 3¼ miles. Osborne House, which was a former royal residence that was built for Queen Victoria and Prince Albert as a summer home and rural retreat, 4¾ miles. Robin Hill Country Park offers exciting rides and adventure play all set in beautiful rolling down land and forest, 4½ miles. Also worth a visit is Amazon World, an educational and conservation centre offering over 200 animal species and rain forest plants, 7½ miles. Calbourne Water Mill, 11 miles, the only working water mill on the Isle of Wight and also features a small war museum, rural exhibits and a café. The island is also a walker’s paradise, filled with over 500 miles of footpaths across contrasting landscapes and beaches. Outdoor pursuits include walking, cycling, riding, sailing and fishing. Private beach 200 yards. Shop, pub and restaurant 1 mile.
Bodwen can be booked together with Bodwen Corner Cottage to accommodate up to 20 guests.

long_description:
Welcome to Robinswood House, your ideal holiday retreat for unforgettable family celebrations! This gated residency provides a spacious holiday home and offers accommodation for up to fourteen guests in six bedrooms and a study. With a range of fantastic amenities both indoors and outdoors, this is the perfect destination for a large family gathering.
On the ground floor, you’ll find two bedrooms, one with twin beds and the other with a comfortable single bed, providing a peaceful night’s rest. There’s also a convenient cloakroom with a toilet. The study includes a sofa bed, perfect for additional guests. The living room comfortably accommodates all fourteen guests, and the adjacent sunroom is an ideal space for group dining. The modern kitchen is fully equipped with all the latest appliances and features a welcoming breakfast bar for relaxed mornings. Ascending to the first floor, you’ll discover four more bedrooms, including two double rooms and a double room with an additional single bed. The luxurious master bedroom boasts an en-suite shower room and a sumptuous king-size bed for your comfort. Additionally, a deluxe bathroom with an extra-large tub with shower overhead is located on this floor, ensuring relaxation and convenience for all. Outside there’s a large grassed area for garden games, perfect for keeping everyone entertained. A charming pergola with seating offers a delightful spot for outdoor gatherings, and the outdoor kitchen with a coal BBQ is ideal for grilling up delicious meals. Relax in the bubbling outdoor hot tub, creating unforgettable memories with your loved ones. A large outbuilding provides an excellent entertainment space. It features a bar, a cinema screen, and a pool table for hours of fun and relaxation.
Robinswood House is a truly exceptional holiday home, offering everything you need for a memorable family celebration. Whether you’re basking in the spacious indoor comfort or enjoying the stunning outdoor amenities, your stay here will be a cherished memory for years to come. Book your holiday getaway now and make this beautiful property your home away from home! Right on your doorstep is a local shop and pub, along with the much-loved Robinswood Hill Country Park, a firm favourite with kids and pooches, be sure to take a stroll to the top for the panoramic views as far as the eye can see.
Within 10 minutes you can be in the historic Gloucester Quays, a premier shopping destination with a mix of designer outlets, shops, restaurants, and bars. Cheltenham can be reached within a 20-minute car journey, with the world-famous Cheltenham racecourse only 10 miles away from Robinswood House. In addition to the attractions in Gloucester, there are some beautiful Cotswold villages and towns nearby that are worth exploring. Your nearest village is Painswick a picturesque village with charming streets, historic buildings, and beautiful Rococo Gardens. Bourton-on-the-Water is 30 30-minute drive, Bourton-on-the-Water is famous for its picturesque stone bridges that span the River Windrush. It is also home to attractions like the Model Village and the bird park.

long_description:
Nestled within the glorious Devon countryside, Barwick is the perfect choice for families, couples and friends wanting to escape the hustle and bustle of everyday life and enjoy a holiday together. Surrounded by some of the country’s most beautiful landscapes, with Dartmoor and the lovely rolling hills of Devon on your doorstep, Barwick is also within easy reach of the coast. This spacious property has the benefit of a large open plan living space downstairs and an additional sitting room upstairs, complete with a balcony so you can take in the glorious countryside views.
Barwick sits on the edge of the lovely village of Exbourne with an inn serving meals and local ales, an eco-friendly, underground shop, post office and historic church. Approximately 100 yards from the property, there is a lovely playpark for the children to enjoy. The local town has a cinema, supermarkets, castle, museum and a variety of restaurants. The property is just 6 miles from the breathtaking Dartmoor National Park, where you can see Dartmoor ponies, beautiful landscapes, quaint villages, castles, culture, and an altogether slower pace of life. You can settle down at a pub, or find an idyllic spot to enjoy a picnic whilst taking in the spectacular scenery. Meldon Reservoir is just 8 miles away and offers fishing, water sports and lovely lakeside walks. The pretty towns of Okehampton and Tavistock are close by, and there are also many beautiful gardens including RHS Rosemoor and The Lost Gardens of Heligan within easy reach. Devon and Cornwall offer fantastic coastal walking and boast sandy beaches and hidden coves, ideal for surfing or exploring the many rock pools. Fishing, tennis, horse riding, pony trekking and an 18-hole golf course are all close by. The Tarka Trail is one of the country’s longest, traffic-free, walking and cycling paths, and forms part of the Devon Coast to Coast cycle route. Beach 27 miles. Shop, pub and restaurant 350 yards.

long_description:
Situated in a quiet part of Cadeleigh, these beautiful, detached, barn conversions overlook the ponds and the deer with amazing views across the rolling hills of Devon. Set 100 yards apart within the owner’s 40-acre deer farm, nestled next to the ponds, the properties are accessed by an unmade track and provide beautiful, spacious accommodation. Perfect for friends to get together, celebrations or a family holiday.
The Otters (ref UKC3930) has been decorated and furnished to a good standard, each bedroom has en-suite facilities, and there is a spacious open plan living area with underfloor heating.
The Linhay (ref UKC1290) has a kitchen/dining room with large picture windows offering lovely views down the valley; the living room has a wood burner, ideal for those cosy nights in throughout the winter, and most of the bedrooms have en-suite facilities.
Kingfishers Lodge (ref UK36063) is a luxurious and spacious three-bedroom barn conversion, showcasing open plan living, underfloor heating, a private hot tub and bi-fold doors.
Deer Park (ref UK36064) is a luxurious and spacious three-bedroom barn conversion, showcasing open plan living, underfloor heating and bi fold doors seamlessly blending the living spaces with the outdoor landscape. The kitchen is fully equipped and there is also a utility with a washing machine.
All of the properties have their own private garden and on balmy summer evenings, is the ideal spot to relax with the prossecco which the thoughtful owners will leave for your arrival. All of the properties have a private hot tub, so don’t forget your towels!
With these properties being located on a deer farm, red deer and amazing stags can be seen close up, and there are sometimes otters in the ponds. Although the ponds are unfenced, the properties gardens are fenced, so there is some barrier between the garden and ponds.
The village of Cadeleigh lies just 9 miles from Exeter, with its magnificent cathedral and many shops and canalside pubs. Tiverton is just 6 miles away, and Bickleigh Mill with its lovely river walks, small fun railway, shop and café, is nearby. Spend a day exploring tranquil moorland and winding rivers in the Exmoor National Park, as well as the breathtaking coastline full of secluded bays and spectacular cliffs. Exmoor is sprinkled with quaint villages, attractive towns and charming harbours. Enjoy a day out at Tiverton Canal, walk with the horse drawn canal boat or enjoy a boat trip. Alternatively, take a trip to the north Devon coast and explore the dramatic coastlines and sandy beaches. Beach 24 miles. Shop 6 miles, pub and restaurant ½ mile.
These properties can be booked together to accommodate up to 40 guests.

reviews.comment: Great quiet location.  Great views of the wildlife when sat in the hot tub. The Otters is an amazing space for large family get togethers

Otters is an amazing very rural retreat.  Saw all sorts of wildlife except an otter!  The venue is wheelchair accessible but only for those with an assistant.  We took lots of our own kit to adapt the toilet etc.  Turning circle in bedroom limited and only then by moving / removing some furniture.Local roads are not for the feint hearted.  It will take you an extra 15 mins until you get to an A road.The June weather was disappointing which meant we spent less time outside / BBQ / hot tub than we would have liked but the views were still wonderful and every evening we had all sorts of wildlife on the other side of the lakes: deer, foxes, rabbit, birds but sadly no sight of the otter.

An amazing property which accommodated easily 16 of us. With 8 bedrooms and 8 bathrooms we all had some privacy!The downstairs open plan area was perfect for our family and friends get together, with plenty of seating the the living and dining areas. The location was perfect for what we wanted - a little remote with tight lanes to drive to the house- but there is a pub just down the road which we used twice for food which was great, and Tiverton is a 15 minute drive if you want a supermarket etc. we had only 1 small issue whilst we were there and that was a lack of towels. Each room should have had two, but after a couple conversations, more were delivered. May be worth bringing your own if you like a bath sheet or for when using the lovely hot tub. The views are stunning with the deers visiting across the ponds daily. I would recommend this property and the others in this area. I hope to return soon.

long_description:
Welcome to The Big Old Dairy, a fabulous holiday home sleeping up to sixteen people, suitable for all ages to enjoy a fabulous family holiday or celebrations! From family suites to a fabulous arctic cabin and hot tub, The Big Old Dairy really does have it all. Starting at the top, on the first floor you will find your two family suites set either side of the oak staircase. To the left you have the first bedroom which has a double bed, two single beds and a spacious en-suite with central roll top slipper bath to sink into and relax! On the right of the staircase is the second family room with double bed and two singles. Back on the ground floor, you will find four more bedrooms, one king, a twin and two king beds that can split into twins on request, there are three bathrooms on the ground floor, two with walk-in showers and one with spa bath that has a shower over.
The communal areas of this stunning property are fabulous. The large kitchen has everything you’ll need. The wonderful breakfast bar is the perfect spot to relax with drinks while meals are being prepared! The large dining room seats sixteen on a long table, a fabulous place to gather around for a meal at any time of day. Highchairs are also available on request free of charge. The spacious living room with underfloor heating has large comfortable sofas to sink into while the log fire crackles away; from here the living room opens up into the games room, a real fun area with a pool table, and even a beer fridge. The pool table has a solid cover, making it multi-use for suppers, board games or laying out a grazing platter for snacks! Outside is just as enchanting as inside. The cobbled courtyard houses the six-person cedar sauna, an invigorating cold bucket shower, barbecue area, chimenea, and a wonderful hot tub.
Another exciting feature of The Big Old Dairy is the gorgeous arctic cabin with centralised grill, a stunning chillout space to really escape and relax in. If you can bear to drag yourself away, local attractions include family entertainment at Weston-super-Mare and Brean, Wookey Hole, Cheddar with its famous caves and gorge, the beautiful cathedral city of Wells, Bath, and Glastonbury Tor visible from the top road. Golf and fishing lakes nearby. Why not hire a bicycle and join the Strawberry Line? The local award-winning pub is only 2 minutes walk away which is dog friendly we cannot stress enough BOOK IN ADVANCE. The best Chinese takeaway is just around the corner.

EPC Rating = B

long_description:
Experience relaxation at this stunning seven-bedroom mansion in Romford, Essex. This exquisite property offers five-star accommodation and an array of high-end amenities, including an indoor swimming pool, cinema room, games room, gym, sauna, and indoor and outdoor hot tubs. Set within 4 acres of beautifully landscaped grounds, it’s the perfect retreat for families, friends, or special gatherings, blending elegant interiors with world-class facilities for an unforgettable stay.
Each of the seven beautifully appointed bedrooms comfortably sleeps up to sixteen guests, with plush beds, quality linens, ample storage, en-suite bathrooms, and some rooms offering terrace access. Begin your day with a swim in the heated indoor pool or a workout in the private gym. For a more relaxing experience, unwind in the indoor sauna or soak in the hot tubs after a busy day.
Entertainment is at the heart of this property. The games room includes a pool table, table tennis, and various board games to entertain all ages. Movie nights come alive in the dedicated cinema room, complete with seating and a state-of-the-art sound system for an immersive experience.
Outside, the 4 acres of manicured gardens offer plenty of space for outdoor activities. Enjoy a picnic, lawn games, or a peaceful stroll around the grounds. The expansive patio provides a sunny spot for relaxation, while the poolside is perfect for lounging with a book. An outdoor BBQ and dining area invite al fresco meals, and the large kitchen, fully equipped with premium appliances, is ready for any culinary endeavour, whether you’re hiring a private chef or cooking for the group.
Just a short drive from Romford’s town centre, this property balances seclusion with easy access to nearby attractions. Enjoy excellent restaurants, local shops, and a range of activities, with London just a short trip away. Discover nearby gems like Thames Chase Forest Centre, with scenic trails for hiking, cycling, and wildlife spotting; Stubbers Adventure Centre, offering outdoor activities like kayaking, rock climbing, and high rope courses; and Cely Wood, a tranquil spot perfect for nature walks.
For those seeking more adventure, London is only an hour away, offering premier shopping, famous attractions like Covent Garden and Hyde Park, and a vibrant theatre scene. This Essex mansion is the ideal retreat to build lifelong memories with family and friends.
These properties can be booked together to accommodate up to 22 guests.

long_description:
Designed by Augustus (AWN) Pugin for the original directors of The Kendal Windermere railway, Number One, the flagship house on The Terrace is now available as a holiday let sleeping 14 people. The house has been renovated in a boutique hotel style, whilst retaining the features which gave it its grade II listing. On the ground floor there is a beautiful hand made kitchen with 4 oven Aga, it’s a fabulous space to cook up a gastronomic delight. Next door is a large utility room for those muddy boots and dogs and a very posh downstairs toilet. The large lounge has sumptuous leather Chesterfield sofas to seat up to 20 people in front of the fire. Perhaps Number One’s most special feature is a bar/dining room/party room. We’ve designed the space around get togethers, it has the capacity for the occupants of both number One and Two The terrace to dine together or if you’ve taken even more of our 5 houses on The Terrace you can push the tables back and use the room as your very own bar. In the cellar there’s an 18 seat cinema with 75 inch Smart TV. Login to your Netflix or Amazon Prime account and go to the movies in the comfort of your own holiday home. On the first floor there are 4 double bedrooms each with their own unique style. Bedroom one is a king size with en suite bathroom. Bedroom 2 has a super king size sleigh bed. Bedroom 3 is a standard double with antique style metal bedstead. Bedroom 4 is decorated and furnished in French style. There is also a large family bathroom with walk in wet room and huge free standing bath. The second floor is home to a room we affectionately call "The Dormitory", it has 4 single beds, the perfect place for the kids to disappear into. Next door is a double room with sloping feature eaves. There is an elegant bathroom with shower over bath and a second shower room. Outside is a large patio area with outdoor furniture, perfect for a barbecue, as well as a private hot tub. You can watch a short film about Number One here www.youtube.com/watch?v=sRNipLshK2E. You can view videos of this property and others on the street here www.youtube.com/user/TheTerraceWindermere.
This property can be booked together with any of the neighbouring properties or RENT THE WHOLE STREET Boston House (CC127199) and Bannerrigg (CC127195)  Alice Howe (CC127187) and White Moss (CC127244) to accommodate up to 66 people in 30 bedrooms!

All or part of the complex can be booked for large groups, parties or family gatherings. It would make an ideal venue for a wedding, with facilities allowing up to 100 guests to attend, by arrangement. They each have their individual character including beams and most with wood burners, with catering and a chef available to be booked directly with the owner.
Golf, horse riding, cycling and fishing are available locally, along with clay pigeon shooting and fly fishing. Take a stroll next to the river in the 20 acre grounds. Alternatively, there are many delightful, scenic countryside walks nearby including the spectacular scenic coast between Minehead and Combe Martin. Tiverton, 7 miles, offers a selection of shops, restaurants and pubs as well as the famous Grand Western Canal and Bickleigh Castle.
The nearest coast with sandy beaches and family attractions including Somerset World and West Somerset scenic steam railway is at the seaside resort of Minehead. The medieval town of Dunster with its magnificent castle, deer park and mill, and the historic cathedral city of Exeter with its variety of shops, restaurants, theatres, racecourse and the Maritime Museum, are both 20 miles away. Delightful Bickleigh, 8 miles, has lovely, thatched inns overlooking the river, and serving good food and local ales - the perfect location to get away from it all.
Taunton, Ilfracombe, Sidmouth, Seaton and Exmouth are within easy driving distance. National Trust properties within easy reach include Knightshayes Court, Powderham Castle and Castle Drogo to name a few. Brampton is 2 miles away, and sailing is available at nearby Wimbleball Lake. Shop 1½ miles, pubs 2 miles.

reviews.comment: Orchard Barn was a fantastic base for our large family group to explore Tiverton and the surrounding area. Downstairs has a well equipped kitchen and dining area plus three comfortable sitting rooms and an easily accessible downstairs bedroom. The other bedrooms are three groups of three and accessed by individual staircases, which gave a sense of privacy whilst still providing direct access to the communal areas.There is plenty of space outside, with several patio tables providing seating for "al fresco" dining, a covered BBQ area as well as a lovely summerhouse (also set up for dining) and quirky BBQ hut. A patio with garden furniture looks out over a large grassy field with climbing frame where the kids can run around whilst the adults enjoy their beverage of choice...Other features included a hot tub (which our host kept topped up with cleaning chemicals every day), wood fired sauna and games shed with a small billiard table and plenty of outdoor games. The only potential downside is that there are no local shops and the nearest pub is ten minutes walk up a busy country road with no pavements - however Tiverton is only ten minute's drive and has two large supermarkets who will deliver to the address.All in all Orchard Barn was exactly what we needed for our week-long family get together.

We had an absolutely fabulous time at Orchard Barn. The house was brilliant with everything you could need. The grounds were superb with an outside eating room for dining in and another for barbecuing. The children particularly loved the climbing frame,  swings and hot tub. The large field was used for playing football and family rounders. The position of the house was not too far from the coast. We had wonderful weather as well.

long_description:
Begin your stay by driving up the rural lane through the private electric gates and discover Firs Retreat at the top of the hill. Surrounded by a lawned garden area with a patio and plenty of seating, perfect for enjoying a morning coffee or evening cocktails. The property also features private parking for multiple vehicles, making it easy to explore the surrounding area.
The large sitting room features a large wooden dining table big enough to seat everyone around and plush seating, the perfect space to gather and enjoy each other’s company. The spacious kitchen/breakfast room area is fully equipped with top-of-the-line appliances and plenty of seating for the whole party. This stunning property boasts four spacious bedrooms, while the two beautifully appointed bathrooms ensure that everyone can stay comfortable and refreshed throughout their stay. For those looking for a touch of luxury, the spa bath in one of the bathrooms is the perfect place to soak away the stress of everyday life. And when you’re ready to take your relaxation to the next level, step out into the fabulous covered outdoor area. Here you’ll find a hot tub that can seat up to eight people, making it the perfect spot to unwind under the stars. Overall, this holiday house is the perfect place to escape the hustle and bustle of every day with family and friends.
Amazing walks can be found straight from the doorstep for you and your four-legged friends and the property is very close to Newark which is a market town and civil parish sitting within the Newark and Sherwood district of Nottinghamshire. Resting amongst the River Trent and the important Roman road of Fosse Way, it offers its visitors plenty to explore. Growing around the historic Newark Castle, which is now ruins that boast picturesque gardens, and a bustling marketplace, the town is now lined with a plethora of historic buildings waiting to be discovered. At the centre of the town you can find a wealth of historic wonders, enjoy a refreshing beverage in plenty of local pubs, including one of the oldest pubs in the town, or marvel at the tallest church in the county; The Church of St. Mary Magdalene, a Grade I listed building notable for its tower and octagonal spire, it’s just one of many architectural delights in the town.
With a rich history surrounding the English Civil War, the Nottinghamshire Civil War Trail is well-worth exploring if you’re seeking the main spots relating to this key period in history or spend a day in the Newark Museum to see diverse exhibits of this period up close. Besides its enticing history, the town also offers a plethora of shops and eateries where you can while away the hours, offering all kinds of cuisines to cater for every taste, or for those seeking an outdoor experience, be sure to venture into the Beacon Hill Conservation Park, a wonderfully peaceful park with plenty of wildlife and scenic settings to explore, it makes a lovely day out for all. Nearby Nottingham is well-worth visiting to discover its legend of Robin Hood. Pub and restaurant 1¼ miles.

long_description:
This stunning semi-detached country home is the perfect escape for families, couples, or those looking for the perfect house in which to celebrate a special occasion! Downstairs the extremely spacious open-plan living room, dining room, and kitchen take over the entire ground floor space, with gorgeous bi-fold doors leading to the garden area which really brings the outside in. Large sofas and armchairs surround the wood burner and large smart TV, the huge dining table is the perfect place for family breakfasts or long evenings eating dinner and playing games, the kitchen comes well equipped, while upstairs each of the bedrooms features kingsize or double beds and all of them come with their own en-suites and lovely views! Outside, the wonderful and large hot tub is the perfect place for relaxing whilst watching the sun go down, and there is a fabulous covered seating area looking over the hills beyond. The large garden is grassed and there are further seating areas on the other side of the parking area as well as a large area great for kids and dogs to run around and let off some steam!
The location is ideal for dog walking or simply taking in the wildlife and scenery, with much to enjoy within easy driving. There are many historic houses in the area, such as Montacute House and Gardens, and Forde Abbey and Gardens, or, guests can drive to Glastonbury Tor and walk to the top with some magnificent views of Somerset, call in Clarkes Village for some outlet bargains, head for a day out in Bath or visit Wells Cathedral. The Quantocks and Exmoor National Park are not far away and for a trip back in time, travel from Taunton along the West Somerset Steam Railway to Minehead. Going south, visit West Dorset and Devon, maybe spending a day or two exploring the World Heritage Jurassic coastal resorts of Sidmouth, Seaton, and Lyme Regis. The county town of Taunton is also well worth a visit, with its many shops, restaurants, and places of interest.
Beach 17 miles. Shop 4 miles, pub and restaurant 1 mile.

long_description:
Tucked away in the peaceful village of Great Urswick in the South Lakes within 5 minutes walk is a local pub with dining, this impressive newly converted holiday home offers a luxurious base for large families and multi-generational stays looking to explore one of the most beautiful corners of Cumbria. Sleeping up to 16 guests, with eight bedrooms configured for family’s with large beds and upper mezzanines with separate beds, four bathrooms with two baths and separate shower cubicles. The house has been finished to an exceptionally high standard while still retaining plenty of charm and character. This is a property which has had much thought, detail and design into such a unique and charming property. It really does need to be seen and explored, with it’s hidden doorways, glass walkways and lovely warmth.
Inside, the property is spacious, welcoming and thoughtfully designed for spending time together. The beautiful modern open-plan kitchen is fully equipped with everything needed for cooking for a full house, while the elegant dining area provides the perfect setting for long, relaxed meals. A generous lounge with a large TV offers a comfortable place to unwind after a day exploring the Lakes. One of the home’s standout features is its own private bar, making evenings in just as enjoyable as nights out. The bedrooms are varied and flexible, offering a range of sleeping arrangements to suit different family setups. A particularly unique space is the downstairs suite, which includes a living room with log burner, and a mezzanine level with double bed, and its own bathroom—ideal for guests wanting extra privacy. Outside, there is plenty of parking along with a lovely patio area featuring seating and lighting, plus a hot tub for relaxing under the stars.
Beyond the house, the surrounding area offers plenty to see and do. Just under five miles away lies Bardsea Beach, a peaceful coastal spot overlooking Morecambe Bay, perfect for a seaside walk or enjoying the fresh air and famous ice-cream, with restaurant and eateries providing additional beachfront snacks and drinks.
The property is also well positioned for exploring the western side of the Lake District National Park, an area often considered one of the quieter and more scenic parts of the region. A beautiful drive brings you to the landscapes around Coniston Water and the village of Coniston, where visitors can enjoy lakeside walks, water-sports and hiking in the surrounding fells.
Nearby market towns such as Ulverston offer independent shops, cosy pubs and excellent restaurants. With coastal scenery, lakes, mountains and charming villages all within reach, this holiday home in Great Urswick is an ideal base for memorable stays in the South Lakes.

reviews.comment: We had a fabulous time staying in Yard End for my 70th birthday. Lovely spacious house, comfortable beds and a very quiet site. We had a problem with our fridge freezer when we arrived and this was sorted immediately. Loved that we could book an hour a day personal use of the pool, which went down very well with our grandchildren. The hot tub went down very well too! All the site staff were so friendly and helpful and we got to know Bella the site cat very well. The food at the on-site Nine Eighty bistro was fabulous, with very generous portions, and it is a lovely venue just to sit and have a quiet drink. The site is close to many amenities and we visited Scarborough, Filey, Whitby, Bempton Cliffs, Flamborough Head, Dalby Forest, Pickering. All of these places were just a short drive away. My only criticism, and it is a small one, is that the equipment provided was a little basic.  There were no glass or pot bowls that could be put in the microwave (metal ones provided) also the largest of the normal pans did not appear to be compatible with the hob. The other thing was that no coasters were provided for the lovely coffee table. That said, it certainly didn't spoil our holiday and really was minor details.  We will definitely be back, fabulous place!

Great place for 3 generations of our family to stay together. Scarborough, Filey and Whitby within easy reach and even York. Circus just up the road was well worth a visit with discount vouchers from reception! Great having a bistro on site which suited everyone. Kids loved the play park and adults loved the hot tub! We also thought being able to book the pool for a private hour was a good idea. We spent our last day on Cayton beach which was perfect. The only downside was the wasp nest which affected the children’s room. It was dealt with by a professional firm, but as there was a chance that some larvae might survive the treatment we didn’t feel happy to use the room again, so had to change sleeping arrangements, which wasn’t ideal. Having said all that, we would definitely book this property again. Would also like to say that every member of staff we spoke to were extremely helpful and polite and nothing was too much trouble.

We had a 3 generational family holiday here recently and found the accommodation fitted our needs perfectly. There was plenty of room  for everyone. The cottage was only a short ride to both Scarborough and Filey. The site was quiet and safe with the pool, playground and eating area so close it allowed our grandson's more freedom than normal. They absolutely loved the pool and hot tub. Our only concern with the field and playground was that the surface was a little uneven and could lead to some injuries. Some of the furnishings were a little past their best, a sofa with covering coming off the headrests, a blind in the smallest bedroom not staying down, a cracked light shade in the hall and two mattresses that really could do with replacing. We also had concerns with the glass doors, maybe door stops could be provided as the doors slammed if we had the French windows open. We also had a bit of an issues with flies. The property was close to the bins but maybe some fly catchers could be provided. We did have a wonderful time and would definitely go back.

Electric underfloor central heating, electricity, bed linen and towels included. Wi-Fi, £5 per 2GB. Travel cot and highchair available on request. Welcome pack. Enclosed lawned garden with patio, garden furniture and barbecue. 60-acre natural grounds (shared with other properties on-site). Hot tub for 6 (private). There are steps, slopes and an unfenced lake in the grounds. The property has a natural water supply from a spring. This property has a security deposit of £400.

Bowlees Holiday Cottages are nestled on a hillside in the heart of County Durham, located a mile from the idyllic conservation village of Wolsingham in the Durham Dales. Raby Cottage (ref 27764), Durham Cottage (ref 27765) and Heartwell Cottage (ref UKC1473) are delightful, semi-detached properties. The Farmhouse (ref UKC3218) is detached and boasts everything a large party could ask for. Furnished to a very good standard, The Farmhouse is spacious, light and has ample facilities for up to 16 guests. There is a family suite on the ground floor which has curved walls and a high ceiling, and was previously a gin gang. There is a further suite on the first floor which has a galleried en-suite boasting a huge bath and equally impressive shower area. With a private hot tub, large lawned garden and views across the owner’s unspoilt grounds, which cover nearly 60 acres, guests may never want to leave. These holiday properties are absolutely perfect for families, walkers, cyclists and groups of friends wanting to enjoy a super holiday together. Additionally there is an on-site facility (open 9am-9pm) with games room with full-size snooker table, a heated indoor swimming pool and a shared hot tub. There is also a fishing lake that can be used by guests. Whether you choose to take in the scenic countryside that County Durham has to offer, or are looking for a quieter retreat, this is an ideal holiday base.
For guests who enjoy exploring the local area on foot or by bike, there are numerous established public footpaths and cycle paths that lead directly from the owner’s grounds. These paths go through some of the most scenic woodland and unspoilt countryside in the county. Just minutes away are Tunstall Reservoir and Hamsterley Forest, with bike riding, horse riding and many other activities available. Kilhope Lead Mining Centre and Beamish Museum are close by, as is a real snow ski lift.
Located around 30 minutes from the historic city of Durham with its World Heritage site status, cathedral and castle, guests really must take a day trip there to explore and enjoy all of the historic attractions, as well as indulging in a spot of well-earned retail therapy in one of the many boutiques. Alternatively, visitors can treat themselves to afternoon tea in one of the numerous cafés, restaurants and bistros. The National Railway Museum at Shildon, High Force Waterfall, the Metro Centre, Newcastle Airport, Durham Tees Valley Airport, Diggerland and Newcastle city centre, with its cultural attractions, are all within easy reach. Visit Hadrian’s Wall, Lake District National Park and the beautiful north east coastline. Shop, pub and restaurant 2 miles. These properties can be booked together to accommodate up to 43 guests.

The kids absolutely loved the heated swimming pool, the dads enjoyed the snooker table, and the mums relaxed in the hot tubs.The only thing that might make a longer stay challenging is the lack of a tumble dryer. Not a major problem, but something that could be improved.Overall, we would definitely recommend this property!

long_description:
In an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, this luxury celebration property is set on the owners own farm and enjoys beautiful views from the property, perfect for large groups of guests looking to get away and enjoy the area. Private driveway parking and a private rear garden are included with the property.
Nearby there are excellent circular walks, such as the Stiperstones, Clee Hills and Wenlock Edge, there are also walks direct from the door. Well worth a visit in the area are the National trust properties of Croft Castle, Powis Castle and Berrington Hall and Within easy reach there are the popular towns of Ludlow (with gourmet restaurants), Shrewsbury and Ironbridge are easily accessible all of which host an array of Bars, shops, and restaurants.
Shropshire is host to some delightful little towns such as Church Stretton and Much Wenlock, both with a good variety of individual shops and pubs. Bridgnorth, Ironbridge, Shrewsbury, Hereford, Worcester and Mid Wales are all easily accessible. This property is detached and is set across four levels. On the ground floor is a large, well-equipped farmhouse kitchen with breakfast table, a large utility space perfect for boots and coats, a downstairs W/C, dining room and living room. There is also a double bedroom on this floor. On the lower ground floor there is an additional kitchen, so plenty of space for rustling up hearty family meals or a midnight snack. Up on the first floor are six comfortable double bedrooms, three with their own en-suite, along with a family bathroom with bath and shower cubicle. The final bedroom, a twin room, can be found on the second floor along with a snug area, great as a cosy hideaway for the kids.
Outside you will find private gardens with patio seating area and a flat lawned area to the rear of the property, taking in the surrounding views. The property also boasts a private hot tub. There is a BBQ hut which has bench seating for 16 and a charcoal BBQ. There is driveway parking to the rear of the property.
This property can be booked with The Stables (ref UK35985) to accommodate up to 20 guests.

reviews.comment: The accommodation was excellent and had a great time.

Fabulous stay for our family birthday celebration. Excellent facilities and would highly recommend. Couple of  suggestions - take a pack of toilet rolls as one in each bathroom for 12 people over 3 days was nowhere near enough. Also we didn’t see anyone checking the filters or chemical levels in the hot tub which is something I would recommend. However none of those things spoiled our stay and would love to return in summertime to make the most of the outdoor terrace and bbq area.

A couple of extra large saucepans or casserole dishes are needed for home cooking for 12 people and the very worn IKEA crockery needs replaced. Also one of the internal bedroom doors didn't shut and a bathroom lock is broken.There is a lack of well organised facilities for recycling with no info in the house manual. The bins were overflowing and landfill was mixed with recycling. No food waste bin in the house so no encouragement to separate

long_description:
Set in the Exe Valley and very accessible from major roads, are these three beautiful properties which all offer the perfect holiday retreat. Catering and a chef is available to be booked directly with the owner. All or part of the complex can be booked for large groups, parties, or family gatherings. It would make an ideal venue for a wedding, with facilities allowing up to 100 guests to attend, by arrangement.
They each have their individual character including beams and most with wood burners. Duval Priory (ref 9985) dates back to 1086 is also Grade ll listed and enjoys its own private hot tub. Guests can also enjoy the River Exe, Devonshire Heartland, Somerset and the North Devon coastline on your doorstep, the properties are situated in an excellent countryside location offering a good base to explore the beautiful area and are within easy driving distance of Exmoor National Park and the Devon and Somerset border.
Golf, horse riding, cycling, and fishing are available locally, and clay pigeon shooting, fly fishing. Take a stroll next to the river in the fields. Alternatively, there are many delightful, scenic countryside walks to be found nearby including the spectacular scenic coast between Minehead and Combe Martin. Tiverton, 7 miles, offers a selection of shops, restaurants, and pubs as well as the famous Grand Western Canal and Bickleigh Castle.
The nearest coast with sandy beaches and family attractions including Somerset World and West Somerset scenic steam railway is at the seaside resort of Minehead. The medieval town of Dunster with its magnificent castle, deer park and mill, and the historic cathedral city of Exeter with its variety of shops, restaurants, theatres, racecourse and the Maritime Museum are both 20 miles away.
Delightful Bickleigh, 8 miles, has lovely, thatched inns overlooking the river serving good food and local ales, the perfect location to get away from it all. Taunton, Ilfracombe, Sidmouth, Seaton, and Exmouth within easy driving distance. National Trust properties within easy reach include Knightshayes Court, Powderham Castle and Castle Drogo to name a few. Bampton is 2 miles away, and sailing is available at nearby Wimbleball Lake. Shop 1½ miles, pubs 2 miles.
Please note: super-fast wifi, speeds up to 30 mbps.

reviews.comment: Enjoyed a special birthday celebration weekend with the family; 16 of us from 9 months to 81 years old staying in this lovely house! The inside of the house was spacious and comfortable and the snooker table well used by some of the family! The outside was enjoyed particularly by the children playing on the climbing frame. The owner was very helpful and friendly too. Would definitely recommend for a special family gathering!

We had a really enjoyable stay at the cottage. The property was relatively clean, with all the amenities described in the listing available and working well. The kitchen and washing facilities were particularly useful, and the living space was a good size and comfortable. It might feel a little cramped if occupied at full capacity, but for our stay it worked very well.The location is lovely, with a good amount of parking available. EV charging is available at the property, although we found it to be on the more expensive side. That said, there are other charging options available in the surrounding area.The property management was helpful and communication throughout our stay was good. Check-in was straightforward and checking out was very easy.Overall, we had a good experience and would happily stay here again with the family.

We had a wonderful stay at Duvale Priory for my mum's 70th. Plenty of space for 17 of us and great for a multi generational getaway. The kids loved the garden, especially the climbing frame and hot tub. Plenty of dining space inside and out. Bedspreads and some areas could do with an update but lovely for a few days.

long_description:
This ten-bedroom manor house is more than just a holiday let; it’s a gateway to indulgence, luxury and lasting memories. Perfect for gatherings with loved ones or celebrating a special occasion.

Welcome to a world of refined elegance and opulent relaxation at the enchanting Grade II listed ten-bedroom manor house near Awre near Newnham-on-Severn in the Royal Forest of Dean. This majestic holiday retreat offers an unparalleled experience, combining historic charm with modern luxury, and spanning across 7-acres of pristine grounds. Approaching the estate, you’ll be captivated by the grandeur of the manor, a testament to timeless architecture and meticulous craftsmanship. The property is embraced by lush gardens, stately trees, and the serene backdrop of the Gloucestershire countryside, inviting you to immerse yourself in nature’s embrace.
Step inside, and you’ll find a haven of sophistication and comfort that caters to your every desire. The manor boasts a spectacular kitchen, equipped with top-of-the-line appliances and ample space for both gourmet creations and casual meals. The dining areas, drenched in natural light, set the stage for lavish feasts and shared memories. Indulgence knows no bounds with not one, but two lavishly appointed lounges. The first, a refined space featuring exquisite furnishings and a fireplace, is an oasis of tranquillity. The second lounge embraces a more casual and convivial ambience, perfect for laughter-filled gatherings and leisurely evenings. For those who appreciate the finer things in life, the bar area beckons, inviting you to toast to special moments and enjoy each other’s company in style.
As you explore the estate, you’ll discover a private heated pool and hot tub, a sanctuary for relaxation and rejuvenation. Immerse yourself in the soothing waters, basking in the serene atmosphere and the beauty of the surrounding landscape. Beyond the manor’s walls, an external kitchen offers an outdoor culinary haven. Fire up the grill, prepare alfresco meals, and dine under the open sky as the sun sets over the sprawling grounds. The majesty of the estate is further revealed in the beautiful grounds that stretch across 7-acres. Stroll through the lawns, meander along pathways, and find solace in quiet corners where you can appreciate the beauty of nature in its purest form.
Awre and Newnham-on-Severn offer a glimpse into local life, while the wider region presents opportunities for outdoor adventures and cultural experiences. Whilst staying at The Manor House, why not take advantage of The Manor’s Fine Dining Experience? The grounds’ private chef will create hearty seasonal menus to tantalise the taste buds. For those extra special celebrations, opt for the bespoke al-a-carte menu to wow your party guests and make it an occasion to remember. Please speak directly with your hosts to discuss your requirements and they will be happy to help you. Please note: all caterers must be booked directly through White Birch Events. No external caterers are permitted at the property. With all this, you may never wish to leave the property but if you do then the location is excellent.
The River Severn is a 10-15 minute walk from the property whilst the Forest of Dean offers plenty for the adventurous including mountain biking, zip wires, Go Ape, kayaking and horse riding. There is an abundance of cycle tracks and valley walks where you may even encounter the native wild boar. Alternatively, just relax and enjoy the peace and tranquillity of this rural retreat.
Please note: There are open, steep, spiral or narrow stairs at the property.

long_description:
Alice Howe, (’sister property’ to Bannerrigg and Boston House) a grade II listed property, was designed by Augustus (AWN) Pugin (1812-1852), arguably the greatest British architect, designer and writer of the 19th century whose name is synonymous with the interior of the House of Lords and Westminster Abbey. This majestic home has its own cinema room and is furnished and presented in a unique style - chunky king-size four poster beds, solid ash single beds give and lush decoration - qualities that have justified the property’s 4 star status with Visit Britain.
Alice Howe has 7 bedrooms, and 7 bathrooms ( 5 of which are en-suite). Making it an ideal base for the larger party. The train and bus station are literally around the corner, so the house is easily accessible for those members of your group that are travelling from far and wide. We’ve also extended the car park to accommodate up to 6 cars. The addition of more single beds has made this property ideal not just for couples and families but now also for groups of single friends. The property also boasts its own private hot tub. If you’re looking for a big house to rent in the lakes for an ’upmarket’ stag or hen weekend Alice Howe is the ideal choice.This property can be booked together with any of the neighbouring properties or RENT THE WHOLE STREET - Boston House (CC127199), Bannerrigg (CC127195), White Moss (CC127244) and Number One (CC127243) to accommodate up to 66 people in 30 bedrooms!
Please note: There are open, steep, spiral or narrow stairs at the property.

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing, had the best time. This was booked for a big family get together with lots of small children, we were looking for something cheap and cheerful where the basics such as cleanliness and comfort was the main priority. This was all covered. We didn't need to be to concerned with the little ones running around. There was a few things that need to be improved but nothing that ruined our experience. We will definitely be booking again for family get togethers.

This property served its purpose for a family get together celebration weekend. It is a 'no frills' property in a good location to explore Blackpool and set on the front with great sea views.The rooms are all ensuite and clean although some fixtures and fittings do need attention. Beds clean and comfortable.The dining room is great, the reception rooms are adequate but need a little attention especially some of the conservatory furniture. There is access to some very unpleasant 'dumping rooms' which does detract from the property and there is no waste recycling availableThe kitchen is a galley kitchen and on the whole good, however some cupboards need a clean out and the crockery and glassware sorting. One of the fridges is out o action and the door off. The kitchen obviously has the original pots etc of a hotel so there is a lot of unwanted, unnecessary ware. There is a shortage of essentials such as glasses and mugs and cooking utensils. It just needs a good sort out as I suspect there has been many breakages over time due to stag and hen party groups and items not replaced. I do think it is important to sort these issues and then hopefully any visitors will show more respect. The property served us well, as a family ranging in age from 18mnths to 93 years. The hot tub and sauna were great but the pool table equipment and games room furniture needed attention. Again this is due to visitor mis-use.  We left several things in a better condition than we found it, Having said all that , we felt it was excellent value for money, the owner and housekeeper easily contactable and very helpful and friendly. Parking at the property for 4 cars (5 small cars) with free parking on adjacent streets was a bonus.. Directions and access to the property was very straight forward. Access to the promenade and beach, and regular trams down to the attractions were excellent. We had a lovely afternoon tea (birthday celebration) in the Tower ballroom and the nearby Gynn pub and restaurant, which we pre booked, did us an excellent family meal for 23.
There were no serving dishes. Ivan was not working, Dona was not working, no toilet trees included tissue, no bin bag,

long_description:
Cotswold Valley Court Manor is a handsome six-bedroom residence tucked away in the peaceful hillside community of France Lynch. Set in the heart of the Cotswolds, this graceful detached home offers an inviting blend of rural seclusion and effortless comfort, making it ideal for celebratory gatherings, relaxed family holidays or weekends with friends.
The surrounding landscape is classic Cotswold scenery, wooded valleys, honey-coloured villages and footpaths that weave between meadows and streams. Guests can head out on long country walks, wander through nearby market towns or pause at local tearooms, bakeries and old-world inns. Well-known attractions such as Painswick’s Rococo Garden, the Corinium Museum in Cirencester, Westonbirt’s world-famous arboretum and the lakes of the Cotswold Water Park are all within easy reach.
Inside, the house has been thoughtfully arranged to encourage both togetherness and a quiet retreat. The bright kitchen and breakfast room forms the centre of the home, with bespoke finishes, ample workspace and doors opening straight to the courtyard. It’s well supported by a practical utility area and a ground-floor toilet. Formal meals can be enjoyed in the elegant dining room, while the main sitting room, anchored by its traditional stone fireplace, provides a warm spot to unwind after days out exploring. A smaller snug offers additional space for reading or escaping into a film.
Upstairs, four stylish bedrooms occupy the first floor, each paired with its own en-suite for privacy and comfort. The top level hosts a generous suite with a superking and twin beds alongside a luxurious bathroom with a free-standing clawfoot tub, plus an additional 3 berth room completing the accommodation.
Three acres of private grounds surround the manor, offering lawns, open fields and tranquil corners to enjoy. Younger guests can make the most of the outdoor play area, while adults may prefer the soothing warmth of the hot tub as dusk settles. With its charming setting and spacious interiors, Cotswold Valley Court Manor promises a restful and memorable countryside escape.

Party of 11 adults, 1 child, 3 babies and 1 dog. The owner lives next door and shares access and parking on the drive, which meant we had to put 2 cars in the field. I wasn't comfortable with cctv recording outside 24/7. The owners complained about one of our babies crying after 10pm!!! This was an extremely hot summer and all windows needed to be open. This put a dampener on our stay as we felt we couldn't sit out for too long in the evening. It was nice that 5 of the bedrooms had an en-suite, however there is no communal bathroom, so the unlucky 6th bedroom occupier (on the top floor!) had to come all the way to the ground floor, just to use a loo. And then wait for someone to get up to be able to get a shower. Being able to see a floor plan of the accommodation would have helped us to see this was not ideal for us.
A great cottage, well equipped. The owner was attentive and responded quickly to emails and texts. We were a family of 8 adults and 4 children.

long_description:
Located in a peaceful village seven miles from the historic harbour town of Padstow, famed for its thriving harbour and superb seafood restaurants. Greenacres, as its name suggests sits proudly amongst rolling countryside and valleys. In the distance the sea glistens, inviting you to explore the beaches, rock pools and coves and seaside villages which punctuate the stunning North Cornwall Coast. Harlyn Bay Beach, just 5 miles distant has a far-reaching stretch of golden sand, which meets the vast Atlantic Ocean, whilst Trevose Head offers vistas to behold, offering walks in abundance for the intrepid adventurer! Venture south to Newquay, vibrant and alive and with water sports to the fore or inland to ancient and mysterious Bodmin Moor. Marvel at the world-famous Eden Project or beautiful Lost Gardens of Heligan, have fun at the Camel Creek Family Theme Park... The opportunities for a brilliant day out really are truly never ending.
Your holiday home has space for up to 14 guests, with bright and airy rooms providing the perfect setting to unwind, relax and recharge. The recently refurbished kitchen has all you need to facilitate your stay, whilst the living areas have comfortable soft furnishings to sink into, including several wonderful sofas. There are 2 bathrooms finished to a high standard on the ground floor too, along with a king-size bedroom and twin room, both wonderfully furnished. Also find a useful utility room with washing machine and tumble dryer. Advance upstairs and this impressive home boast a further four bedrooms, a family room with twin beds and bunks, a twin room and 2 king sized bedrooms, all of these providing en-suite facilities. The charming garden with its spectrum of green shades has a special treat instore…..it’s very own hot tub, where you can feel the hustle and bustle of everyday life as it just drifts away.
Padstow is 4 miles, Newquay is 9 miles and Porthcothan bay is a 15 minute walk away. There is a large car park opposite to Porthcothan bay which is free November to March.

long_description:
Glenvar is a very special and unique property with lift access to the first floor. A brand-new modern build completed in 2021. It has direct access to its own beach at the end of the garden and enviable direct sea views. A sublime and idyllic beach setting making it a place to make special memories, whether walking in the shoreline, soaking in the hot tub, hanging out listening to lapping waves or celebrating in this large spacious home and garden with family and friends.
As you enter the property you are immediately greeted by a sense of light and space, with a feature staircase up to the first floor, large open-plan kitchen and living space. This area was made for entertaining, being together and relaxing in this amazing setting. This floor is also fully accessible by a lift if required. After a day on the beach, you will want to kick off your footwear, swimmers, or wellies in the handy utility room, where you can wash and dry clothes or the dog if needed.
The underfloor heating will also make you feel warm and cosy. This home has been lovingly built by its owners with lots of attention to detail creating a minimalistic and modern feel whilst maintaining a sustainable building with environmentally friendly characteristics.
This is really evident when you arrive at the property. It also offers a very generous balcony that has mood lighting where you can sit and watch the world go by as you listen to the waves lap against the beach. This pet friendly property has some amazing features like a hot tub and a large lawned garden with a beach at the end. It also has its own lift so that you can access the top floor should you have mobility needs. With bedrooms on the ground floor and the first floor this is certainly a home that has all the accessibility you need for a staycation this year. The minimalistic and modern décor gives you a really modern feel and with the underfloor heating and the huge open plan kitchen/dining room is a very special place to sit and enjoy a relaxing time.
A perfect location to explore Sussex and Hampshire. Within easy reach of Portsmouth, Chichester, Bognor Regis, Littlehampton, and Brighton. Goodwood is only 10 miles away which hosts the Festival of Speed, Goodwood Revival, Goodwood festival plus many more. Or you can just sit and relax in your own private hot tub.

long_description:
Town House I is situated in a prime position in Scarborough, just a short walk from the North Bay. All the bedrooms have TVs and en-suite facilities, and the icing on the cake is the hot tub, enclosed in its own area, in the courtyard!
The town and shops are within walking distance with a great indoor shopping centre and lots of boutiques, and for those who prefer the nightlife, there are plenty of bars, restaurants, clubs and a casino. Just around the corner is the Scarborough cricket ground where the famous Scarborough Festival is held each year, an end of season competition featuring Yorkshire County Cricket Club. For those who love a faster sport, there’s Oliver’s Mount racing track with high powered road race bikes. As you walk to the beach you pass one of the entrances to Peasholm Park. Take a detour and walk around the park with its stunning gardens, lakes and waterfalls. There are boats and pedalos, and in summer, a brass band to entertain you. The park is famous for the Naval Warfare Battle where model ships re-enact a battle on the lake. It’s great entertainment for the kids and has been for the last 80 years.
One of the best things about Scarborough is that it has two bays, quite different from each other. The South Bay is a traditional seaside resort with donkeys, amusements and shops, whereas the North Bay is much quieter and more relaxed. Half way between the two bays, the castle stands proud on the cliffs above. You can walk the full length of Marine Drive from North to South Bay, and it’s nice and flat making it easy for that evening stroll. If you prefer, there are the open top buses that run along the seafront. At the far end of North Bay is the Sealife Centre and the open air theatre, one of the largest outdoor theatres in Europe where international acts play during the summer.
Further down the coast is Filey, Flamborough and Bridlington. The RSPB bird sanctuary at Bempton is worth a visit where you can see puffins in their natural habitat. North of Scarborough are the beautiful North York Moors, and Whitby, a bustling fishing town famous for Whitby Jet Jewellery and the Goth weekends. You are only an hour away from York, a beautiful medieval city where you can visit the Railway Museum, take a leisure cruise on the river or walk the city walls which surround it. Beach 700 yards. Shop and restaurant 200 yards, pub 400 yards.
Town House 1 (ref UK12894) can be booked together with Town House II (ref UK12892) to accommodate up to 24 guests.

long_description:
Gather with extended family and friends and celebrate a special occasion in style, where you can relax in the hot tub or simply relax in the courtyard or outside gardens.. A perfect choice for friends and family wanting to holiday together but retain full privacy. Cosy nights in can be enjoyed snuggled up by the wood burner and the well-equipped kitchen offers the opportunity to dine in. There is a private enclosed garden, a sun trap with seating furniture, perfect for al fresco eating and relaxation. The large, landscaped gardens are perfect for younger children wanting to run around or play football. This substantial barn conversion is soaked in original features and character.
A wonderful home ideal for social gatherings and any special occasion. Boasting a hot tub and large wrap-around landscaped gardens with enclosed central courtyard garden, offer complete privacy. Perfectly positioned to explore all the delights of Norfolk, with its amazing coastline, wide sandy beaches and the famous Norfolk Broads National Park, a natural haven and habitat for wildlife. Sleeping 12 guests in 6 bedrooms, some with views of the courtyard, it is an ideal retreat for all generations, benefiting from no stairs. All doors open to the central courtyard garden. The kitchen has a breakfast table and extended lounge seating area, and the formal dining room is the perfect place to host any family celebration. There is a conservatory with great outlook across the garden. You can find games and seat cushions for the garden inside the utility room.
Nestled within the Broadland village of South Walsham, set in lush countryside, excellent walking and cycling that can be enjoyed from your doorstep, with designated footpaths, trails and quiet country lanes surrounding the property. The market town of Acle, 4 miles and Brundall, 5 miles offer railway stations, post office, mini-market, hairdressers and local eateries. There are many good food serving pubs within the surrounding area, some of which are located alongside the river. Jump on the train to visit the city of Norwich, or the traditional seaside towns of Great Yarmouth and Lowestoft. Norwich is 11 miles away where guests can visit the cathedral, castle museum, theatre, excellent shopping and art galleries. Wroxham, only 5.5 miles away, is known as the capital of the Norfolk Broads, and has waterside shops, cafés, and daily boat hire with river trips available to explore the expanse of waterways. There is an RSPB reserve at Strumpshaw Fen and Steam Museum, 6 miles. 9-hole golf course and driving range at Blofield, 4 miles.
Norfolk’s finest sandy beaches are within 14 miles and include Winterton-on-Sea, Waxham, Horsey and Sea Palling. For fun-filled family days out there is Thrigby Hall Wildlife Gardens, Reedham offers Pettitt’s Animal Adventure Park, BeWILDerwood at Horning, and Dinosaur Adventure Park at Lenwade. There are several National Trust properties in the region and three heritage railways: The North Norfolk Railway, The Mid Norfolk Railway and the Bure Valley Railway. Daily boat hires available at Wroxham, Acle and Brundall.
