reviews.comment: Just spent a week at Lodge Barn Farm wirh a family group of eight spanning four generations.  The place was well above expectations providing everything we needed.  We could have family time in the open plan kitchen/ living area but also quiet time  in the lounge at the end of the property.  Every room has its unique character with furniture to match.  The hot tub was great at the end of the day followed by playing games that were also provided.  The location was excellent with most attractions within 30 mins travelling. Overall this was a great place and we thoroughly enjoyed staying there.  We would not hesitate to use this cottage again should the occasion arise.

I would definitely recommend Lodge Farm Barns for a family holiday. We spent four days here with 6 Adults and 4 children. The place was beautiful, clean and well stocked in the kitchen with everything imaginable.. Everything you could need in a family home was there. Lots of safe areas to play outside for the young children. For the adults a hot tub and we let the children join with supervision. Although Lodge Farm is next to the road you do hear the traffic from the bedroom side of the house as it’s nearer to the road, but it was not a problem The rest of the house is quiet. The family enjoyed the table tennis, darts/ dartboard and basketball in the barn  at the side of the house. All in all we had a fabulous long weekend and the family all agreed that we would love to come back again sometime in the future .

We had a family holiday at Lodge Farm Barn, 6 adults and 4 children aged 6, 5, 3 & 2, three generations, and we all thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The 3 year old is still asking to go back to our holiday home as she wants to go in the hot tub! We were all taken aback at the sheer size of the place, as we've never stayed anywhere that big before.  The kitchen was very well equipped and had everything we needed. We mainly used the kitchen/day room as it was cosy and a central place to hang out in, and enough seating for all us adults in the evening.  The children were very happy to have such a large place to play in and enjoyed playing in the library area mostly.  The front garden was also a  great play area for them as long as there was an adult with them, and the inner garden perfect as it was fully enclosed and safe for them. The bedrooms and bathrooms were plentiful and suited our needs. If I had to say anything negative, then the conservatory area is cold this time of year, which wasn't a problem if you kept the doors closed, but the little ones were going back & forth, leaving the doors open. Some of the bathrooms had carpet in, which from a hygiene point of view, wasn't ideal. Neither of these small negatives would stop us from returning  however,  as we all had a fab time - plenty of room for us all and in a great location being handy for the Broads and Great Yarmouth.  We left the barn clean and tidy and I got my security deposit back quickly.  We were all sad to leave as we all enjoyed spending family time together.

Biomass central heating, gas, electricity, bed linen, towels and Wi-Fi included. Initial logs for wood burner included. 1 cot and 2 highchairs. Welcome pack. Large enclosed lawned garden with courtyard, terrace, garden furniture, summerhouse and BBQ. 80-acre grounds with mini golf and woodland (shared with other properties on-site). Hot tub (private). Private parking for 20 cars. No smoking. Please note: There are 15 steps, 33 yards from the mansion house, and an unfenced pond/small lake with the ornamental summerhouse, 66 yards from the mansion house. There are 3 other unfenced ponds within the 80 acres of grounds.

Nestled in the beautiful Cumbrian countryside Blaithwaite Estate is surrounded by 80 acres of estate grounds made up of 30 acres of gardens and grounds and 50 acres of woodland. Blaithwaite House (ref UKC1358) is a Grade II listed, detached country mansion which has been in the same family since the 1700s and is now available for guests to enjoy. The spacious country mansion is awash with original features from original ceiling roses and exquisite fireplaces to stained glass windows which adorn the building, helping it achieve its listed status. Comfortable accommodation is provided for up to forty people, in single, double and family rooms. The bedrooms, all but one room with en-suite facilities, enjoy views down to the sprawling front lawn and rose garden or across the courtyard.
Blaithwaite House is set in a large mature garden, ideal for your children or the dog to play in, with manicured lawns and a charming walled rose garden with a beautiful summerhouse set on an island (the small ornamental water is over 300 meters from the property and down a set of stone steps).
You don’t have to go too far to explore, as the estate grounds offer a wealth of activities available (at cost) are laser tag, or bushcraft, and seasonal event days or for something a little gentler (and no cost), play crazy golf, play on the play areas, and football fields, take a walk around the woodland including a specialist arboretum and wetlands that you can explore, you can even grab the estate nature passport to assist with your exploring!
If you fancy exploring the area, the estate is set midway between Keswick and Carlisle where you can find a great range of shops, restaurants and bars, plus museums and activities to suit a wide range of tastes and interests. Beach 10 miles. Shop 1½ miles, pub 2 miles and restaurant 5 miles.
These properties can be booked together to accommodate up to 80 guests.

long_description:
Magnificent 16th-Century Manor House with hot tubs, set in idyllic Kent countryside.
Tucked away in the heart of the Kent countryside, this exceptional 16th-century manor offers a rare opportunity to stay somewhere truly unique. Surrounded by open skies and overlooking miles of peaceful marshland, this beautiful home combines historic charm with generous space, making it perfect for large family gatherings, celebrations, and memorable escapes.
Sleeping up to 14 guests across six beautifully presented bedrooms (five kingsize and one twin), the house has been designed for bringing people together. At its heart is a spacious, well-equipped kitchen diner, ideal for long, sociable meals, alongside a formal 14-seater dining room perfect for special occasions. Two welcoming reception rooms, complete with open fires, create warm and inviting spaces to relax, while a bright sunroom offers a quieter spot to unwind and take in the surrounding views.
The bedrooms are thoughtfully arranged to suit both families and groups, including a large family room, while the mix of stylish shower rooms and characterful roll-top bathrooms adds to the home’s charm.
Set within approximately one acre of gardens, the grounds are a true highlight. With far-reaching views across five miles of marshland, there is a real sense of peace and privacy. For those looking to celebrate something special, the space also lends itself beautifully to small weddings or events, with the option to hire a marquee and create a truly bespoke countryside setting (by prior arrangement).
For relaxation, guests can enjoy not one but two hot tubs, including a traditional Japanese wood-fired tub, perfect for unwinding under the stars after a day exploring.
The location is ideal for discovering some of Kent’s most sought-after coastal and historic destinations. Just a short drive away, the charming seaside town of Deal offers a wonderful mix of independent shops, cafés and a picturesque seafront. History lovers can explore the impressive Deal Castle and Walmer Castle, both steeped in Tudor history and set along the coastline.
Nearby Sandwich, one of England’s best-preserved medieval towns, provides cobbled streets, historic buildings and a timeless atmosphere, while also being home to world-renowned golf courses along the coast. The surrounding area is perfect for walking, cycling and enjoying the natural beauty of the Kent countryside, with the coast just a couple of miles away offering fresh sea air and wide, open beaches.
Whether you’re planning a relaxed countryside escape, a coastal adventure, or a special celebration with family and friends, this remarkable manor house provides a truly unforgettable setting.

short_description: Two renovated farm cottages sleeping 16, with a hot tub, large garden room for group meals and fenced gardens, plus meadows by the River Severn for walks and the chance to fish or swim.
long_description:
For big get-togethers, these two renovated farm cottages sit side by side and sleep up to 16 guests in total. The setting is made for sociable breaks, with wraparound patios and extensive fenced gardens, plus a hot tub for post-walk soaks. Meadows by the River Severn add an extra dose of countryside, whether you want a gentle stroll or a quiet spot to sit and watch the water.
Inside, there is plenty of room for groups to spread out as well as come together. The larger cottage has an airy garden room that can seat everyone for shared meals, with a double-sided wood burner for cooler evenings. You will also find a cooker range and a wine fridge, along with a Smart TV and table football for friendly competitions. The second cottage includes a snug that works brilliantly as a movie room for children, giving adults space to chat elsewhere. Sleeping is arranged across a mix of king-size, double and bunk-style rooms, with en-suite facilities for the king rooms, family bathrooms, and an additional ground-floor king bedroom with its own private bathroom in the larger cottage.
Outside, the patios and handmade lounge seating encourage long, lazy afternoons, while the raised beds and garden space give children room to play. When you fancy a change of pace, wander down to the riverside meadows for fishing or a bracing dip, then return to the hot tub and plan the next day’s adventures. It is a welcoming choice for multi-generation breaks, reunions and celebrations where everyone wants to stay close, without being on top of one another.

short_description: Elegant Georgian manor with extensive gardens and hot tub, set in the Lincolnshire countryside and ideal for large group gatherings or special occasions.
long_description:
Set within the peaceful South Lincolnshire countryside, this impressive Georgian manor offers a refined retreat surrounded by extensive grounds and open views. Approached along quiet country lanes, the house enjoys a sense of privacy while still providing a welcoming base for gatherings and special occasions. The surrounding gardens and woodland create a calm setting for relaxing walks, outdoor dining and time spent together in the fresh air.
Inside, the manor retains a wealth of original character, with elegant proportions and period features throughout. A sweeping staircase sets a striking first impression, leading to a series of spacious reception rooms designed for both entertaining and unwinding. Each room has its own atmosphere, from more formal spaces with traditional fireplaces to a quieter library for reading and reflection. A billiards room offers a sociable setting for evenings, while a bright studio space provides a flexible area for creative pursuits or peaceful moments away from the main group. The kitchen combines character with practicality, offering ample space for preparing and sharing meals.
The seven bedrooms are thoughtfully styled to provide comfort and a restful night’s sleep, with a mix of layouts suited to families and groups. Outside, the grounds extend to generous lawns, formal planting and areas of woodland, offering plenty of space to explore. A terrace creates a lovely spot for dining alfresco, while the hot tub provides a relaxing place to unwind at the end of the day. With its blend of heritage, space and countryside setting, this manor is a memorable choice for group stays.

long_description:
Set within beautiful grounds near Newark in Nottinghamshire, this magnificent country house offers a grand and memorable setting for family gatherings, celebrations and special occasions. Built in 1812 on a site of notable English history, it combines impressive period architecture with generous leisure spaces, giving guests the feeling of a private estate stay. With accommodation for up to 18 guests, it is well suited to larger groups who want room to gather, relax and mark time together.
Inside, the house is designed for entertaining on a generous scale. Elegant reception rooms provide space for formal meals, relaxed conversations and quieter moments, while the private cinema and sophisticated cocktail bar add a sense of occasion to evenings in. Leisure facilities include a heated swimming pool, sauna, steam room, gym equipment and hot tub, offering plenty to enjoy without leaving the grounds. Alongside the main bedrooms, two sofa beds provide additional flexibility, one in the study and one in a bedroom.
The landscaped gardens give the property a calm and private backdrop, with space to wander, sit outside or enjoy the setting between shared activities. The Nottinghamshire location places guests within reach of Newark and the surrounding countryside, while the house itself provides more than enough to fill a stay with comfort and interest. Whether planning a milestone birthday, a family reunion or a special group break, this is an impressive country residence where history, space and leisure come together for an unforgettable stay, with plenty to keep every generation entertained throughout the stay.

long_description:
Town House II is situated in a prime position in Scarborough, just a short walk from the North Bay. All the bedrooms have TVs and en-suite facilities, and the icing on the cake is the enclosed hot tub in the courtyard!
The town and shops are within walking distance with a great indoor shopping centre and lots of boutiques, and for those who prefer the nightlife, there are plenty of bars, restaurants, clubs and a casino. Just around the corner is the Scarborough cricket ground where the famous Scarborough Festival is held each year, an end of season competition featuring Yorkshire County Cricket Club. For those who love a faster sport, there’s Oliver’s Mount racing track with high powered road race bikes. As you walk to the beach you pass one of the entrances to Peasholm Park. Take a detour and walk around the park with its stunning gardens, lakes and waterfalls. There are boats and pedalos, and in summer, a brass band to entertain you. The park is famous for the Naval Warfare Battle where model ships re-enact a battle on the lake. It’s great entertainment for the kids and has been for the last 80 years.
One of the best things about Scarborough is that it has two bays, quite different from each other. The South Bay is a traditional seaside resort with donkeys, amusements and shops, whereas the North Bay is much quieter and more relaxed. Half way between the two bays, the castle stands proud on the cliffs above. You can walk the full length of Marine Drive from North to South Bay and it’s nice and flat making it easy for that evening stroll. If you prefer, there are the open top buses that run along the seafront. At the far end of North Bay is the Sealife Centre and the open air theatre, one of the largest outdoor theatres in Europe where international acts play during the summer.
Further down the coast is Filey, Flamborough and Bridlington. The RSPB bird sanctuary at Bempton is worth a visit where you can see puffins in their natural habitat. North of Scarborough are the beautiful North York Moors, and Whitby, a bustling fishing town famous for Whitby Jet Jewellery and the Goth weekends. You are only an hour away from York, a beautiful medieval city where you can visit the Railway Museum, take a leisure cruise on the river or walk the city walls which surround it. Beach 700 yards. Shop and restaurant 200 yards, pub 400 yards.
Town House II (ref UK12892) can be booked together with Townhouse 1 (ref UK12894) to accommodate up to 24 guests.

long_description:
Westfield Courtyard is a standout option within Westfield Country Park, tailored for groups, extended families or celebratory get-togethers. It comprises six self-contained cottages laid out around a rustic, landscaped courtyard, creating a communal yet private retreat.
Each cottage is designed with open-plan living in mind: you’ll find a lounge/dining/kitchenette area fitted with a widescreen TV, an electric fire, and space to relax together. Bedrooms are double occupancy, and each cottage has its own modern bathroom with a walk-in shower. Cottage 3 includes a whirlpool bath along with a separate shower, and Cottage 6 features a whirlpool bath (though without a separate shower).
To support group dynamics and shared activities, Cottage 3 is fitted with a large group dining kitchen capable of seating all twelve guests — ideal for communal meals or celebrations. Cottage 5 adds a recreational twist, featuring a games lounge complete with a pool table and a projector.
At the heart of the courtyard is a shared outdoor hot tub. The cottages do not interconnect internally, preserving privacy for each unit even while being part of a larger group setting. In terms of setting, the Courtyard is just about 100 metres from the on-site fishing lake, giving guests convenient access to angling as part of their stay. As part of Westfield Country Park, the Courtyard shares in the park’s broader amenities: the park itself spans roughly 37 acres of landscaped countryside close to the East Yorkshire coastline, and offers a quiet, natural backdrop.
Westfield Courtyard welcomes dogs and includes all the standard comforts. It strikes a balance between group togetherness and individual cottage independence, making it a compelling choice for those wanting a shared holiday experience with enough space to retreat.

long_description:
Impressive and welcoming, Corffe House is an 18th-century, Grade II listed, Georgian country house and former rectory to the 13th-century church of St Peter from 1801 to 1948. When you stay here you could be forgiven for thinking you are starring in your own episode of Downton Abbey, with its generous sized rooms and sweeping staircase. It is this combined with the modern-day touches, such as the cinema room with pool table and uninterrupted views over the beautiful Devon countryside, that make for an unforgettable stay. Corffe House is ideal for family gatherings and group celebrations due to its idyllic location and first class facilities. With ample reception rooms, nine bedrooms and eight bathrooms, the house itself offers both space and character with many charming period features including large sash windows, original shutters, marble fireplaces and ornate coving.
The excellent facilities on-site include an indoor swimming pool with hot tub and children’s paddling pool, 5 acres of grounds and situated on the top grassy area beyond the woodland, there is a goal for any budding Beckhams! Anyone for tennis? Well, there’s also a free all-weather court for you to hit a few balls on! There is a lovely barbecue cabin in the woods which can be hired. During the winter months, you can stay cosy and warm cooking around the fire, and over the summer you can spill out onto the outdoor seating area. If you like pizza, then there’s a regular weekly mobile pizza night brought to the courtyard by a local pizza expert!
Barnstaple is the regional capital where you can have a taste of North Devon life by wandering the streets and river front. The town also offers a leisure centre with swimming pool, a purpose-built tennis centre with indoor and outdoor courts, an indoor trampoline centre and Rock Park.
The location is perfect for exploring North Devon and all its attractions, such as Exmoor National Park with its magical night skies. There are plenty of family-oriented places to visit including Exmoor Zoo, Milky Way Adventure Park, The Big Sheep farm-themed park and many others.
If stunning beaches are your thing, then North Devon will leave you spoilt for choice with Saunton, Woolacombe, Croyde and Westward Ho! The fantastic South West Coast Path runs through the region’s rugged coastline and is perfect for walkers. The popular Tarka Trail can be accessed from the town centre, which will take you through Fremington Quay, with its excellent café, and Instow, with its estuary beach and view towards the lovely fishing village of Appledore.

long_description:
Peace, tranquillity and luxury is everything that you will find during your stay at The Hoggest, along with 360 degree views of some of Lakelands finest scenery. Nestled at the foot of Blencathra, this stunning location really is surrounded by natural beauty, settled behind the village of Threlkeld and within easy reach of Keswick and the Lake District National Park, making it an ideal place to explore from.
Luxuriously renovated from a former stone farm building, this detached property offers quality and comfort to an excellent standard, and even has its own hot tub. Relax in the bright and airy living room with the bi-folding doors opening out to the views, or for a warm and comfy evening, light the wood burner and relax in the large sumptuous sofas. The open plan layout provides the perfect place to entertain in, with large dining table and well equipped kitchen, where everyone can enjoy mealtimes and come together. After a good night’s sleep in the comfortable beds open the curtains and take in the views of the surrounding fells, and down towards St Johns in the Vale, a truly inspiring way to start your day. For larger parties why not book The Hoggest in conjunction with the annexe (UK31000) sleeps up to 12 people altogether, whilst offering some privacy to family or group of four.
Threlkeld has a golf course and two renowned pubs, each serving real ale, good food and one with a restaurant, whilst the vibrant market town of Keswick is only a few miles away. With fabulous fell walks from the doorstep, The Hoggest provides a great base for your holiday in the North Lakes. Shop 4½ miles, pub and restaurant 1¼ miles.

Surrounded by peaceful countryside, yet just 5 miles from the bustling city of York, Murton Grange is perfectly located to enjoy the best of both worlds. The traditional farmhouse and eight cottages are comfortably furnished and ideal for large group bookings (including hen and stag parties). Five of the properties include a private hot tub and guests are requested to bring their own towels for use with the hot tub.
There are walking trails from the doorstep and easy access into the city centre. York offers all year round appeal, with world-renowned attractions including the iconic minster, Castle Museum and the Jorvik Viking Centre. There is a busy racecourse at the Knavesmire and regular festivals and Christmas markets. Enjoy a riverboat trip, join a ghost walk or take a stroll around the city walls. An abundance of inns, restaurants and traditional teashops can be found in the city centre which is packed with interesting and individual shops, and the Designer Outlet, Vangarde and Monks Cross provide excellent out of town shopping.
Murton Grange provides an ideal base from which to explore the surrounding area where there are stately homes at Castle Howard, Beningbrough Hall and Sledmere House. Quaint market towns at Malton, Helmsley and Pickering and the famous steam train which travels through the stunning scenery of the North York Moors. The coastal towns of Filey, Scarborough and Whitby are all within an hour’s drive. Shop 3½ miles, pub and restaurant 2¼ miles.

long_description:
Low Jock Scar Country Estate is made up of four separate properties within the same complex, including two hot tubs; offering group accommodation in a unique way for up to 18 guests. Lily Cottage sleeps 2 and is next to the main house Riverside Cottage. Riverside Cottage will become the hub of your group activities with a large conservatory seating your whole group for dining, this sleeps 8 and has a fantastic garden with hot tub and a beautiful beck running by the side of the garden. Butterfly Cottage sleeps 6 and Tulip sleeps 2, the unique dynamic of being able to vacation together but have your own space is widely popular and a great way to holiday!
The four cottages have a shared garden and BBQ dining area just by the beck. They are set in 6½-acres of land, including woodland to explore at your leisure. With the changing seasons the woodland creates an ever-changing environment to be enjoyed. The bluebells create a carpet of blue in late Spring while the glorious colours of Autumn leaves are hard to beat. Guests will be delighted to spot that the grounds are often frequented by a wide variety of birds and wildlife including woodpecker, deer and hares.
Located in the ‘Gateway to The Lakes’ Low Jock Scar provides an ideal base for guests who are looking to explore. Whilst it may be difficult to drag yourselves away from this perfect spot, both The Lakes and Dales are easily accessible. Head east to Sedbergh, Dent and Hawes or west to Windermere and Bowness. Equally within easy reach for a day out are the Northern Lakes with Ullswater and Haweswater less than an hour’s drive. For guests looking to stay local, walks and cycle routes for all abilities can be found. Just a few miles away, the town of Kendal offers something for everyone. A popular historic market town, Kendal provides a castle, historic buildings and its famous ‘yards’, a riverside setting, shops for all and a great selection of pubs, cafes and restaurants to be enjoyed. Shop, pub and restaurant 5 miles.

This substantial detached holiday property is great for large families to enjoy. With a huge games room for the kids and for the adults, a hot tub set in the half-acre wrap around gardens, there is something to entertain everyone. Multiple living rooms and kitchens give you flexibility of living options. The owners have thought of everything for guest comfort from family rooms for those with little children, to a large number of bathrooms and TVs in every bedroom. Set in the centre of Halton Lea Gate, the property used to contain the village shop, this part of the house is now a spacious kitchen and dining area. The village borders the North Pennines Area of Oustanding Natural Beauty, with the famous Pennine Way walk being just to the east of the village. There are numerous walks, footpaths and cycle paths in and around the village to explore, as well as a children’s play area. On the boundary between Northumberland and Cumbria, there is a wealth of tourist attractions open to guests, including Hadrians Wall, RSPB Geltsdale Nature Reserve and Alston, England’s highest market town. long_description:
Welcoming larger family groups offering accommodation for up to fourteen people. Within expansive grounds approaching three acres, offering a perfect retreat for relaxation. The pet friendly accommodation welcomes up to five dogs, having a fully enclosed one-acre dog field allows pets to roam freely and safely, giving owners’ peace of mind while their furry companions explore without the risk of escape. The landscaped lawns provide ample space for outdoor activities, whether it’s a friendly game of football, a relaxing afternoon picnic, or simply enjoying the open air. Covered BBQ area offer an ideal setting for al fresco dining, no matter the weather.
Blending rustic charm with modern comforts, this large property combines two charming cottages and a first floor apartment; allowing everyone to retain their privacy, while still having shared spaces to gather and make memories together. The surrounding landscape enhances the sense of seclusion, creating a tranquil haven where you can unwind in nature’s embrace. Comfy sofas, a wood burner, and Netflix-equipped TV’s offer great ingredients to relax. Boasting in total seven bedrooms and five bathrooms; two ground floor bedrooms both with shower cubicles offers step-free access, and upstairs four bedrooms with two bathrooms, and a further bedroom and bathroom located in the apartment, accessed via external staircase. Outside you have seating patios with BBQ’s, Two hot tubs, each seats up to six people, to soak with bubbles and jets, under a sky full of stars.
An excellent location to discover both Suffolk and Norfolk. Wonderful market towns of Bungay, 9 minutes’ drive and Beccles, 16 minutes’ drive, where the River Waveney passes through, for great riverside walks, and waterside boating activities. Each offer independent boutiques and chain shops, an excellent collection of eateries including fine dining, to many cafés serving homemade cakes and savouries. Visit the weekly markets, which are excellent for all things local, should you wish to enjoy a night of cooking and dining in.
Beccles is also home to the lido open-air heated swimming pool, seasonal opening, booking recommended. The quintessential town of Southwold, with its pier and sandy beach, numerous shops, pubs and restaurants. Coastal town of Aldeburgh has a good selection of restaurants, serving fresh seafood, and shops.
Market town of Framlingham with magnificent 12th Century castle and parkland offer a historic treat for all. Saturday and Tuesday markets for local produce, together with trinkets and collectibles. Shops, boutiques, antiques, cafes, pubs and restaurants. Visit the cathedral city of Norwich, 21 miles, for culture, theatre, castle museum, plenty of eateries, excellent shopping opportunities and a market square. Supermarkets, shops and pub serving good food, 4.9 miles. Beach 13 miles.

reviews.comment: We have just returned from a week in Chestnut Barns with a group of 9 including. 4 children aged 9-15. They all agreed it was the best holiday accommodation in Suffolk that we have had over 5 years! We hired the whole place-2 adjoining cottages and a 2 person flat. Claire and Scott were lovely hosts and made our stay a very enjoyable and easy experience. Their small dogs Atticus and Bear were so well trained and welcoming that the grandchildren loved them. The outside space was perfect for four keen footballers who also enjoyed the badminton and pickle ball games with plenty of space for other games. The accommodation was ideal and the flat was only used as a space for two of our group to work without distractions on a couple of days. The hot tub was large and cleaned daily and the accommodation would have was easily accessible and could have accommodated 2 more couples. Claire and Scott were really helpful with ideas of where to eat and explore and we are very grateful to them.

It was a fantastic place and so lovely to be greeted and seen off by the extremely friendly owners.  The whole family had a wonderful time, including the dogs. There is stacks of space for everyone, the BBQ s excellent as were the hot tubs, childrens play area. the two dogs had a great time playing in the dog paddock with the owners dogs. Other than ourselves it was an exceeding nice change to be in the peaceful country side with just the birds and nature.  Weather could have been a bit warmer but that did not stop us enjoying our surroundings. The party was made up of an 80 year old right down to 3 months. A holiday will all remember with fondness.  and hope to go again some time.

name: Elm Farmhouse
short_description: A charming period farmhouse set within 65 acres of thriving Devon countryside, offering an intimate retreat for families or friends to unwind, celebrate, and enjoy the beauty of the outdoors.
long_description: The farmhouse has been lovingly renovated by its owner, who is passionate about wildlife, sustainable farming, and creating a place where guests can escape everyday life and reconnect with nature. It offers a luxurious retreat for families and groups, perfect for socialising, celebrating, or even hosting an intimate wedding in the stunning Devon countryside. While the surrounding natural habitats remain beautifully wild, the interior is elegantly designed, with cosy sofas, open fires—including an inglenook—and a welcoming kitchen for gathering over food and conversation. Enjoy relaxed country living with days spent playing garden games or savouring barbecues, and evenings around the piano or toasting marshmallows over the firepit under Exmoor’s star-filled skies. When you wish to venture out, the village of Bampton, with its shops and pub, is just a short drive away.

name: Celestria
short_description: A unique large countryside retreat with hot tub, sauna and games room, perfect for group gatherings in a striking setting surrounded by Yorkshire scenery.
long_description:
Set in the North Yorkshire countryside, this striking and spacious retreat offers a memorable setting for large gatherings, celebrations and special occasions. Combining the character of a historic building with bold contemporary design, it provides a unique place to stay, surrounded by open grounds and within easy reach of scenic walks and local attractions.
Inside, the sense of space is immediate, with high ceilings and large windows allowing light to pour in throughout the day. The heart of the house is the impressive open-plan kitchen and dining area, where a substantial table invites everyone to come together for long, sociable meals. A central island and range cooker make catering for a group feel effortless, whether preparing food yourselves or enjoying a relaxed evening in. A separate preparation kitchen and utility room provide additional space and practicality, particularly for larger groups. The interiors are thoughtfully curated, with an eclectic collection of modern artwork adding personality and interest to each room.
Designed with entertaining in mind, there are several spaces to suit every mood. A dedicated games and social room provides plenty of options for fun, while a more intimate sitting room with an open fire offers a quieter place to unwind. A separate bar area adds to the sense of occasion, ideal for pre-dinner drinks or late evening conversations.
The accommodation has been carefully designed with flexibility in mind. There are six beautifully appointed bedrooms, each featuring a zip-and-link super-king-size bed that can be configured as twin single beds on request, making the property ideal for a variety of group arrangements. Two of the bedrooms benefit from en-suite bathrooms, while the remaining bedrooms are served by two stylish house bathrooms, ensuring ample facilities for larger groups. To enhance your stay, robes and dedicated hot tub towels are provided for every guest.
Outside, the generous grounds offer room to explore and relax, with a hot tub and sauna providing the perfect way to recharge after a day out. With its blend of comfort, style and space, this is a distinctive countryside escape where groups can come together and make lasting memories.

name: Fieldside
short_description: A spacious dog-friendly barn conversion for 12 in North Yorkshire, with six bedrooms, a private hot tub and wide views across Coverdale and the Dales.
long_description:
Set amid rolling North Yorkshire countryside, this newly converted stone barn is a generous rural base for families and groups exploring the Yorkshire Dales. With wide views across Coverdale, towards Middleham and beyond, the setting feels wonderfully open and peaceful, while still placing guests within reach of characterful market towns, walking routes and days out through Wensleydale and the surrounding dales. Sleeping up to 12 guests across six bedrooms, it is well suited to special get-togethers, relaxed celebrations and shared holidays with plenty of space for everyone to settle in.
Inside, the barn has been thoughtfully converted to create a warm, sociable home with a contemporary country feel. Original stone character sits alongside comfortable furnishings and calm, tasteful styling, giving the interiors an inviting balance of old and new. The spacious living and dining areas make it easy to gather together after a day outdoors, whether that means lingering over a meal, planning the next walk or simply enjoying an unhurried evening in. The bedrooms offer restful spaces for guests to retreat to, making the property practical for mixed generations, friends or several families travelling together.
The accommodation comprises six spacious bedrooms, all located on the first floor. Each bedroom features a zip-and-link super-king-size bed that can be configured as twin single beds on request, providing excellent flexibility for a variety of group arrangements. Two of the bedrooms benefit from en-suite bathrooms, while the remaining bedrooms are served by two additional first-floor house bathrooms, ensuring plenty of facilities for larger groups.
Outside, the views take centre stage. The dog-friendly outdoor areas provide space for relaxed mornings, fresh-air lunches and evenings under the big Yorkshire sky, with the private hot tub adding a lovely way to unwind at the end of the day. From here, guests can discover the lanes, villages and sweeping landscapes of the Yorkshire Dales, with Middleham and the wider Wensleydale area offering plenty to explore. It is a welcoming countryside escape for memorable group stays in a beautiful corner of North Yorkshire.

long_description:
Ravines is situated in a prime position in Scarborough, just a short walk from the North Bay. Ravines is two houses which can be let as one so a party of 24 people can enjoy holidaying together but still have your own space, with each house having 6 bedrooms and sleeping 12 guests. All the bedrooms have TVs and en-suite facilities, and the icing on the cake are the enclosed hot tubs in the courtyard!
The town and shops are within walking distance with a great indoor shopping centre and lots of boutiques, and for those who prefer the nightlife, there are plenty of bars, restaurants, clubs and a casino. Just around the corner is the Scarborough cricket ground where the famous Scarborough Festival is held each year, an end of season competition featuring Yorkshire County Cricket Club. For those who love a faster sport, there’s Oliver’s Mount racing track with high powered road race bikes. As you walk to the beach you pass one of the entrances to Peasholm Park. Take a detour and walk around the park with its stunning gardens, lakes and waterfalls. There are boats and pedalos, and in summer, a brass band to entertain you. The park is famous for the Naval Warfare Battle where model ships re-enact a battle on the lake. It’s great entertainment for the kids and has been for the last 80 years.
One of the best things about Scarborough is that it has two bays, quite different from each other. The South Bay is a traditional seaside resort with donkeys, amusements and shops, whereas the North Bay is much quieter and more relaxed. Half way between the two bays, the castle stands proud on the cliffs above. You can walk the full length of Marine Drive from North to South Bay and it’s nice and flat making it easy for that evening stroll. If you prefer, there are the open top buses that run along the seafront. At the far end of North Bay is the Sealife Centre and the open air theatre, one of the largest outdoor theatres in Europe where international acts play during the summer.
Further down the coast is Filey, Flamborough and Bridlington. The RSPB bird sanctuary at Bempton is worth a visit where you can see puffins in their natural habitat. North of Scarborough are the beautiful North York Moors, and Whitby, a bustling fishing town famous for Whitby Jet Jewellery and the Goth weekends. You are only an hour away from York, a beautiful medieval city where you can visit the Railway Museum, take a leisure cruise on the river or walk the city walls which surround it. Beach 700 yards. Shop and restaurant 200 yards, pub 400 yards.

reviews.comment: excellent family break

We booked the two houses for a family reunion weekend. Both houses were spacious clean and well equipped. Parking permits were provided for the on street parking, although parking spaces were difficult to get at times. However the location was great and everything we needed really was within walking distance. There were bus stops close (5 min walk) which regularly went up and down between north and south bay and the number 100 went hourly in a circular route to the sealife centre. North Bay Fish and chips just down the road did amazing chips but closed at 7.30pm which we thought was a little early for a Friday in late July. Peasholm park was lovely and only a few mins walk away and we could hear Tom Jones from here as he performed at the open air theatre opposite. The castle is well worth a visit as views from here are amazing. We did have issues with the hot water which we managed to get sorted via the helpline number. The hot tubs were a great option but found them a little on the cool side with no obvious way of manually increasing the temperature. We loved the fact that each room had its own en-suite and TV. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay here but please be aware that the seagulls wake up very early!!

Went for my 60th birthday to celebrate with all my children and grandkids, thetr was 22 of us, both houses were lovely, had everything you needed our stay. The bathrooms in every bedroom was a hit with everyone. Hot tubs were good. Plenty of room. Locatuon was perfect walking distance of both beaches with young children in tow. Would definitely recommend, and would stay again in the future.

long_description:
Tapestry House is a spacious mid terrace property situated on a quiet side street just a two-minute walk from the beach in the bustling harbour town of Bridlington on the stunning Yorkshire coast. This spacious holiday home offers both a private hot tub and sauna and is ideal for families or a group of friends wishing to enjoy a traditional seaside holiday. The accommodation is spread over three floors and retains some of the original features including the beautifully tiled entrance hall floor. The light and airy rooms of are traditionally furnished, showcasing some of the artwork collected from the owner’s travels around the world, and decorated to a high standard offering a very comfortable holiday home. The sitting room is spacious and offers a large bay window. The deep filled sofas are ideally placed to gather on an evening and enjoy a TV night or perhaps a competitive board game. An open arch takes you through to the dining room which offers plenty of seating for twelve and is decorated in dark shades and with an electric wood burning stove. A piano sits to one side and there are shelves packed with books should you wish to enjoy a quiet read during your visit. The kitchen is a delight and offers a large range cooker with gas hob and oven. There is also a host of appliances including a washing machine, tumble dryer and dishwasher. There is plenty of work top space from which to prepare a delicious picnic to enjoy on the beach or perhaps cook up a feast to enjoy together on an evening. A toilet can also be found tucked away to complete the ground floor accommodation. On an evening take the stairs to the upper floors where you will find six bedrooms over two floors. All individually styled with Freeview TV in five of the bedrooms. On the first floor a single bedroom doubles as a study and a door leads out onto an unexpected balcony with seating and the luxury of a private sauna. A further double and kingsize, sea view, and house shower room sit across the hall. On the second floor are two further doubles and a family three room styled for children. A further bathroom completes the accommodation. Outside, there is off road parking for three cars and a small enclosed decked courtyard with hot tub. Enjoy a lazy afternoon in the bubbles or take a dip at night and watch the night sky.
The town of Bridlington offers miles of golden sands and a lovely promenade which leads to the historic harbour. Close by is the Spa Theatre with an excellent entertainment programme throughout the summer months, whilst the town centre has a good array of shops, pubs, cafés and restaurants. A short drive out of town is the RSPB reserve at Bempton and wonderful cliff top walks at Flamborough Head, whilst nearby are various historic houses and gardens such as Burton Agnes Hall and Sewerby Hall. The unspoilt rolling hills of the Yorkshire Wolds offer a plethora of walking and cycling opportunities whilst the Cultural City of Hull and ancient walled City of York are both under an hour#s drive away. Tapestry House makes an ideal base from which to explore this wonderful part of Yorkshire.

long_description:
Gas central heating (underfloor in kitchen/dining room), gas, electricity, bed linen, towels and Wi-Fi included. Initial logs for wood burner included. Travel cot. Welcome pack. Games room with table football, dartboard, a selection of games and 65" Smart TV. Enclosed, lawned front garden with garden furniture. Large, rear decked area with garden furniture and gas barbecue. Table tennis. Mini putting green (bring own putters and balls). Hot tub for 4 (private, £100 paid to owner). Sauna (private). Private parking for 6+ cars. No smoking. Please note: Sorry, no hen or stag parties. There are 10 steps and an unfenced pond in the garden. This property has a security deposit of £500.

Brackenwood is a distinguished and spacious, six-bedroomed period house with a separate two-bedroom cottage annexe, located on the beautiful Wirral Peninsula. In a prominent elevated position, it borders extensive areas of natural beauty with direct access to the beautiful woodlands of Caldy Hill. Offering far-reaching views, the property is detached and gated with CCTV making it private and secure. Filled with as much history as it has character and charm, it offers flexible and usable accommodation. The main house covers three levels, is beautifully presented, and luxuriously modernised to match the needs of today’s living. Upon entering via the original period front door, the grand entrance hall opens to a spacious sitting room where there’s a Fendi chaise lounge, comfy sofas, Smart TV, parquet flooring and beautiful Persian rugs. Next door is a spacious bedroom with a super kingsize bed and an elegant oak desk. The impressive underfloor heated kitchen/diner is based around a quartz top centre island and is a foodie’s dream. There are three inbuilt fridges (including a bespoke drinks fridge), plus a large larder freezer - perfect for entertaining. The AEG ovens and microwave are at eye level and self-cleaning; there’s a Nespresso coffee machine and an Alexa. The large dining table and soft seating space is flooded with natural light thanks to huge bi-fold doors, and the utility houses a Miele washing machine and tumble dryer. Finally there’s a downstairs toilet.
On the first floor is the master suite with super kingsize bed, sofa seating and TV. It has a vast en-suite with stand-alone bath and power shower. There are three further double bedrooms, of which one is en-suite, and the main family bathroom. The second floor boasts another luxurious bedroom with sky lights and en-suite facilities, and many of the bedrooms can be offered as twin upon request. All beds have pocket sprung luxury mattresses with 200-thread-count cotton linen, and duvets and pillows are ethically sourced goose/duck down.
The luxurious two-bedroom cottage was newly converted in 2023 and sleeps four guests in two double bedrooms. Finished to a high specification throughout, it includes a luxury bathroom with walk-in shower. The showroom kitchen is fully equipped making it completely self-contained; it’s modern, elegant, and comfortable.
The extensive landscaped grounds are equally impressive and offer the ultimate outdoor experience. The spacious sun terrace overlooks the Wirral Peninsula and includes a hot tub, sauna, outdoor ping pong and XL gas BBQ and grill. The gardens have been lovingly maintained and play host to different feature patio areas. There’s a delightful putting green designed by the Head Greenkeeper at Royal Liverpool Golf Club, that meanders down to a secluded fish pond, and the rear gardens enjoy a swing set for children and can be enclosed for both children and pets.
Brackenwood resides in a hugely popular location in the prestigious village of Caldy, a mere mile from the many attractions and services of West Kirby, including a fabulous array of beaches. West Kirby boasts the historic Hilbre Islands, the stunning Marine Lake and numerous boutique shops, restaurants and bars. The Wirral has an excellent range of leisure pursuits within its vicinity including sailing on the Dee Estuary, golf at the Royal Liverpool Golf Club and horse racing at Chester and Aintree. The cities of Liverpool and Chester provide a metropolitan range of shopping, restaurants and nightlife. On the recreational front there’s four Premier League football clubs in the region, rugby, cricket, and tennis clubs, and at Oulton Park there’s a motor racing circuit. Pub within a mile.

long_description:
Brockholme Barns offer a range of two converted barns sleeping from 10 to 12 guests with a holiday home for larger groups or families. Ideally situated in open farmland with grounds that overlook Hornsea Mere (the largest freshwater lake in Yorkshire), the semi-detached barns, Barley Edge with an attached cottage, and The Granary form part of a shared gravelled courtyard, and make the perfect retreat for families.
The rural setting is an excellent base for exploring east Yorkshire’s magnificent coastline with its wealth of sandy beaches, RSPB bird reserves, and traditional seaside towns of Hornsea, Bridlington, Filey and Scarborough with activities for all ages. Within walking distance is Honeysuckle Farm, a great day out for children, offering delicious ice cream and cart rides. You can also visit Wassand Hall, a grand Regency house and walled garden (open on selected days), and Hornsea Mere which has over 250 species of birds, a café and opportunities for sailing, fishing or feeding the ducks and swans.
Hornsea, 1 mile, offers beaches, promenade, a leisure complex, golf course, museum, skate park, the retail outlet Hornsea Freeport, Bugtopia The Zoo, pubs and restaurants; it’s also the end/start point of the Trans-Pennine Trail, where guests can hire electric bikes at an exclusive discount. Other local attractions include water sport activities and clay pigeon shooting at Brandesburton, 4 miles, and the the medieval town of Beverley, 10 miles, which boasts an attractive blend of past and present with its 13th-century minster, boutiques, bistros, polo club and renowned racecourse. The harbour and spa entertainment centre in Bridlington is 14 miles away, while The Deep, a spectacular aquarium, maritime museum and marina, are all located in Hull, ‘City of Culture 2017’, 15 miles away. Also within easy reach is Bempton Cliffs RSPB Reserve with its spectacular colonies of sea birds and the many stately homes in the area at Burton Agnes, Burton Constable, Sledmere House and Sewerby Hall. Travel a little further and you’ll find the historic city of York, where you can learn more about the Vikings at the Jorvik Viking Centre or head north and go cycling at Dalby Forest. Shop, pub and restaurant 1 mile.
The properties can be booked together to accommodate up to 22 guests.

reviews.comment: All communication with Ryan before we arrived was great and we received a warm welcome from Rachel.  The property was spotlessly clean when we arrived and it had a very comfortable feel to it. This was a family celebration with three families and as grandparents it was great to have access to the annex!   Barley Edge was very spacious with lots of rooms with quiet spaces as well as great sized family rooms.  We had everything that we needed to eat in and bbq outside.  The hot tub was a bonus and you have to do the usual glass of bubbles whilst in there - plastic glasses available as well as steps to place them on!The children had a whale of a time playing football on the large grass area where there was a safe route from the barn. The location was great - surrounded by farmland and you wake to a beautiful sun rise. Also very quiet!We would all happily go there again and thoroughly recommend a stay.
It was a great place to stay

A smashing location with easy reach to Beverley Hornsea Bridlington and Hull.Ideal for a large party, we were 11 in the end and it worked well. The adaption is excellent and retains the character of the farm buildings, like the rounded corners on pillars I remember so well. The  equipment  was all good, and the instructions were in a folder in the kitchen cupboard.The sitting room was ideal for us all to congregate in the evening and the beds were really very comfortable. Everything was spotless when we entered the cottage.We had a great walk round Hornsea and I was able to show my family, my roots, and behind the scenes. WE spent an afternoon at the cricket field up Atwick road which was lovely, where I cut the grass as a boy

long_description:
Sinatra Villa is the ultimate celebration house that accommodates up to sixteen guests. Get the family together and round up your friends for the ultimate weekend. Sitting proudly in one of the best tree-lined postcodes in Cheltenham, Sinatra Villa is spread over four floors, with eight luxurious bedrooms, seven bathrooms, and a cavern bar and cinema room. Off the main entrance hall on the ground floor, you have a large formal dining room that features a glittering chandelier and direct access to a large kitchen; why not celebrate in style and request Sinatra’s private chef to create a memorable dining experience for all? There are two sitting rooms on the ground floor, a formal sitting room, and the second within the self-contained two bedroom apartment suite.
On the first and second floors you will find six kingsize bedrooms, five of which are en-suite and one large family bathroom that features a whirlpool bath. Outside you have a large garden that’s great for summer soirées, barbecues and garden games. If relaxation is more on your agenda, take a dip in the bubbling hot tub, followed by a steam room. Morning, noon and night you can keep the party going, as based on the lower ground floor, is Sinatra’s very own cavern bar. It boasts a 4K UHD TV with top specification surround sound, karaoke system, a bar area with seating, and a piano (piano is only available by prior agreement). There is also another basement room that has a pool table and table tennis.
If you want to venture beyond your magnificent pad, you are a short stroll from Montpelier Boulevard, where designer shops, uber cool cocktail bars and restaurants are in abundance. For a truly Cotswold experience, why not hop in the car for a short drive to Bourton-on-the-Water, Chipping Campden and Painswick, where honey-hued houses and quintessential English tearooms await you.

Oil central heating, electricity, bed linen and Wi-Fi included. Cot and 2 highchairs available on request. Welcome pack. Large lawned garden with sitting-out area and garden furniture. Hot tub for 8 (private, open until 11pm). Private parking for 10 cars. No smoking. Please note: There is an unfenced pond in the grounds, 45 yards away. Fireworks are not allowed in the garden. Couples and family bookings only, no stag or hen parties. 3 steps to property. Hot tub for 8 people, open until 11 pm. Pond 45 yards, care to be taken with young children. No fireworks allowed. Bed linen and towels provided, bring your towels for the hot tub. There is a £350 security deposit.

Doves Barn dates back to the 16th century and is a detached, Grade II listed barn, brimming with charm and character. Boasting original oak beams and timeless charm, yet perfectly mixed with modern day comforts. There is a vaulted ceiling criss-crossed with exposed beams in the living room, and the large inglenook with wood burner to provide the warmest of invites. There are eight bedrooms in total, including two galleried bedrooms. With plenty of space for guests to celebrate a special occasion, and yet still have the opportunity to enjoy the escape from everyday life pressures, and simply sit back and relax in the peaceful surroundings. Nestled within two acres of extensive grounds, Doves Barn offers spacious accommodation that is well furnished for comfort and enjoyment. Relax and enjoy your own eight person hot tub and a large courtyard garden with a choice of two patios, great for those al fresco dining opportunities. Whatever the season, Doves Barn will provide you and your guests with the warmest of welcomes.
This is a great location that is close to all the necessary amenities and an excellent base to explore the rolling countryside and unspoilt coastline. The area offers good bird watching, walking, and cycling opportunities. Needham Market is just 1 mile away, a pretty small town, rich with its historic roots in the wool industry. Bury St. Edmunds is 19 miles away and is a shoppers’ paradise with an abundance of shops in the picturesque medieval streets, and elegant Georgian squares along with award-winning restaurants, fantastic annual festivals, family entertainment, stunning parks, cafés and a Georgian theatre. Ipswich is 12 miles away with its town centre and pretty harbour. There are local train links to London and Bury St. Edmunds. Visit Suffolk’s stunning Heritage Coast which includes the popular seaside town of Aldeburgh with its great choice of eating establishments and shops, the intriguing village of Dunwich, a peaceful haven for wildlife with its beautiful heathland and the popular coastal town of Southwold, the home to Adnams Brewery, with pubs, galleries, shops, lighthouse and beach huts. Beach 29 miles. Shop, pub and restaurant 1 mile.
Please note: There are open, steep, spiral or narrow stairs at the property.

With a beautiful setting on the Pyle Hall Farm estate, Gladices Barn is a luxury barn conversion set amidst 250 peaceful acres. With unspoilt scenery in every direction and dramatic views across to the West Wight coastline, this Isle of Wight home from home makes an unforgettable setting for a family gathering, group or corporate stay in the heart of the island’s countryside.
Beautifully converted, Gladices Barn is home to seven spacious en-suite bedrooms, and each one has been furnished to a standard that’ll take your breath away. Five of the bedrooms welcome their guests with super kingsize beds, and the bridal suite has a black-laquered four poster bed and matching console by an award-winning designer to make your stay extra special. Downstairs, the three reception rooms can be opened up to create one elegant 80 foot space – perfect for that special event.
Outside, you’ll find a large, one acre garden complete with an ever-so-inviting hot tub that makes the perfect place to sink beneath the bubbles and admire the views for a while. On warmer days, the barbecue makes it easy to enjoy the views while you dine al fresco, and the decked terrace means you can sit back and watch the herd of deer and stags in the nearby paddock.
A stay at Gladices Barn is a unique opportunity to embrace life on a working farm, and the resident herd of waygu cattle are always a delight to see as you set off for a wander along one of the nearby footpaths or bridleways. In fact, those of you keen to spot wildlife during your holiday will be in your element thanks to the pheasants, badgers, hares, cuckoos, corn bunting and red squirrel that call the area home.
Located on the south east coast of the Isle of Wight in a designated Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, Gladices Barn offers guests a tranquil, rural setting with an abundance of activities on the doorstep. For those looking for action, try surfing at Compton Bay or for a slower pace enjoy one of the many scenic inland or coastal walks. Gladices Barn is an ideal base for a relaxing holiday with family or friends or a wonderful venue for a special celebration or even an intimate wedding reception. Corporate events are also catered for and provide an alternative venue for off-site meetings or team building activities. A fine selection of local food and drink can also be arranged for your special event.

reviews.comment: I can’t believe you’ve received no negative reviews for Gladices Barn. The place, and the owner, were lovely but the photographs on the listing must be more than ten years old - I've determined it was built around 2012. As a facility it was perfect but it simply hasn't been adequately maintained. The owner was as helpful as he could be (we had a major electrical failure) but he wasn't going to be able to replace matresses, showers, and kitchen appliances while we were there. It's a real shame and I believe these properties should be inspected annually to ensure their quality is maintained.

If you are a large group looking to spend some quality family time, away from the hustle bustle of the city, this is the place for you.Its a mini mansion that has 7 en-suites plus a common bathroom, large living and dining space, huge well equipped kitchen and a 6 seater hot tub having distant sea views. A bit pricy but worth the money if you are looking for something secluded.enough car spaces for 4-5 cars.Owner was super friendly and helpful and guided us well.Next to the barn is an enclosed space where owner has over 30 deer which could be spotted from the living room patio.  Nearest convenience is 10 mins drive so having own car is kind of essential and a bit of pre planning is advised.All in all, we loved our stay here.

Was perfect for our needs.  The barn was huge, with lovely big rooms and en suite bathrooms.  It was wonderful for our family gathering - the children loved seeing the deer.  Michael our host was very welcoming and was contactable throughout our stay.   The hot tub was a real treat.  With a little more attention to the outside spaces Gladices Barn would be amazing

name: Catterick House
short_description: Large village townhouse beside the green, sleeping up to 14, with a garden hot tub, private sauna, games room and space for group meals, plus room for up to three dogs.
long_description:
Set beside the village green, this roomy townhouse is designed for big celebrations and easy get-togethers, sleeping up to 14 guests across three floors. With plenty of shared space and a choice of quiet corners, it works well for multi-generational breaks, birthdays and long weekends with friends. Up to three dogs are welcome too, so no one needs to miss out on the fun.
Step inside to find generous, sociable rooms that make group holidays feel straightforward. Two kitchens mean you can spread out at meal times, while the dining room is ready for long, lingering suppers. When it is time to unwind, there are comfortable sitting rooms with open fires, ideal for chats, board games and a good film. Sleeping is arranged across seven bedrooms, with a mix of doubles and twins, and there are three bathrooms to help the morning routine tick along. A separate games room adds an extra layer of entertainment, with space for a friendly darts match and a round of snooker, and there is also a gym if you fancy keeping up your routine while away.
Outside, attractive gardens provide a welcoming backdrop for morning coffee and summer evenings. The patio is a lovely spot to gather, and the bubbling hot tub seats up to six, perfect after a day out. For an extra dose of indulgence, there is a private sauna where you can warm through before heading back to the house. Off-road parking for up to four cars helps take the stress out of arrivals, leaving you free to settle in, stock the fridge and start making memories together.
No smoking. This property has a £450 security deposit.

long_description:
The Old School House is a superb property situated in Horrabridge, on the edge of Dartmoor National Park.
It’s an extremely spacious 5000 square foot, late-Victorian former schoolhouse, built in 1875 of local stone and slate. This beautiful seven-bedroom holiday home comfortably accommodates up to twenty two guests and presents a wonderful base for a group of family and friends to enjoy a luxurious and relaxing break. The property showcases two hot tubs, six bathrooms, bath tubs lavishly positioned in two of the bedrooms, a games room, large garden, and a children’s play area. The main part of the building on the ground floor has a magnificent large kitchen and dining area with seating for up to twenty guests, an island worktop, exquisite quartz countertops and plenty of appliances. Other features include a pantry, boot room, cloakroom, the enormous living room with two large seating areas and a wood burner, patio doors opening out into the garden and a games room with a pool table and dartboard.
The annexed area at the far end can be accessed through a connecting hallway or via a separate entrance and it contains an additional open plan kitchen, living and dining area, a shower room and a staircase leading to the two bedrooms above. This beautiful, detached home has three staircases in total leading to the first floor which divides two bedrooms at the far end for eight guests, the extraordinary master ensuite bedroom in the middle for a couple and the other three bedrooms at the other end accommodating up to twelve guests. The final en-suite double bedroom is located on the ground floor. The private enclosed garden has a large lawn, a sprawling decked area, barbeque, outdoor seating, children’s play area, plus a large shed for all outdoor activity equipment. In front of the property is a large parking area with space for up to eight vehicles plus a covered carport.
Horrabridge is a beautiful village with a village green and medieval bridge on the banks of the River Walkham. It is serviced by a selection of shops including a post office and stores, bakery, fish and chip shop, art gallery and two pubs. Tavistock, a nearby thriving market town rich in history and tradition dating back to the 10th century, just 3½ miles away to the northwest.
Please note: There are open, steep, spiral or narrow stairs at the property.

long_description:
Get ready for some fantastic memories. This magnificent Grade II listed Victorian Gothic mansion set beside Lake Windermere makes the perfect venue for large family get togethers, special occasions and surprise celebrations. Set in private grounds with lawned gardens and only a 5-minute walk to Bowness-On-Windermere, this place is simply unforgettable. High ceilings and stunning features offer a glimpse of its Victorian heritage. Following a stylish renovation, the impressive Fallbarrow Hall features the latest in interior design and contemporary fashion.
Featuring fifteen spacious en-suite bedrooms, plus two apartments with three additional bedrooms. You’ll find the combination of rooms, beds, and flexible sleeping arrangements ideal for an amazing holiday with up to 36 of your friends and loved ones. The themed bedrooms, sumptuous furnishings and luxurious surroundings are just the treat you’re looking for. Kick back in the jazzy cocktail bar or unwind while you catch the latest entertainment in the TV lounge. Enjoy some quiet time in the library or take in a movie in the cinema room. Take on your mates at pool or table tennis, while the little ones chill out in the kid’s den. Whether it’s a cosy night in or a much-needed family reunion you’re after, this place has it covered.
During the day, the large windows flood the area with plenty of daylight and great views of the grounds and gardens. If you’re planning a special meal, there’s a stunning dining room big enough to host an amazing banquet and you can easily get everyone together. The large kitchen is well equipped and provides a social and communal hub with all the cooking facilities you need. There is a utility and laundry room, ideal for walking gear and muddy boots, and plenty more to explore when you get here. Outside you can enjoy a large expanse of gardens with views of Lake Windermere.
Fallbarrow Hall is in a private and secluded area of Fallbarrow Holiday Park which features The Willow, a fine dining restaurant and cocktail bar, a marina with direct access to the lake, an adventure playground, and sports courts for the kids. Turn right from the park entrance and in 5 minutes’ you are in the popular tourist magnet of Bowness-On-Windermere with an abundance of shops, pubs, bars, and restaurants offering every type of cuisine you could wish for. Here you can ride the steamers on Lake Windermere to Ambleside or Lakeside. Grab an ice cream, feed the ducks, hire a boat, play mini golf, or play in the arcades. There’s so much to do and of course you are in the heart of The Lake District National Park, so if you love the outdoors, you’re in the right place. Walkers, cyclists, climbers will be in their element. Look no further, you’ve found the place of your dreams!

Perfect for large family holidays or groups, Old Hall Barn is a detached, architect-designed barn conversion that can sleep up to fourteen guests in total comfort and luxury.
The heart of the property is the spectacular living space, with its original, vaulted oak-beamed ceiling that creates a vast space for family and friends to congregate. There’s a cosy seating area with a large inglenook fireplace as well as a pool table. There is also a well-equipped kitchen with everything you could need during your stay while the dining area has seating for 14 guests.
Downstairs you will also find a twin bedroom and a shower room as well as a separate cloakroom. The first floor consists of a spacious seating area – ideal for reading and relaxing with stunning countryside views as well as six double bedrooms and five bathrooms. Outside you will find a superb landscape garden with plenty of seating, barbecues and two top-of-the-range hot tubs.
With plenty of local footpaths and bridleways from which to explore the countryside, Old Hall Barn is the perfect location for a family holiday, yet within easy reach of some of Suffolk’s most historic destinations, beautiful countryside, unspoilt beaches and traditional market towns.
Old Hall Barn aims to provide the ideal combination of luxury, fun and relaxation. It will be ideal for families, groups or those seeking somewhere private – an ideal venue for a holiday, break or to celebrate a special occasion at any time of the year. Beach 3 miles, shop 1½ miles, pub/restaurant ¾ mile.

long_description: Boston House (’sister property’ to Alice Howe and Bannerrigg) is the perfect base for large groups of friends or families to take a holiday or a short break. The property sleeps 14 comfortably in 7 bedrooms, each bedroom has white cotton bedding and TV. Five of the bedrooms have en-suite shower rooms; the other two rooms have separate bathrooms, which means every bedroom has private facilities. For the romantics in your party there are two four poster beds and one half tester bed. The rear courtyard has a raised slate bed patio and a seven seater private hot tub. At the front of the property the car park has been expanded and there is parking for up to 6 cars. The kitchen has solid oak units, Lakeland slate work-tops, a 7 ring burner - twin oven range cooker, 46 bottle wine cooler and 8 seat central island unit. The lounge has a living flame gas fire, leather settees, larger flat screen TV, DVD player cinema surround sound system and a hifi. The fireplace designed by Pugin is believed to be a small-scale replica of the one he designed for Westminster palace. The dining room has a huge table perfect for entertaining a large group. New 14 seat cinema in the cellar with hi-def, Blu-Ray projector and proper fold down cinema seats. The rear courtyard is walled all round and is extremely private. There is a huge teak table and chairs sitting on a raised slate bed patio perfect for dining al fresco and its surrounding walls mean that it is well protected from the wind. At the front of the property there is a second patio with table and four chairs, which is a real suntrap - perfect for a quiet coffee! The house has private parking for up to 6 cars. As you would imagine the property has been thoughtfully decorated and furnished in keeping with its Grade II listed status. So if you’re looking for a house in the Lakes to celebrate a 30th, 40th, 50th, 60th or even 70th birthday Boston House is the ideal choice. You can view videos of this property and others on the street www.youtube.com/user/TheTerraceWindermere. This property can be booked together with Alice Howe (CC127187), Bannerrigg (CC127195), White Moss (CC127244) and Number One (CC127243) to accommodate up to 66 people in 30 bedrooms!

Set in the Exe Valley and very accessible from major roads, these three beautiful properties all offer the perfect holiday retreat. All or part of the complex can be booked for large groups, parties or family gatherings. It would make an ideal venue for a wedding, with facilities allowing up to 120 guests to attend, by arrangement. They each have their individual character including beams and most with wood burners. This fantastic property sleeps 44 guests across 16 bedrooms all accessed via five different staircases ensuring you have some privacy whilst still being able to gather for celebrations in the living areas. Catering and a chef is available to be booked directly with the owner.
With the River Exe, Devonshire Heartland, Somerset and the North Devon coastline on your doorstep, the properties are situated in an excellent countryside location offering a good base to explore the beautiful area and are within easy driving distance of Exmoor National Park and the Devon and Somerset border. Golf (TIVERTON GOLF COURSE) horse riding, cycling and fishing (WIMBLEBALL LAKE) are available locally, along with clay pigeon shooting and fly fishing. Alternatively, there are many delightful, scenic countryside walks nearby including the spectacular scenic coast between Minehead and Combe Martin. Tarr Steps, Dulverton, Tiverton Canal, Wimbleball Lake are all favourites for walks. Tiverton, 7 miles, offers a selection of shops, restaurants and pubs as well as the famous Grand Western Canal and Bickleigh Castle.
The nearest coast with sandy beaches and family attractions including Somerset World and West Somerset scenic steam railway is at the seaside resort of Minehead. The medieval town of Dunster with its magnificent castle, deer park and mill, and the historic cathedral city of Exeter with its variety of shops, restaurants, theatres, racecourse and the Maritime Museum, are both 20 miles away. Delightful Bickleigh, 8 miles, has lovely, thatched inns overlooking the river, and serving good food and local ales - the perfect location to get away from it all.
Taunton, Ilfracombe, Sidmouth, Seaton, Dawlish and Exmouth are within easy driving distance. National Trust properties within easy reach include Knightshayes Court, Powderham Castle and Castle Drogo to name a few. Bampton is 2 miles away, and sailing is available at nearby Wimbleball Lake. Shop 1½ miles, pubs 2 miles.
Please note: Duvale Barn has four kitchens making it ideal for families to stay together whilst still having plenty of space.

Our family weekend away at Duvale Barn was great. We found it tricky finding somewhere which catered to a big size (41 of us in total) so was excited to see Duvale Barn and it was a great match. Enough bedrooms for everyone (including en-suites), as well as living areas and kitchens for a comfortable stay. We managed group games in the big lounge but also time individually.The place was very clean - ideal when we had a busy weekend as no need to clean anything beforehand. We felt like the place was well looked afterIt was also well equipped. We didn’t need to bring much with us, as there was enough utilities, en-suites, and plenty of parking. The highlight was the play area outside for the kids who loved it! We had 3 babies under 2, so not having to pack our own high chairs and cots was handy as these were provided and good quality.The owners were helpful and great communicators. Helping us beforehand and meeting us there to explain.Overall, we loved our stay. Our family age ranged from 9 months to 74 years old and it was a great fit for the whole family. We’ve already mentioned returning in our future family holidays

Unspoilt, far-reaching views are sure to capture your heart, while the curation of playful patterns, pretty prints and carefully considered furnishings make for the most enchanting aesthetic.

Think traditional oak-beamed ceilings and open brickwork bejewelled with statement-making accessories and bewitching bold flashes. Sitting pretty beneath the skies, this open-air oasis welcomes you to plunge into its depths at your leisure, before warming up inside the super-toasty Finnish sauna.

Its sweeping steps and expansive veranda echo the Hamptons and coastal New England yet, set against the Cornish sky, it feels entirely unique — one of the most striking and distinctive properties in the area.
Elevated and gloriously south-facing, the sun-drenched deck becomes the heart of summer living. Outdoor sofas and sun loungers invite long, unhurried afternoons, while the gas barbecue sets the tone for relaxed feasts that stretch into golden evening light. The hot tub enjoys its own private deck — a secluded sanctuary beneath open skies — while below, another terrace nestles under the trees, offering generous dining and seating space wrapped in twinkling festoon lighting. As night falls, it glows softly and atmospherically; music hums, glasses clink, and time seems to slow.
Inside, Palm Court is a love letter to breezy American sophistication layered with warmth and personality. Natural materials — warm woods, woven bamboo and tactile jute — create a calm, unified backdrop. This is artfully enriched with vibrant contemporary pieces, vinyl records displayed on the walls, coffee-table books evoking Ibiza summers and surf culture, and personal artefacts gathered from around the world. There’s a confident nod to Ralph Lauren’s iconic interiors, blended seamlessly with the cosy ease of a ranch-style lodge. The white tongue-and-groove kitchen feels crisp and coastal, fresh and uplifting without a single nautical cliché in sight.
Sleeping up to twelve guests across six beautifully styled bedrooms, the house is thoughtfully designed for togetherness without compromising on comfort. Two en-suite king rooms offer indulgent privacy, alongside a ground-floor en-suite double, an additional double, a twin room and a playful bunk room that younger guests will adore. Four bathrooms in total ensure space and ease for everyone.
Bright, airy living spaces are layered in soft natural tones and textures, with bespoke furnishings that instantly encourage you to unwind. Two welcoming reception rooms, each with a feature open fire, provide the perfect setting after blustery coastal walks.
The spacious kitchen and dining area flow effortlessly onto the terrace and subtropical gardens, ideal for al fresco suppers or slow morning coffees. Add a games room with pool table, deep sofas for film nights, WiFi and Sonos sound throughout for good measure.
Beyond the house, Polperro brims with charm, from boutique shops and galleries to welcoming eateries and a rich smuggling and fishing heritage. Wander its narrow lanes, relax on the beach, or hike the Coast Path for breathtaking views. Nearby Looe offers sandy shores, boat trips and coastal trails — perfect for exploring Cornwall’s characterful coastline.
These can be booked together to accommodate up to 16 guests.
