long_description:
Set close to the western fringes of the Lake District National Park, Dunningwell Hall offers a memorable countryside retreat designed for special gatherings, celebrations and relaxing getaways. Built in 1876 and carefully restored, the stately Victorian mansion blends historic character with modern comfort. Located just outside the national park boundary, the hall enjoys the peace and space of the surrounding countryside while still providing easy access to some of the Lake District’s most spectacular landscapes. The property sits within a tranquil 26-acre estate of gardens and woodland, creating a sense of privacy and calm from the moment you arrive.
The property is particularly well suited to larger groups. Sleeping up to 22 guests across 11 beautifully designed ensuite bedrooms, Dunningwell Hall provides the perfect setting for extended families, multiple families travelling together, special events, celebrations or even small business retreats and meetings. Spacious communal areas encourage guests to spend time together, with elegant lounges, two dining rooms, a snooker room and a fully equipped kitchen ideal for shared meals and social occasions.
There are also plenty of ways to relax and enjoy time together without leaving the estate. Guests can unwind in the 16-seater outdoor hot tub, enjoy lawn games in the gardens, play board games or make use of the Xbox for family entertainment. With scenic walks through the grounds and plenty of peaceful corners to sit and enjoy the countryside, the hall offers a wonderful balance of social space and quiet relaxation.
Dunningwell Hall is also perfectly placed for exploring the quieter and more dramatic landscapes of the western Lake District. Families can easily visit Wast Water, England’s deepest lake, renowned for its breathtaking scenery and peaceful shoreline. Surrounded by dramatic mountains, it is an ideal place for lakeside picnics, gentle walks or simply taking in one of the most striking landscapes in the country.
For those who enjoy adventure, the nearby Scafell Pike — England’s highest mountain — offers a rewarding challenge for walkers, while lower routes and valley trails nearby provide family-friendly walks with stunning views. The western fells are often quieter than the central lakes, making them perfect for exploring at a relaxed pace.
Within easy reach is the picturesque village of Coniston and the beautiful Coniston Water, where visitors can enjoy lakeside walks, boat trips, welcoming cafés and opportunities for kayaking or paddleboarding. With dramatic mountains, tranquil lakes and countless outdoor activities nearby, Dunningwell Hall provides an exceptional base for groups looking to experience the very best of the Lake District together.

long_description:
This spacious house situated in the heart of the popular resort of Blackpool boasts six en-suite bedrooms alongside a small private spa and hot tub, making it a perfect escape for a getaway with a large group of friends or your extended family. There is a contemporary dining room, along with a very well- equipped kitchen offering added touches of convenience, including also being equipped with cocktail shakers and martini glasses! A sumptuous living room creates the perfect place to relax at the end of a busy day exploring the town and area. The property also benefits from a ground floor small wellness spa with an infra-red sauna, body tropical jet shower and a steam cabinet. Outside there is a spacious decked area housing a large hot tub with a roof cover, so can be used all year round.
The property is located in the heart of Blackpool, a vibrant coastal town on the northwest coast of England, with a kaleidoscope of entertainment and attractions that cater to a diverse range of tastes and interests and is an all-year round centre for fun. The famous Pleasure Beach boasts a myriad of adrenaline-pumping rides, including the world-famous Big One roller coaster. The Winter Gardens is an architectural gem, hosting a variety of events from concerts to theatrical productions. Why not visit the Blackpool Tower? This symbol of the town is a must-visit landmark, offering panoramic vistas from its observation deck.
Along the historic Blackpool Promenade visitors can stroll along the sandy beaches, taking in the invigorating sea breeze and marvelling at the stunning views of the Irish Sea, or after sunset, take a trip to Blackpool Illuminations, boasting a dazzling light display that graces the promenade providing a captivating spectacle. Additionally, Blackpool’s rich cultural scene includes art galleries, museums, and the Grand Theatre, ensuring there’s something for everyone in this lively and dynamic seaside destination. Beach 400 yards. Shop and restaurant 200 yards, pub 100 yards.

long_description:
Come and enjoy a stay in the country at Linden Lodge. You’ll find a large dining table, perfect for bringing in a private chef.

Linden Lodge is in a great location, situated in the village of Wick, a perfect holiday base for those who wish to explore the many attractions Wiltshire has to offer, or stay in and enjoy the house and its features.
The house and annexe sleep twenty-six people. The house has five bedrooms, an annexe with two more bedrooms, a living room, a thirty-seater dining table, a fully equipped kitchen with two ovens, and four bathrooms. In the garden you will find a games room, two hot tubs and a BBQ area. There is adequate parking for up to 10 cars.
Bath and Bristol are both less than 10 miles away and under a 20-minute drive, and within a short drive are the picturesque villages of Lacock and Castle Combe, both favourite locations for TV and film directors. Lacock features in Harry Potter, Downton Abbey and Pride and Prejudice, and Castle Combe was the backdrop for War Horse.
Experience the Georgian city of Bath, only 7 miles away by car. With its famous architecture, the Jane Austen Centre, and thermal spa (Thermae), the city offers something for everybody. The Roman Baths, The Royal Crescent, the famous Pulteney Bridge, and the Christmas markets are among the city’s many must see attractions.
Nearby National Trust properties can be found within a short drive, as well as other stately homes. Head to Longleat Safari Park or visit Avebury and Stonehenge, all under an hour away.

long_description:
West Barn comprises a main house, which sleeps twenty guests, and an annexe that sleeps four. You’ll also find two hot tubs, a campfire, pool table room, large dining table and terrace with stunning views across the countryside, making this the ideal group getaway! You’ll have full access to the house and grounds, and there is adequate parking for up to six cars.
West Barn is in a great location, situated in the village of Wick, and is a perfect holiday base for those who wish to explore the many attractions the area has to offer. Bath and Bristol are both less than 10 miles away, and also within a short drive are the picturesque villages of Lacock and Castle Combe, both favourite locations for TV and film directors. Lacock features in Harry Potter, Downton Abbey and Pride and Prejudice, and Castle Combe was the backdrop for War Horse.
Experience the Georgian city of Bath, only 7 miles away by car, with its famous architecture, Jane Austen Centre and thermal spa (Thermae), the city offers something for everybody. The Roman Baths, The Royal Crescent, famous Pulteney Bridge and the Christmas markets are among the city’s many must see attractions. Nearby National Trust properties can be found within a short drive, as well as other stately homes. Head to Longleat Safari Park, or visit Avebury and Stonehenge, all under an hour away.

long_description:
Welcome to Cotswold Escarpment Manor, a stunning newly refurbished six-bedroom detached retreat designed for unforgettable gatherings with family and friends. Combining contemporary comfort with generous social spaces, this beautifully finished home offers everything you need for a relaxing countryside escape.
At the heart of the house is the impressive fully fitted kitchen, complete with all modern appliances, a welcoming breakfast area, and two comfortable sofas positioned at the far end beside the TV — perfect for keeping the cook company. With integrated SONOS speakers, you can set the soundtrack to your stay from morning coffee to evening drinks. A large formal dining room provides ample seating for all guests, creating the ideal setting for celebratory meals and long, laughter-filled dinners.
For entertainment, the funky kids’ games room is a real highlight, featuring table football and an air hockey table to keep younger guests (and competitive adults) busy for hours. The huge living room offers pure relaxation, boasting a cinematic TV, surround sound, and SONOS speakers — ideal for movie nights or big sporting events.
Downstairs you’ll find two spacious bedrooms: one double with a stylish ensuite and walk-in shower, and another with a king-size bed and additional single bed. There are also a utility room and a separate bathroom with shower on this floor.
Upstairs, the master suite enjoys breathtaking rural views and a luxurious ensuite complete with roll-top bath, double walk-in shower, and his-and-hers sinks. Three further bedrooms each feature a king-size and single bed, making them perfect for families. One benefits from its own shower ensuite, while a contemporary family bathroom with walk-in shower serves the remaining rooms.
Outside, the large, enclosed garden is made for entertaining, with a hot tub, covered patio, and gazebo area featuring a gas BBQ and full dining table for memorable al fresco evenings under the stars.

long_description:
Set in a rural location with stunning views of the surrounding countryside.This large, imposing, detached country house is the ideal place for a large family or group to come and stay whilst enjoying all that North Devon has to offer. The house has large living areas, a very well equipped kitchen with a quintessential Aga. There is a spacious dining room which is ideal for celebrating a special occasion, and well-furnished bedrooms, the majority of which have en-suite facilities, complete this charming house. Outside, there is the use of a private hot tub as well as a private swimming pool. There is a large well tended garden with plenty of space and sitting out areas for all to enjoy and a play area for small children. Located just outside the village of Beaford, there is also a local pub within walking distance.
North Devon has plenty to see and do, and is home to some of the best beaches in the country including Woolacombe and Saunton. The nearest beach is at Instow and is ideal for children or just a great place to walk off life’s stresses, and then enjoy a meal or drink at one of the pubs and restaurants along the front. The town of Great Torrington is only a short drive away and has most amenities you may require. The larger regional town of Barnstaple has a busy high street, the Pannier Market and famous Butchers Row. There are numerous places of interest close by including the RHS gardens at Rosemoor, Dartington Crystal and the historic fishing village at Clovelly. For the younger ones a visit to the Big Sheep or Milky Way Adventure Parks is a good option. There is walking on Dartmoor or hire a bike and cycle the Tarka Trail, and there is also golf and fishing available locally.
Beaford House is also a registered wedding venue and as well as the large house, there is also access to a great, well equipped function room should you decide to spend your big day here. Shop 5 miles, pub ¾ mile.

long_description:
Completely renovated in 2022 into a stunning home to create the best holiday let possible! Ticking all the right boxes, offering luxury, contemporary accommodation beautifully blended with the original features of the property to maintain its charm and character. There is plenty of space on offer so that you can choose to spend quality time with your loved ones or enjoy your own pursuits. The impeccable detail is on show throughout the home. Having a spacious open plan kitchen/dining room, fully equipped to delight any chef, and the large dining table is perfect to seat the whole family and celebrate any occasion in style, and also being a great socialising space without leaving the master chef of the group. The living room offers large comfy sofas, here you can enjoy quality time together with good conversation or enjoy a film. The snug TV room is a cosy and comfortable room where you can kick back and enjoy, also a great space for the kids to enjoy their games and own preferred TV choices. You can see stunning sea views throughout the property. There are six individually designed and thoughtfully furnished bedrooms and five bathrooms. At first floor there are three bedrooms, a kingsized bedroom, and two bedrooms each with triple single beds, perfect for families and a favourite for children. At second floor there three further bedrooms, a twin bedded room and two kingsized double bedrooms. Every bedroom at rear of the house benefits from a distant sea view.
Boasting a central location and within easy walking distant of the amenities of this seaside village. Mundesley itself boasts lots of places to eat and drink and a wide sandy beach which is considered by many to be one of the best in the area, and a golf course to enjoy; all this is just walking distance. You will be tempted to enjoy your whole holiday at High View House, but the location is exceptional to explore all the delights the North Norfolk Coastline and the famous Norfolk Broads National Park. Discover the popular coastal resorts of Cromer, with its famous pier and Sheringham, home to the North Norfolk Steam Railway. The pretty seaside village of Happisburgh has picturesque lighthouse, Waxham, Horsey offers excellent beaches backed by dunes. Shopaholics head to the medieval city of Norwich with two indoor shopping malls, market square and plenty of eateries. For those seeking culture and history, why not visit the Blickling Hall Estate, Flebbrigg Hall, Sheringham Gardens, the Thursford and Muckleburgh Collections. Young at heart will enjoy a day out at Bewilderwood in Horning, Dinosaur Adventure Park at Lenwade, Banham Zoo or Amazonia Zoo in Cromer. Birdwatcher will delight at RSPB Nature Reserve Marshes of Blakeney, Cley Next the Sea and Salthouse. Beach 1 mile. Shops, Pub, café and restaurants 500 yards.

long_description:
Beautifully renovated, Ttich Manor is the perfect hideaway home for families and groups of friends looking for a picturesque retreat. The Grade II listed historic manor house is tucked away in a quiet, tranquil area with uninterrupted views and an acre of garden to explore. It is a period property, believed to date from the 12th century, which has been modernised whilst retaining its grand period features. Sleeping up to 17 guests across four floors, it has a games room/arcade machine, music and karaoke system, piano, outdoor hot tub and private sauna for guests’ use.
Transport yourself back in time as you enter the sweeping driveway and are met by this eye-catching period property. Enter via the double doors onto the ground floor where you will find a traditional yet stylish dining room, with full height windows to allow light to cascade into this wonderful room. There is an expansive, period-style living room with U-shape sofas, Smart TV and Wi-Fi, plus a large kitchen with all modern comforts including a pod coffee machine, air fryer, three ovens and a waffle maker.
The lower ground floor showcases elements of the old stone castle that once stood here, and offers a fantastic entertaining area for friends and families. There is a games room, karaoke machine, Sony music system, private sauna and additional living area located on this level.
The bedrooms are split between two further levels. On the first floor East Wing is a double bedroom with en-suite, and one single bedroom. On the first floor West Wing, there are two double bedrooms with en-suite shower rooms, two additional double beds, one with a single bed, and a family bathroom. On the second floor you will find a double bedroom, a second bedroom with 3 single beds, additional bathroom and further living area.
Behind the main house is what was once a formal garden, again surrounded by mature trees and flora. From the main garden you are led through an opening to a further expanse of garden from where you can enjoy views over local farmland. Lots of countryside walks along nearby rivers and lakes are available from your doorstep.

long_description:
Nestled within the heart of St Issey, a hamlet just outside Padstow, you can find our ARC – an 18th-century building restored to its original plan by Parti Architects.

Formerly a listed manor house, courthouse and mill, the building is united together by the characterful garden at the heart of the property, which is rigged with garden rooms, an oval sun lawn, an outdoor kitchen and a wood-fired hot tub. Entertaining twenty six guests spread across twelve en-suite kingsize rooms, fortified by five reception spaces, it hass plenty of room to relax in, recover, dance and dine.
As you approach the entrance hall, there are two living spaces to welcome you, both with open fires and logs to get you started. A delightful playroom offers children some interactive space of their own with a door out to the garden. The kitchen is state-of-the-art, with four ovens, a pizza oven, Braai and much more, so there is ample opportunity to explore your culinary skills, taking advantage of ARC’s lobby to fuel your stay and kindle your time spent together. The dining room is a stunningly designed space connecting outside and in, with an entire glass wall which slides open to the patio and hot tub, a bar area and wine storage, and a catwalk entrance for the ultimate arrival. The table in the dining room seats 18 as standard but can seat up to 20. Across the first, second and third floors are eleven out of the twelve bedrooms and bathrooms; all wonderfully calm spaces with gentle décor and a relaxing ambience. Four of the rooms have kingsize beds, and the other eight have super kingsize beds. All bedrooms are either en-suite or have close access to their own private bathrooms, finished with Italian carved marble basins, deep soak tubs, and walk-in showers.
From its scenery and sand to its seafood and Sauvignon, Padstow epitomises a serene sanctuary abundant with the simple pleasures we’ve fallen accustomed to living without in the bustle, hustle and tussle of modern life. Tucked west of the River Camel, the balmy fishing port and harbour town has become ubiquitous for its delicate dining scene and remarkable trails, dutifully set within a stone’s throw of the Seven Bays, and the accompanying dramatic coastline and awe-inspiring pastoral landscape of North Cornwall.
Guests can plan as much or as little as they’d like, using the owner’s online lobby to curate their stay; from the best local breakfast delivered to your door, and a private bartender for cocktails night, to in-house yoga and a personal photographer to document the getaway. Throughout the home, you’ll find the latest extraordinary work from the ARC Salon, an ever-updating in-house cultural programme exhibiting the artwork of emerging talent – created to support the greatest local artists, designers and thinkers. There to admire and inspire, all pieces are also available to purchase as a lasting keepsake of time well spent together. Beach 5 miles. Pub and restaurant 120 yards.

Amazing property featuring floor-to-ceiling glass, a swimming pool, cinema room, games room with bar, and en-suite bathrooms in every bedroom—all with full-house surround sound.

Welcome to your ultimate escape in the heart of Radlett, where luxury and comfort blend seamlessly in this exquisite 5-star property. This opulent retreat accommodates up to twelve guests, making it the perfect destination for family gatherings, celebrations, or an unforgettable getaway with friends. Located in a serene and prestigious neighbourhood, the property boasts floor-to-ceiling glass walls and graceful curves throughout.
Arranged across two wings, highlights include a magnificent circular master suite with a dressing room and bathroom, accessible via an enclosed glass walkway, and a roof terrace with a hot tub offering uninterrupted views of the stunning surroundings. The sumptuous basement leisure complex includes a fabulous indoor pool and steam room, a cinema with a 110-inch Curve screen, a luxury bar and wine cellar, a gym, and dedicated staff or guest accommodations.
Each of the six bedrooms is a haven of style and comfort, with plush beds, luxurious linens, and ample storage. The inviting living areas are perfect for relaxing and socializing, with plush sofas and large windows that overlook the grounds. Adjacent to this space is a fully equipped kitchen with top-of-the-line appliances and ample counter space, ideal for creating culinary masterpieces. The spacious dining room is perfect for shared meals, and outdoor patio dining allows for an al fresco experience in the warmer months.
Indulgence is at the heart of this property’s amenities. The indoor pool offers a refreshing escape, with loungers nearby for relaxation. Enjoy the rejuvenating steam room or visit the private gym, equipped with high-quality gear to meet all your fitness needs. The cinema room with theatre-style seating and an expansive screen is a show-stopping feature, perfect for movie nights.
Radlett’s prime location offers the best of both worlds: peaceful countryside surroundings and easy access to urban attractions. The charming town boasts upscale restaurants, boutique shops, and scenic parks. For aviation enthusiasts, the De Havilland Museum is nearby, while families will love a visit to Winnie the Pooh Park. Warner Brothers Studios and Harry Potter World are also within easy reach, offering memorable day trips.
With central London just a short train ride away, you’re perfectly positioned for a day of sightseeing, shopping, theatre, or dining at celebrity restaurants. This exclusive Radlett property is more than a stay—it’s a luxurious escape crafted to elevate your holiday experience. With amenities rivalling the finest hotels and a setting that balances tranquillity and convenience, Radlett Mansion promises an unforgettable retreat where every detail is designed for comfort and luxury. Book your stay today to unwind, rejuvenate, and create cherished memories in one of Radlett’s most luxurious holiday homes.

long_description:
Escape to The Stables, a truly unique countryside retreat sleeping up to 27 guests, where beautifully converted stable rooms meet contemporary luxury just minutes from Newcastle upon Tyne. Perfect for large family gatherings, celebrations, hen and stag weekends, corporate retreats or holidays with friends, this exceptional property offers the ideal blend of privacy and sociable open-plan living.
Entering through the private gates, you’ll discover eight individually numbered ensuite bedrooms arranged around a charming courtyard, creating the feel of your own boutique retreat. Five stylish mezzanine bedrooms feature cosy lounge areas with upstairs sleeping accommodation, while three spacious ground-floor bedrooms provide added accessibility and comfort. Follow the pathway to the heart of the estate, an impressive open-plan barn conversion designed for bringing everyone together. Here you’ll find a contemporary, fully equipped kitchen with a large island, spacious dining facilities and a comfortable lounge with plush seating and a Smart TV. Throw open the bi-fold doors to reveal a wraparound patio with outdoor seating, an inviting hot tub and peaceful woodland surroundings, where a gentle beck and generous lawn provide the perfect setting for relaxing, dining al fresco or enjoying garden games.
Ideally positioned in Gateshead with excellent access to the A1, The Stables is perfectly placed for discovering the very best of the North East. Newcastle city centre is just a short drive away, where you can stroll along the vibrant Quayside, admire the iconic Tyne Bridge and Gateshead Millennium Bridge, enjoy shopping at Eldon Square or experience the city’s renowned restaurants, bars and nightlife. Visit Newcastle Castle, catch a performance at The Glasshouse International Centre for Music or cheer on Newcastle United at St James’ Park.
For those who love the outdoors, Beamish Museum offers a fascinating glimpse into the region’s past, while Gibside National Trust, Derwent Walk Country Park and the North Pennines National Landscape provide miles of beautiful walking and cycling routes. Durham Cathedral and Castle, both UNESCO World Heritage Sites, are also within easy reach.
A visit to Northumberland is a must, with its breathtaking coastline boasting award-winning beaches, historic castles and picturesque villages including Bamburgh, Alnwick, Warkworth and Seahouses. Enjoy a boat trip to the Farne Islands, explore Hadrian’s Wall or spend the day at Kielder Water & Forest Park. Closer to home, The Woodmans Arms is just a few miles away and is a popular choice for a traditional pub meal, especially its renowned Sunday roasts.
For even larger groups, The Stables can be booked alongside The Farmhouse at TyneView Estate, allowing up to 45 guests to stay together across both properties. Whether you’re planning a wedding, milestone birthday, family reunion or corporate event, the two properties provide exceptional accommodation with fantastic social spaces, making TyneView Estate the perfect destination for unforgettable group celebrations.

The Farmhouse is a stunning Grade II listed farmhouse that perfectly combines historic charm with stylish modern living, creating an unforgettable retreat for up to 18 guests. Set within peaceful countryside yet only minutes from the A1 and Newcastle, it’s an ideal choice for family gatherings, celebrations, hen and stag weekends, corporate stays or simply escaping with friends. The spacious accommodation features six flexible bedrooms, five bathrooms, a fully equipped kitchen with a large dining area seating everyone together, and a welcoming living room complete with a cosy gas fire and an impressive private bar with an ice maker. Guests can enjoy hours of entertainment in the games room with pool table and darts before stepping outside to relax in the hot tub, gather around the firepit or unwind in the courtyard surrounded by beautiful woodland. With Starlink Wi-Fi, private parking and thoughtful touches throughout, The Farmhouse has everything needed for a memorable stay.
Perfectly positioned in Gateshead, the property offers the best of both worlds, with tranquil countryside on the doorstep and Newcastle’s vibrant city centre just a short drive away. Spend a day exploring Newcastle’s famous Quayside, home to the iconic Tyne Bridge, the Gateshead Millennium Bridge and the striking BALTIC Centre for Contemporary Art. Discover the city’s fantastic shopping at Eldon Square, enjoy live entertainment at The Glasshouse International Centre for Music, or experience Newcastle’s renowned restaurants, bars and nightlife.
Outdoor enthusiasts will find plenty to enjoy nearby. Walk or cycle through the beautiful Derwent Walk Country Park, visit the National Trust’s Gibside Estate with its woodland trails and historic landscapes, or venture further into the North Pennines Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. Beamish Museum, one of the UK’s finest open-air museums, offers a fascinating journey through the region’s history and makes a fantastic family day out.
If you’re looking to dine locally, The Woodmans Arms, less than three miles away, is well worth a visit and is particularly popular for its traditional Sunday roasts. For those wishing to explore further afield, Northumberland’s spectacular coastline, with its sandy beaches, castles and picturesque villages, is within easy reach, making day trips simple and rewarding.
Whether you’re celebrating a special occasion, planning a reunion, hosting a corporate retreat or simply enjoying quality time together, The Farmhouse at TyneView Estate provides the perfect base for creating lasting memories in one of the North East’s most exciting locations.

long_description:
Wow, just Wow!!! At Fell Hall live like a King and enjoy the luxury and opulence of this stunning house. Arriving at Fell Hall you are immediately taken aback by its good looks. As you enter through the double gates you honestly won’t believe your luck! Fell Hall is exquisite and very well located in the stunning Cumbrian countryside so that when you do pull yourself away from the amazing place you can easily explore some famous spots nearby. Fell Hall is perfect for entertaining loved ones and the exquisite details complement the modern build perfectly. When you step inside, you’re sure to be amazed by the great hall with its wood burner, vaulted ceilings with exposed beams, stone chimney breast and lots of wonderful welcome touches have been added for that ultimate relaxation experience. The comfort of Fell Hall extends into the modern high quality kitchen and sociable dining room with large dining table where all the family can enjoy any culinary masterpieces you may create in the kitchen. If you need more space, there is a further sitting room on the ground floor. On the lower ground floor, which can be accessed by a lift, the opulence continues with your very own bar, pool table, a multi-gym with sound system and comfortable seating where you can watch your favourite sport on the large wall mounted TV. If that’s not enough to keep you entertained, the last word in luxury has to be the stunning indoor heated swimming pool and hot tub, also on the lower ground floor. Returning to the ground floor you will find 2 luxury kingsize bedrooms, both with walk-in en-suite shower rooms, one with wheelchair access. You can either take the lift up to the first floor, or from either side of the great hall, up the oak staircase where you’ll find another 6 deluxe bedrooms, tastefully presented with the highest level of comfort in mind, dressed in crisp white bed linen and all with walk-in en-suite shower rooms.
Located in the beautiful Cumbrian countryside, Fell Hall is in the perfect location for exploring the area. Brampton is a delightful little town only 3 miles away, where you will find a variety of shops, delightful cafés and restaurants. The attractions are endless in the area, however a must is a visit to Birdoswald Roman Fort on the path of the world famous Hadrian’s Wall, or Talkin Tarn where you can go boating, coarse fishing and walking, and not forgetting the kids, who will love a day at Walby Farm Park! The location is ideal and central, with visits to the Lake District National Park, the Solway Coast, Scottish Borders and the Eden Valley within a ½ hour drive. That’s if you can pull yourself away from Fell Hall !! !

long_description:
The Cow Shed is a striking renovated farm building which sleeps six guests. Boasting an enclosed private garden with stunning views across the valley and a sheltered hot tub. This property’s garden adjoins its neighbour, The Milking Parlour. Larger bookings can rent both spaces with access into either garden via a gate between the two, giving families and large gatherings the freedom to move between gardens and enjoy access to both hot tubs (double bubble!). The Cow Shed can accommodate up to eight adults with one of the three bedrooms offering either a super kingsize or two single beds, depending on the requirements of your guests. The remaining two rooms have kingsize and super kingsize beds, whilst the sofa bed is located on the ground floor in the living room.
After entering the property’s hallway you’ll see straight into the impressive kitchen and dining area; with its vaulted ceiling, mezzanine balcony and upcycled milking jar lights. The well-equipped kitchen has a large central island perfect for entertaining, with a separate area for dining featuring a handmade wooden table and seating for eight. Adjacent are the French doors which lead to the garden and sheltered hot tub, ideal for opening up the space on warm, sunny days. The spacious living area has a log burner for cosy nights by the fire and large comfy sofas. A specially built wooden room divider partially zones off the far-side giving extra guests on the sofa-bed some additional privacy. The only en-suite bedroom is located off the living room featuring an ample super kingsize bed and garden views.
Climbing the wooden staircase from the kitchen, you’ll find the gorgeous mezzanine balcony where you can relax with a book and a warm drink whilst enjoying the view through the glass balustrade. The first floor bedrooms sit snugly beneath the sloping ceilings of the converted attic; the larger of the two with a super kingsize bed (or 2 singles) and vintage furniture. The shared bathroom has both a bath and shower; with a large roof window letting in plenty of natural light. The sheltered hot tub seats six adults and faces out over the valley where stunning views of the sunset can be enjoyed whilst soaking up the bubbles in the fully-enclosed garden. A patio and outdoor dining area with brick built BBQ give you plenty of excuses to burn a few burgers and enjoy the afternoon sun.

long_description:
Seabreeze is an exceptional coastal holiday home set just moments from the seafront, offering a relaxed and luxurious base for a memorable getaway. Spread over multiple levels, the house is thoughtfully designed to give larger groups plenty of room to unwind while still feeling connected. With eight stylish bedrooms and four modern bathrooms, it comfortably accommodates family groups or friends holidaying together. The contemporary open-plan living and dining space is ideal for socialising, while the well-equipped kitchen makes self-catering easy and enjoyable. For relaxation, guests can enjoy a private hot tub and sauna, perfect after a day out exploring. A dedicated cinema room adds a special touch for cosy evenings in, and the property also benefits from free Wi-Fi and private parking. From the front of the property, guests can enjoy stunning sea views, capturing the ever-changing light and dramatic sunsets across Morecambe Bay.
The location is ideal for families and anyone looking to enjoy a classic British seaside holiday with plenty to see and do. Morecambe Promenade is perfect for gentle walks, cycling and scooter rides, while the expansive beach offers space for paddling, sand play and kite flying. The sunsets across the bay are particularly striking and are among the best in the country. Families will find a wide range of attractions nearby, including parks with adventure play areas, mini golf and seasonal activities that appeal to younger children. Traditional seaside amusements provide light-hearted fun, while indoor activity centres offer an excellent option for rainy days.
For those keen to explore further, the surrounding area offers scenic coastal walks and easy access to the wider Lancashire and Lake District countryside, making day trips simple and rewarding. Boat trips, wildlife spotting and heritage attractions add variety for all ages. Whether your group prefers active days out or slow seaside strolls, Morecambe offers a welcoming mix of relaxation and entertainment.
With its prime seafront setting, stunning outlook and generous facilities, Seabreeze Morecambe provides a comfortable and well-located base for a family holiday filled with fresh air, coastal views and shared experiences.

long_description:
As you pass the magnificent stately home of Broughton Hall and climb up the single track road through the estate, Eden House soon comes into view and will take your breath away.
This magnificent detached house commands a secluded position, surrounded by the 3000-acre grounds of the Broughton Hall Estate... and a few sheep! A popular venue for a wedding and perfect for a group of friends or a family gathering, Eden House offers plenty of space and comfort for everyone. The huge, high ceilinged living room provides a stunning space for everyone to get together in one room. The kitchen is flooded with light thanks to the cathedral-style window and French doors. With a large central island and breakfast area it will be the hub of the house for a natter over a cup of coffee each morning. The traditionally furnished dining room provides contrasting décor to the stylish and contemporary furnishings throughout the rest of the house, but gives ample opportunity for all guests to dine together. A simple relaxation/reading area at the bottom of two staircases provides a quiet retreat. One staircase leads to just two of the bedrooms and a bathroom which gives privacy to those who want to slip away early or to a small family. There are two bedrooms and a bathroom on the ground floor as well as level access throughout the house.
Outside, a sunken wood-fired hot tub for 6 guests provides further relaxation opportunities and the vast expanse of flat lawned garden is ideal for ball games. If you’re planning a party, it’s the prime spot for a marquee to extend the celebrations! Hidden within the two-storey garage is a bar and children’s room, ideal for all guests. The owner has thoughtfully provided a complementary welcome pack including wine, milk and a selection of delicious homemade cakes.
Wander through the huge grounds, meander along the river and explore to your heart’s content. You may even stumble across the cycle track in the woods so don’t forget to bring your bikes with you! For a little more adventure, why not book a Land Rover Experience at the course on site (by direct arrangement with the owner).
Just a few hundred yards away is the A59, but Eden House will feel like a million miles away. Just 3½ miles away is the busy town of Skipton with its long, cobbled high street, an eclectic mix of independent and high street shops and an abundance of cafés and tea rooms await. Stroll along the canal, through the woods or discover Norman history at Skipton Castle.
Within 10 miles drive is Malham with its breathtaking 260ft high limestone cove. If you’re feeling fit, climb the steps to the top where you’ll be rewarded with magnificent views down the dale and be able to see one of the finest examples of limestone pavement in the country, which was also used in a scene from one of the Harry Potter films! Alternative easy walks include Gordale Scar, also a film location for Harry Potter.
For a relaxing day out venture further into the Yorkshire Dales to the picturesque villages of Grassington, 12 miles, and Kettlewell, 5 miles further, calling at Kilnsey Trout Farm on the way and a stop off to watch the climbers hang off Kilnsey Crag. Many walks and cycle routes for all abilities can be found here and all around the area. Country pubs serving local produce are within easy reach of Eden House should you wish to dine out during your stay, with the closest just 500 yards away and easily reached via a stroll through the estate grounds. Eden House provides a tranquil retreat away from the hustle and bustle of everyday life but will come alive when filled with your family and friends, yet is within very easy reach of the main town of Skipton and surrounding attractions – what more could you want? Shops 3½ miles, pub/restaurant 500 yards.
Please note: There are open, steep, spiral or narrow stairs at the property.

Gas central heating, gas, electricity, bed linen, towels and Wi-Fi included. 2 travel cots and 2 highchairs. Telephone. Purpose-built heated games room in garden, with full-size snooker table, bar, cloakroom, jukebox, table football and large 72" Satellite TV. Two Z-beds available (for +2). Garden with patio, terrace, garden furniture and barbecue. 2-acre grounds. Table tennis. Indoor heated swimming pool (10m x 4m, max depth 5ft) with shower/changing facilities. Sauna. Hot tub for 6 (private). Garage parking for 4 cars; additional private parking for 2 cars. No smoking. Please note: There is an unfenced pond in the garden. This property has a security deposit of £200.

Cliff Lodge is an amazing house located in the beautiful village of Maidencombe. The house itself boasts uninterrupted panoramic sea views from the stunning glass balconies situated around the house. The property has been refurbished in 2020 to an exceptionally high standard which enhances the natural beauty of the surroundings. The house has something for everyone and is the perfect location for any sort of celebration or just a relaxing week with family or friends.
Cliff Lodge is set in substantial and beautiful grounds in the heart of the the village of Maidencombe. Neighbouring Teignmouth and Shaldon are only a 5-minute drive away. Cliff Lodge is only 3 miles away from the centre of Torquay, St Marychurch and Babbacombe which are just 1½ miles away. There are numerous beauty spots, pubs, restaurants and attractions all in close proximity to the house. Only a short walk from Cliff Lodge you’ll find the South West Coast path which follows the stunning coastline and beaches as far as you would wish to go.
This wonderful abode is made up of six individually decorated bedrooms, each with their own unique characteristic, dressed in high quality linen, and some of which boasting sea views, en-suite facilities and balconies. There is an indoor heated swimming pool complex that is close to the main house. This beautiful area also has an electric sauna and sun loungers to relax on. The pool house is surrounded by a decked area which has a sunken jacuzzi on one side and a large sun deck on the other. This whole area is surrounded by glass balconies which look directly across the sea. A Sonos sound system is available to enhance the whole experience. A perfect place to relax and enjoy a drink or listen to music with friends and family. Alternatively, head over to the games room where you can enjoy a game of table football or snooker on the full-size table while listening to a variety of music on the juke box. This spacious room has a bar area with a fridge and a 75? Sony TV on the wall.
Back inside the main house, whip up a treat in the fully-equipped kitchen, and dine in either the dining room or conservatory/breakfast room, complete with stunning views over the Jurassic coast.
Please note: There are open, steep, spiral or narrow stairs at the property.

long_description:
This Grand, 1860 Victorian Villa features a living room with wood burner, two sofas, a baby grand piano and TV with Netflix & Prime TV. Also on the ground floor is a private office and separate dining room with table and chairs for eight people. The large kitchen with table and seating for six people is well-equipped with everything you could need during your stay, including a beer/juice fridge and wine fridge. Leading off the kitchen is the utility area with storage, sink, dishwasher, washing machine & tumble dryer. A separate door leads off the utility area to the Spa & Wellness centre.
On the first floor are three bedrooms, one with en-suite shower room and one large bathroom with bath big enough for two (the jets do not work, but with the addition of bubbles and candles, you will have a relaxing time). The second bedroom has a superking bed and the master bedroom has an Emperor bed. On the second floor is a top landing with open sky glass view platform. Up here you will find a further two double bedrooms and one twin bedroom and a shower room.
Spa & Wellness Centre: On entering there is a comfortable seating area. You then move into the large open plan area housing a table tennis table, A seven-foot pool table, a computerised soft-tip dart board and an 18’ (5.5m) Wellis Amazonas Swim-Spa for the perfect workout. After your fun in the Swim Spa, why not then try the Smart Sauna?
Please note that the owners are currently adding a new shower & separate toilet facility to this area, which will not interrupt your fun and relaxation. The owners are also creating two separate mezzanine areas with small cocktail bar, along with a games area. These areas are not yet ready and will not interfere with any of the other facilities currently on offer.
A spacious enclosed rear garden area provides ample opportunity to relax. There is a fire pit, barbecue and garden furniture, from where you will see yachts sailing past on the Clyde Estuary.
Island Seaview Villa with Swim Spa & Sauna is ideally situated to explore the island of Bute for it’s fantastic, sheltered beaches and the famous grand architecture of Mount Stuart. Drive out to the ruined chapel of St Blanes from the 12th-century and a Bronze Age stone circle. The island is also famous for its birdwatching, where you may be lucky enough to spot the Osprey’s around Loch Fad or even a white-tailed sea Eagle at Etterick Bay. There are basking sharks, humpback whales, dolphins and seals aplenty.
There are many walks around the island, including the popular West Island Way. Bute is a superb destination for cyclists. Fishing is available on the island and around it’s coastal waters, as well as loch Fad where boat hire is available to fish for rainbow and brown trout or pike. There are three golf courses on the island, along with a putting green in Rothesay town.

reviews.comment: I visited the house with my family to celebrate my 40th. We had ages 7 - 60+ and the house catered for everyone. The house is stunning and had everything you needed to enjoy quality family time there. We were amazing at how much was provided for us to enjoy. The host was brilliant and on hand to answer any questions we had over the weekend. The pool area was a massive hit and where we spent the majority of our time. We also made great use of the kitchen facilities and large dining table. Everyone had a great time. I would come back and recommend this property to any of my friends.

First of all, all 16 of us had a fantastic family weekend celebrating my wife’s 60th birthday. Our 7 grandchildren had a ball and spent the whole weekend enjoying the large indoor pool. Both adults and children also had great fun with the table tennis, darts and pool table, keeping everyone entertained throughout our stay.  The fantastic facilities also included a great lounge area with a music and karaoke system, which provided plenty of entertainment for everyone.  We would highly recommend this property for family gatherings or get-togethers. We had a brilliant time and hope to return again sometime soon.

I was hoping the last reviewer was particularly harsh with his review as we had already booked and with only a few weeks to our holiday hoped for the best. He wasn’t wrong; this house needs a lot of work to make it into ‘a beautiful and relaxing destination’. The first sight of what was to come was when we opened the fridge and freezer to load some supplies we had bought on arriving on the island, it was filthy. All the trays had food and liquid remains and there was a puddle of liquid on the floor of the appliance, the freezer was only marginally better. We set about cleaning the fridge as we had perishable food. On checking the cookers, they were equally as bad with old fat running out of one door, the seal was broken, and into the cupboard below. The downstairs rooms were not clean and had old cobwebs left in the corners. The upstairs rooms were better but the main bathroom shower was unusable as the walls and floor were crumbling away. After making some phone calls we were contacted by the owner, who was on holiday, and told that the whole house had been cleaned but a friend would come around to check. The owner’s friend agreed with our assessment and it was agreed that her cleaning company would come in the next day whilst we were out and try to remedy the mess. As good as her word the kitchen and downstairs rooms were cleaned and old dirty towels that had been left in the pool area had been washed and hung out to dry, the tumble dryer was broken!  The fitted Microwave didn’t work but there was one in the pool room that did. One ring on the 4 ring hob didn’t work, inconvenient with a large number of guests. We had to shift so much of the owners out of date food stuff in the kitchen cabinets to make room for our own food. With all the facilities available it was a pity the basics were completely overlooked

long_description: Boasting spectacular views over Dunure Castle to the Firth of Clyde coast and across the sea to the Isle of Arran, this cosy cottage sits only yards from the beach and the picturesque fishing harbour at Dunure and is situated on the Ayrshire Coastal Path, 100 miles along one of the finest panoramic coastlines in the British Isles. Crowned with a superb backdrop of the ever-changing profile of the mountains of Arran across the Firth of Clyde, this coastline is steeped in history and teeming with wildlife, including red squirrels, deer, otters and seals and is a haven for bird watchers. Ayrshire offers a varying coastline with villages, beaches and rocky coves to explore. Inland there is walking, cycling, gardens and castles to visit, riding, fishing, racing and a choice of golf courses, including the world famous Turnberry. Culzean Castle Country Park (extending over 550 acres) has a network of wooded trails passing along the beach and the stunning Dumfries House is worth a visit. Ayrshire, also known as "Burns’ Country", is steeped in tradition and history. Visit Burns Cottage, The Burns Memorial Museum and the Brig o Doon, the bridge from the famous poem Tam o Shanter. The seaside towns of Ayr, Prestwick and Troon are all close by with beautiful sandy beaches. Day trips can be taken to Arran and Cumbrae and are well worth the effort. Beach 200 yards. Pub ¼ mile.

Spectacular - Westwynd is a beautiful detached luxury property and the prefect venue for a special family get together where you will enjoy a memorable stay. Completely refurbished in 2022, the elegant accommodation includes a spacious living room with floor to ceiling windows and doors through to a conservatory with your very own bar! The modern and spacious dining kitchen will wow you as you enter Westwynd, and sliding patio doors from here look onto the spectacular indoor heated swimming pool with shower room and sauna. (Please bring own towels for use at the pool). With loungers set around the pool and a mezzanine level above leading to an outside terrace, whatever the weather, you can enjoy the delights of this wonderful house. Luxurious touches continue throughout with sumptuous beds and bedding and modern shower rooms.
Quietly set Westwind is only a few miles from the vibrant harbour town of Stranraer where you can take a stroll along the sea front and spend a few hours in Agnew Park which has a wide range of leisure facilities for all ages, including a boating lake, a play park for the younger kids and an 18-hole putting green, or just enjoy a morning coffee in the café making the most of the views over the bay. The town also offers a wide range of shops, pubs and restaurants where you can dine out
This beautiful area of south-west Scotland, known as the Rhinns of Galloway, is a delightful area and boasts rugged coastlines and secluded sandy beaches, which benefit from the warmth of the passing Gulf Stream, and is surrounded by breathtaking scenery. There are many beautiful gardens to explore, including the world renowned Logan Botanical Gardens. Take a drive out to some of the many pretty little ports such as Sandhead and Portpatrick, or the RSPB Scotland Mull of Galloway Nature Reserve, Scotland’s most southerly point, where thousands of sea birds nest in the cliff face during the spring and summer.
Walking is a delight, whether clifftop, beaches, hills or forests, and the Southern Upland Way passes close by. Perfect for cycling enthusiasts, the world famous 7Stanes is within easy reach. If you prefer golf, there are many facilities nearby, and the county course is just a short drive away. Nearby Cairnryan is home to the Stena Line ferry, making a day trip to Ireland a great day out.

long_description:
This private and self-contained wing of a beautiful Victorian country house is ideal for family gatherings and parties, providing the perfect base for exploring Northumberland and the Scottish Borders with its beaches, historic buildings and stunning scenery. This south-facing house overlooks its secluded garden complete with barbecue, garden furniture, firepit, badminton and a large private hot tub for relaxing in. Beyond Yetholm Loch lies against a backdrop of green rounded hills. The surrounding parkland grazes horses and rare breed Soay sheep. Extensive farm and woodland walks are ideal for families to explore, pets and nature lovers. Interesting ecological and landscape features.
Inside, you can enjoy the soft sofas surrounded by period furniture and paintings, an impressive library of books, a chest full of toys, two open fires, a family grand piano, Wi-Fi, satellite television and a DVD player. There’s a special place for everyone in this spacious house. The well-equipped kitchen has an electric range and a large dining table. An adjacent barn houses a shared snooker table and dart board. The lawns of Lochside House provide space for family fun with a swing and trampoline.
The Yetholm Loch wildlife reserve can be reached along beautiful woodland walks and is home to many species of birds and animals. You may see an osprey or an otter playing in the sunshine. There is a family boat which guests are welcome to use for fishing or for the fun of rowing surrounded by wonderful scenery.
The village of Yetholm is a couple of miles away with pubs, a garage, a grocery store and a post office. Kelso is only 7 miles away with supermarkets and a wide range of shops. Edinburgh and Alnwick with its famous gardens are about an hour’s drive. Shop, pub and restaurant 2½ miles.
Lochside Garden House can be booked together with Lochside Stable House (UPK) and Avenel Cottage (UK10920) to accommodate up to 31 guests.

long_description:
This beautiful Victorian country house, formerly stables and a groom’s flat, sits between its own large garden and the cobbled courtyard of Lochside House. Ideal for family gatherings and parties, it is also the perfect base for exploring Northumberland and the Scottish Borders with its fine beaches, historic buildings and stunning scenery. The large secluded garden and inner dog proof yard is complete with BBQ, firepit, garden furniture, badminton and a large hot tub for relaxing in, or for family and friends to splash wildly in. To the front there is a beautiful outlook over the SSSI Yetholm Loch wildlife reserve with a backdrop of green rounded hills. The surrounding parkland grazes horses and rare breed Soay sheep. Across the whole valley are extensive new native tree plantings along with other associated environmental works. Farm and woodland walks ideal for exploring, nature lovers and dog walks.
Inside, you can enjoy the comfort of soft sofas surrounded by period furniture and paintings, lots of books, an open fire, grand piano, Wi-Fi, television and a DVD player. There’s a special place for everyone in this spacious house. The well-equipped kitchen has an electric range and a large dining table. An adjacent barn houses a shared snooker table and dart board. The lawns of Lochside House also have a shared trampoline and swing.
The Yetholm Loch wildlife reserve can be reached along beautiful woodland walks and is home to many species of birds and animals. If you are lucky, you may see an osprey swooping down to catch a fish or an otter playing in the sunshine. There is a family boat which guests are welcome to use for fishing, or for the fun of rowing surrounded by wonderful scenery. The village of Yetholm is a couple of miles away with pubs, garage, butcher, grocery store and post office. Kelso is only 7 miles away with supermarkets and a wide range of other shops. Edinburgh and Alnwick with its famous gardens are about an hour’s drive. Extensive hill walking and beautiful beaches within a thirty minute drive.
Lochside Stable House can be booked together with Lochside Garden House (S4484) and Avenel Cottage (UK10920) to accommodate up to 29 guests.

reviews.comment: Lovely spacious house with a friendly host who was more than helpful with anything we need. Some slight issues with consistency of the hot tub as it kept erroring out but the host helped us to get it back up and running.

We have just returned from a family bank holiday weekend at Lochside.  There were 10 adults, 4 children/teenagers and 3 small dogs altogether so we booked the stable house as well as Avenel Cottage and Foumartdean Cottage.  Both cottages were very pretty and quaint with everything you would need and the stable house was very comfy and lived in which we loved (ideal for hide and seek).  The kitchen was well stocked with plates and cutlery. There were ample books/games available and a badminton net on the lawn.  We enjoyed the hot tub and sat at the fire pit at night.  The countryside around the house is beautiful and the kids enjoyed playing snooker and darts too.  It was only 5 miles from kelso too from where we collected a takeaway one evening.  It was an ideal setting and i would recommend for family groups who just want to enjoy family time in beautiful surroundings.

As an extended family of 7 adults and 4 small children this property was great for us. Plenty of space to run around in, and fab gardens and walks to explore. The children loved the hot tub, and swing particularly. Edward is wonderful, he couldn’t have been more helpful, a mine of information and useful equipment (even finding jump leads for the family member who forgot to shut her car boot overnight 🙄). The property is well equipped, perhaps an update of the bathrooms wouldn’t go amiss, showering is interesting if you’re tall, but that didn’t spoil our holiday in any way, and we would certainly return.

long_description:
Airyhemming Farm is a detached two storey house situated in peaceful countryside with open views over farmland to the rolling Galloway Hills. There is ample space for families with particularly attractive features such as the farmhouse kitchen with Aga and the delightful sun room to the front offering glorious views. The property also boasts its own stretch of water for brown trout fishing. If fishing is not for you then why not relax in the hot tub or the outdoor entertainment area, complete with a bar area, fire pit and pool table! The charming village of Glenluce has local shops and pubs. This area of Dumfries and Galloway boasts rugged coastlines and secluded sandy beaches which benefit from the warmth of the passing Gulf stream and is surrounded by breathtaking scenery, offering an ideal base from which to explore the Machars Peninsula and the Galloway hills. There are many beautiful gardens to explore, including the world renowned Logan Botanical Gardens. The area boasts many pretty little ports like Sandhead, Portpatrick and the RSPB Scotland Mull of Galloway nature reserve where thousands of seabirds nest in the cliff face during the spring and summer. Walking is a delight, whether clifftop, beaches, hills or forests and the Southern Upland Way passes close by. Also a cyclist’s paradise with the world famous 7Stanes within easy reach. If you prefer shooting or golf then there are many facilities nearby including the County course just two miles away. The town of Stranraer which is only 10 miles away offers a wider range of shops, pubs and restaurants. Nearby Cairnryan is home to the Stena Line ferry making a day trip to Ireland a great day out. Beach 2 miles. Shop and pub 2 miles, restaurant 3 miles.
Airyhemming Farm can be booked together with Airyhemming Dairy (UK5201) and Kelbrook (UK5737) to accommodate up to 22 guests.

reviews.comment: What a brilliant week we had as a family of 10 adults, grandparents, young adult grandkids and mum & Dad.  The house is very warm and welcoming.This is exactly what it says it is, a farm house. You can tell that it was once a much loved family home.  The home itself does have some general wear & tear, however.. this is a farm house and this all adds to the character.We loved this.  You can tell the owner has made great effort to update the property and I'm certain there will be more to come.  Ground Floor has an amazing family kitchen where we enjoyed a lot of card games with snacks. With an electric cooker and wonderful gas stove, there was ample space and accessories for 4 adults to be cooking at same time. There is a laundry room and downstairs bathroom with shower.As you come out of the kitchen there are 2 bedrooms, one with 4 single beds and a large downstairs double bedroom with an amazing ensuite, waking up to those views on a morning is something else.  Room and bed were extremely comfortable and we felt like royalty with such a size room.  Off the bedrooms is an open plan living room, which is extended into a lovely bright and open extra living room. Being all open plan it was never an issue for movie nights, ample seating and extremely comfortable.  Upstairs were 3 double bedrooms and a large bedroom with 4 single beds.  Each room was unique and comfortable with some great views from the front rooms.  One of the rooms was ensuite with a shower and there was also a large Upstairs bathroom with shower and roll top bath. Around the back of the building, tucked away was a secret little annex.. wow !! If you want privacy then this is amazing.  Attached to the property but with its own front door, you walk into a double bedroom with ensuit and shower.How amazing 👏. Leaving the best until last... at the side of the house you will find an extroadinary entertainment area, newly built area where family can get together no matter the weather.  Under shelter looking over the breathtaking views you will find, pool table, dart board, dining table and large bench table, outdoor TV, small bar area and of course, the much welcomed hot tub.  .This area allowed everyone to enjoy the space whilst still all being together. This is just what family holidays are all about.  Overall I would recommend this house and would visit again.  Yes we had a couple of little teething issues but was nothing major, owner was contactable, however we didn't bother, it was nothing major, it didn't deter us. Again please remember this is a farm house, it has bags of character and that's exactly what we wanted.... and got !!There are lots of little areas to visit and local shop is about 10mins in car.  Only 20 mins or so to main supermarket. Night sky was brilliant, bags of stars, defo a dark sky area.  The area was lovely and quiet, peaceful and amazing views. Would highly recommend.( booked by my stepdad, review left by daughter  Donna  on behalf of the family )

We stayed here for a week, 18 of us on a lovely family holiday. We had some delicious welcome cakes on our arrival and the owners were helpful regarding any questions we had. We were also gifted some deer meat, which was very kind. Lovely place to stay in, plenty of room- well equipped kitchen, also beautiful secluded area. We throughly enjoyed our stay here!  We would definitely come back!

Hi, me and a group of my pals recently just stayed here. we absolutely loved it. the place was amazing and very accommodating to everything we wanted and needed. the hot tub was fantastic and we loved using it. A few towns near by which we visited which were nice and lovely scenic views around. would highly recommend 😊😊

long_description:
Discover The Bield, a beautiful sandstone Victorian house which until 2021 operated as a family run guest house since 1989 and is still run by them to this day. A wonderful home which is beautiful inside and out with a welcoming hallway. All the rooms are immaculately presented and there is plenty of space for family and friends, whether it be relaxing in one of the stunning living rooms with open fires, relaxing in the hot tub or soaking up the sun in the garden.
Situated in the picturesque village of Aberfoyle, the ’gateway to the Loch Lomond and Trossachs National Park’, this is the perfect location for families and couples to enjoy a luxurious and comfortable holiday while recharging after a long day exploring the beautiful surroundings. On the ground floor there is a spacious living/dining room with an open fire and a second living room, giving guests a spacious home for all to enjoy whether curling up with a book in front of the fire or everyone relaxing together to plan the next day’s adventure. The spacious kitchen with breakfasting area is well equipped for preparing a celebration meal and there is also a handy utility room. There is a family shower room and three beautifully presented bedrooms, one of which is en-suite. There are three further double bedrooms on the first floor all with an individual en-suite to complete the picture. Step outside into the well-kept garden with a hot tub and private parking for up to 6 cars! There is plenty of space for everyone to enjoy.
You may not want to venture out from The Bield, but there is so much to discover and there is no need to use the car. There are many beautiful walks surrounding The Bield, just get your boots on and head straight out the front door. For adventurous cyclists, Sustrans Cycle Route 7, a challenging long-distance route from Sunderland to Inverness, passes nearby with breathtaking views of forests, hills and lochs. Just a 5-minute drive from The Bield, you’ll find the gently rolling tracks around the picturesque Loch Ard which are made for exploring by bike or on foot, with sculpture trails and play features to find. Makes a great fun day for all the family with woodland and water-loving wildlife along the way to look out for.
Take a cruise on the steamship ’Sir Walter Scott’ on Loch Katrine, one of Scotland’s iconic lochs offering fabulous views best seen from the water. You can take your own bikes or hire bikes from The Pier, board the boat and disembark from Stronachlacher, 13 miles down the loch. Have lunch in the café, and then cycle back on the private road to your start point. For traveling further afield, Stirling, Perth, Edinburgh and Glasgow or all accessible for days out.

There is ample space to either enjoy the company of your friends or family or indeed just to have a little quiet time. At Home Farm - The Farmhouse to keep everyone entertained there a large games room with pool table and not forgetting the hot tub set quietly in the garden. Something for everyone!
This delightful area of Dumfries and Galloway boasts rugged coastlines and secluded sandy beaches which benefit from the warmth of the passing Gulf Stream and is surrounded by breathtaking scenery, Home Farm - The Farmhouse offers the ideal base for exploring the area. The locality boasts some pretty little seaside villages like Sandhead and Portpatrick. With so much on offer whatever you decide return to Home Farm - The Farmhouse and enjoy a relaxing time in the hot tub. Beach 7 miles. shop, pub and restaurant 6 miles.

long_description:
Welcome to Home Farm - The Coo Shed, a splendid holiday let that has undergone a complete transformation, offering a perfect blend of modern luxury and rural charm. This stunning retreat is nestled within the serene countryside of Dunragit, just a stone’s throw from the picturesque coastal town of Stranraer in Scotland. Whether you’re planning a reunion with extended family or seeking a peaceful escape with a group of friends, The Coo Shed accommodates up to 17 guests, making it the ideal setting for a memorable and comfortable stay.
The heart of this magnificent holiday home is its spacious dining and kitchen area, where you can prepare and share delicious meals together. The well-equipped kitchen boasts modern appliances, ensuring you have everything you need for culinary adventures or hearty family feasts. With ample space for everyone to gather and enjoy each other’s company, this area sets the stage for unforgettable moments.
In addition Home Farm - The Coo Shed offers a Games Room with a pool table, providing hours of entertainment for all ages. Whether you’re seeking friendly competition or a relaxing evening indoors, this room adds an extra dimension of fun to your stay.
Another of the property’s standout features is its beautiful enclosed garden, complete with a covered seating area that beckons you to savour the fresh country air. The garden also features your very own private hot tub, perfect for unwinding and stargazing after a day of exploring.
Furthermore, Home Farm - The Coo Shed welcomes your four-legged companions, making it a truly pet-friendly destination. Your furry friends can roam the vast outdoor spaces and join in the adventure.
When it’s time to venture beyond the comfort of The Coo Shed, you’ll find an array of attractions in the surrounding area. Discover the rugged beauty of the Galloway Forest Park, take a leisurely stroll along the picturesque shores of Loch Ryan, or explore the historic treasures of Stranraer. For golf enthusiasts, Stranraer Golf Club and Dunskey Golf Course are within easy reach.
With its idyllic location, generous amenities, and a warm welcome for both two and four-legged guests, Home Farm - The Coo Shed promises an unforgettable holiday experience. Whether you’re seeking relaxation, outdoor adventures, or quality time with loved ones, this charming retreat offers the perfect base for your Scottish getaway.
Home Farm - The Coo Shed can be booked together with Home Farm - The Dairy (UK34626), The Old Stables (CC537251), Home Farm - The Farmhouse, The Hawthorns (UK45616) and The Piglet at Airyhemming (UK45618) to accommodate up to 59 guests.

long_description:
A romantic ‘castle’ in the heart of the Cairngorms; grandeur and cosy are hard to find together but Craigendarroch House combines the two with ease. In truth, a traditional Scottish baronial Villa modelled on Balmoral Castle, Craigandarroch House with turrets and tower was designed by the architect William Smith who also designed Balmoral, a short drive up along Royal Deeside. You’ll find Craigendarroch House traditionally and stylishly decorated with all the convenience of contemporary living for a comfortable family holiday. Every attention to detail has been made, with comfortable seating and dining in the delightful garden, luxury bed linen and towels and even indoor and outdoor bars. From the moment you come through the gates up the sweeping driveway you’ll appreciate the traditional Scottish architecture with the stunning backdrop of Craigendarroch Hill behind the house. Any sprightly visitors must make the effort to walk up and admire the views from the top – a strenuous but short (30-minute) climb.
Whilst the house has all the convenience of being central to the delightful and busy town of Ballater, it also provides total privacy inside and out. Ballater and the surrounding area has a wealth of restaurants and coffee shops, some within easy walking distance, with the benefit of having the Highlands right on your doorstop for exploring further.
The house is exceptionally well maintained, with six large bedrooms, two with en-suite bathrooms and three further family bathrooms, all with modern fittings and tastefully decorated. Full central heating throughout is extremely efficient – you will be lovely and cosy in winter and there is an open fire in drawing room. The home benefits from large rooms for all the family, but there are smaller rooms for a quiet game of chess or reading in the snug or conservatory. Overlooking the front garden, the drawing room is large and sunny with seating for whole family, ideal for relaxed entertaining with its large fireplace. There is also a formal oak panelled dining room with wall-to-wall books. There is an indoor bar with TV and wine/beer fridges, perfect for having a wee dram while watching Scotland win the rugby!
There is certainly plenty to explore in the stunning surrounding countryside with the glorious river and mountain landscape of Royal Deeside and the Cairngorms. A haven for outdoor enthusiasts, leisurely walks can be enjoyed along the banks of the river while the adventurous can tackle the region’s famous mountains. There are good opportunities for canoeing and mountain biking, as well as skiing at the Lecht and Glenshee Centres during the winter months. Golf is available in Ballater itself, as well as Braemar and Banchory. There are castles and gardens at Balmoral, Crathes and Craigievar which are all well worth a visit.
Slightly further afield, the coastal and whisky trails offer the chance to explore the area’s heritage through stunning scenery. In August and September, Highland games are prevalent in all the towns and villages throughout the region. Shop ¼ mile, pub and restaurant ½ mile.

reviews.comment: We had another wonderful stay at this beautiful holiday home/castle with three generations of our family. It was the perfect place for everyone to relax, spend quality time together and enjoy everything Ballater and  the surrounding area had to offer.It was very comfortable, spacious and very well equipped, with plenty of room for everyone to have their own space as well as enjoy meals and evenings together. It was lovely to have a cosy home to return to after days out exploring the stunning Scottish countryside.From the grandparents to the youngest members of the family, everyone thoroughly enjoyed their stay. Thank you Dawn for making our stay so special. Can’t wait to return next year!

Craigendarroch House is a fabulous property with excellent accommodation for large groups. The house is well presented and as a group of nine we had all the space we needed. The grounds were impeccably kept which added to a wonderful experience.  Ballater has everything you need, restaurants, cafes, pubs and shops. There are plenty of activities to do in and around the town and the countryside is so easily accessable.

Craigendarroch House was a joy to stay at. There was plenty of room for our large family gathering and enough space for everyone to either hang out playing games or find a quiet spot to read and dose off! The bedrooms were large and beds were comfortable, with plenty of bathrooms and toilets for a large group. The kitchen facilities were brilliant for catering for large numbers and the equipment and white goods were plentiful and convenient to use. The outside space was great too and the weather even accommodated a bbq and dinner outside one evening! Dawn was friendly, approachable and kept in contact, she welcomed us contacting her if we had a question about the house. You could tell that she loves the house and sharing it with her guests. Ballater is a beautiful village and there are plenty of quaint holiday shops, art galleries and of course restaurants, bars and a supermarket to buy essentials. If you love the outdoors and getting out and about this is a great location for you.

long_description:
Mountain Bear Lodge has that special quality that will make a large family’s or friends’ get together a memorable occasion.

Newly renovated in December 2022 to a luxury standard with a large kitchen boasting top end appliances, stunning new bathrooms with under-floor heating, comfortable new bedrooms with lots of storage and an updated living/dining area with three huge sofas and coffee table, a snug with a desk, bean bags and games, and a large dining table with plenty of seating to suit everyone’s needs.
This stunning, detached, lodge property enjoys a peaceful and private location approximately a mile outside the forest village of Nethy Bridge, and makes the perfect base for exploring this lovely part of the northern Highlands. Sitting on the edge of the ancient Scottish Caledonian Forest, the lodge overlooks moorland and mountains with abundant wildlife, including red squirrels, mountain hares, red and roe deer, and many species of songbirds can often be heard in this secluded setting.
Mountain Bear Lodge is 12 miles from Aviemore which is situated in the heart of the Cairngorms National Park and at the head of the Speyside Way. The whole area boasts a super range of shops, restaurants and bars along with a wide range of outdoor activities including skiing and snowboarding, (Cairngorm Mountains are within an hour’s drive. Glencoe and Glenshee are around 2½ hours’ drive) There is also mountain and quad biking, climbing and hill walking with a variety of water sports available on Loch Insh, Loch Morlich and the River Spey. Take a trip on the Cairngorm Mountain Railway or visit the Cairngorm Reindeer Centre, the Highland Wildlife Park at nearby Kingussie, the Landmark Forest Adventure Park or the RSPB Reserve at nearby Loch Garten, which are all within easy reach of the lodge.
Visit the testing Spey Valley golf course and the Dalfaber Resort with its wonderful array of leisure activities, or a day trip to the Moray coastline peppered with little fishing villages and beautiful beaches. For the less energetic, sit back in the hot tub set in peaceful garden grounds, relax and unwind. There’s a farm shop, pub and restaurant within 1 mile.

Originally a nunnery, this semi-detached shorefront property, sleeping up to 24, offers spacious accommodation. The second living room is sea fronted and has fantastic sea views and the dining room with its large table has enough seating for all guests. It has two private hot tubs for six (one in BBQ cabin is included), a wood burning sauna, infra red sauna, steam room and enjoys fantastic views over the Firth of Clyde and offers the perfect venue for special occasions or large parties.
Situated on the Ayrshire coast only a short walk from the shore, it lies close to the bustling town of Largs with its shops, restaurants and promenade. It is ideally located to explore the islands of Cumbrae, Arran and the Isle of Bute. Ferries also run to Dunoon and the Cowal Peninsula, giving access to Loch Lomond and The Trossachs National Park.
Ayrshire offers a varying coastline with villages, beaches and rocky coves to explore, and is a perfect location for cyclists and walkers - Skelmorlie heralds the start of the Ayrshire Coastal Path, a 100-mile long coastal walk. Inland, there is walking, cycling, gardens and castles to visit, riding, fishing, racing and a choice of golf courses, including the world famous Turnberry. Culzean Castle Country Park, extending over 550 acres, has a network of wooded trails passing along the beach. Glasgow and Edinburgh are easily reached for a day trip, with rail links available from the town. Beach 100 yards. Shop 500 yards, pub 600 yards and restaurant 6 miles.
