reviews.comment: Just back from a 2 night stay at The Old Nunnery. We were a family group with teenagers and dogs and we were celebrating husbands birthday and our Golden Wedding Anniversary. Its a beautiful comfortable quirky house with a real homely feel.  Really well equipped. Loads of dishes, cutlery pots and pans and enough gadgets to keep everyone happy. Loads of rooms and plenty space for everyone.  Kids enjoyed exploring the house and being on the beach, seeing the seals.  When the found a skeleton  albeit fake in the garden they were ecstatic!  The sauna stream room and hot tub went down a storm and the lads enjoyed THE BBQ cabin which girls enjoyed well equipped bar for making cocktails.   Two nights just wasn't long enough.  We will go back!  Alan is perfect host!

What a beautiful house! Our group had an amazing stay here, we paid for both hot tubs and enjoyed the steam rooms and both saunas.The bedrooms were a good size and we had everything we needed.We did have to clean a few items before we were able to use them but this wasn't too big of a deal. We would definitely return in the future if we find ourselves heading down that way again.

The accommodation was ideal for our family party of 24.  We were self-catering and found the kitchen facilities adequate although a larger fridge would have been helpful.  One of the two dishwashers did not perform well at first and we found the filter and spray arms to be badly in need of cleaning!  The beds were comfortable and the bathroom facilities were adequate, although the hot water took a very long time to reach the two downstairs bathrooms.  The hot tub, sauna and steam room provided an enjoyable indoor activity, while the closeness to Largs, Wemyss Bay and the island ferries allowed for some good daytime excursions.  Relative nearness to Glasgow Airport was also an advantage.

long_description:
Set amidst the tranquil beauty of the Black Isle, this magnificent eight bedroom country home offers an exceptional escape for families, friends, and groups seeking a luxurious stay in the Scottish Highlands. With elegant interiors, sweeping views, and every comfort thoughtfully provided, this property combines traditional Highland charm with contemporary indulgence.
Sleeping up to twenty-four guests, the house features nine beautifully appointed bathrooms, ensuring space and privacy for everyone. The welcoming lounge, with its crackling wood-burning stove, invites guests to unwind after a day exploring the surrounding countryside, while the separate music room provides a perfect space for entertainment or relaxation. A convenient ground-floor WC and a fully equipped utility room add to the home’s practicality.
The heart of the property lies in its stunning kitchen, complete with a traditional Aga, breakfast area, and adjoining family space, ideal for gathering together over morning coffee. Meals are enjoyed in the light-filled conservatory dining room, where floor-to-ceiling windows frame panoramic views of rolling farmland and distant hills.
Outside, the grounds are equally impressive. The large private garden offers plenty of space for children to play, complemented by a dedicated play area and a bubbling hot tub where adults can relax under the stars. Whether hosting a summer barbecue, enjoying an evening drink, or simply taking in the peace and beauty of the Black Isle, the setting is truly unforgettable.
Duncanston is perfectly positioned for exploring the many attractions of the Highlands. Nearby Cromarty, a charming historic village, offers cobbled streets, galleries, and a lovely shoreline. Dolphin spotting at Chanonry Point is a must, with frequent sightings of bottlenose dolphins just offshore. Golf enthusiasts will find several excellent courses within easy reach, and outdoor lovers can enjoy coastal walks, cycling trails, and forest adventures. Inverness, just a short drive away, provides shopping, dining, and cultural experiences, while Loch Ness, Urquhart Castle, and the scenic North Coast 500 route are all within easy touring distance.
Whether you’re planning a family reunion, a special celebration, or a luxurious Highland getaway, this exceptional Duncanston property offers the perfect blend of comfort, style, and location a true home-from-home in one of Scotland’s most captivating regions.

long_description:
Situated on the most accessible of the west coast islands and straddling the Highland Line, this spacious, detached, country house with large deck and its own hot tub, boasts stunning views over the open water and lies in a rural location, just a few yards from the shoreline. Most rooms enjoy sea views, the 6 bedrooms each have a TV, and some have a DVD player. Chandlers is full of elegance and charm and enjoys a cosy snug area with comfy sofas and a bar, which can be stocked to your requirements. The music room has a grand piano, guitars and amps for budding musicians, while the impressive dining room can easily seat 20.
A popular destination for fishing, the inland lochs are popular with anglers for coarse and game fishing. Loch Fad offers the opportunity to fish for rainbow trout, and is only 3 miles away. Relax as you explore the gently, undulating hills, catch glimpses of the wildlife and marvel at the vistas. For such a compact island, Bute offers varied landscapes from the lush, fertile and rolling hills of the island’s heart to the craggy, heather-covered moorlands of the north and the delightful sandy beaches around the coastline. A haven for walkers, cyclists and outdoor enthusiasts, Bute has a wealth of wildlife to spot including feral goats, buzzards and roe deer. Scalpsie Bay which is set against the magnificent backdrop of Arran, is the home of a large colony of seals.
There are many historical sites to visit including the standing stones at Ettrick Bay, the ancient chapel of St Blane, and the vitrified Iron Age Fort at Dunagoil. Visit the Victorian Gothic mansion of Mount Stuart, the ancestral home of the Marquesses of Bute, and is open to the public along with its beautiful gardens, Bute Museum, Rothesay Castle and the fabulous gardens of Ascog Hall and Ardencraig.
There are many events throughout the year, including the famous annual Jazz Festival, the spectacular Highland Games, traditional agricultural shows, concerts and art festivals; whatever your interest it can be found on the Isle of Bute.
Catch the ferry for the 5-minute trip to Colintraive on the Cowal Peninsula and explore Argyll’s Secret Coast where you have easy access to Loch Lomond and The Trossachs National Park, or head north to Inverary and beyond. Take the ferry from Portavadie over to Jura and Islay, and Tarbert where you can explore Kintyre. The house is licensed for weddings and many extras can be arranged such as catering, prior to arrival direct with the owner. Beach 40 yards. Shop, pub and restaurant 2 miles.There is also a loch/sea just 40 yards from the property.

long_description:
This spacious house is set in a delightful position in the coastal town of Rothesay, on the beautiful Isle of Bute. One of the most accessible Scottish islands, the Isle of Bute is just a short ferry ride across the Firth of Clyde. Here you will find the Victoriana meets art deco-style resort of Rothesay with its palm trees and promenade. Bute has some extraordinarily varied landscapes considering it is only 15 miles long and 4 miles wide.
Set over three floors with a main house and annex, Argyle House is a wonderful base for families and friends to come together for a special occasion or family catch-up. The well-equipped kitchen is perfect for rustling up a holiday feast to enjoy together in the impressive dining room, means there is plenty of space to spread out and relax after a busy day.
When you’re ready to explore, the captivating town of Rothesay offers plenty of amenities from independent shops to pubs, bars and restaurants, not to mention the impressive castle ruins and Mount Stuart House. To the north of Rothesay, through the small community of Porth Bannatyne, lies Ettrick Bay, Bute’s most accessible beach, which is a haven for able swimmers· Bute is perfect for cycling, and the circuit of the island on the quiet roads is about 21 miles with none of the hills being too taxing· There are plenty of lovely beaches for a seaside stroll, and there is sea fishing off the piers if you want to try for mackerel and inland there are lochs to catch rainbow trout and pike· The Firth of Clyde is a sailing paradise, and golf enthusiasts are well catered for on the Isle of Bute· This quaint island even has its own gin distillery, definitely worth a visit! Exploring the rest of Scotland could not be easier; simply catch a ferry across to Glasgow and make the most of the fabulous attractions and amenities on offer. Beach 50 yards.

reviews.comment: We spent a week at Argyle House in July 2026, 8 adults and 10 children. Our honest review is that it is a good house but would benefit from quite a lot of attention and TLC. Good points: spacious, multiple bedrooms and bathrooms, two living spaces, beautiful views, short walk to town centre, plentiful free parking on street. Needs attention: the decoration needs attention. Whilst generally neutral there are various damp stains, peeling paper etc. the beds advertised at kingsize were doubles. The rooms were incredibly hot and should have had fans. Various furnishings and fixtures were damaged or broken. The hot tub had clearly been neglected and after a few days was unusable. There's no BBQ. A lot of the kitchen utensils were past their best and missing for example no hand blender. The house should have 2 dishwashers for the size of it. One of toilets was broken and it took days for the plumber to attend and declare it broken.  The TV in the back livingroom doesn't seem to work without a fire stick or similar device. The house has a lot of potential and we had a brilliant week. However, to market itself as luxury and to charge quite a lot of money per week, it needs to come up to scratch. We go away every year as a large group and have stayed in many houses of this type. This was one of the most neglected.
Great place to get the family together.  Plenty of space and so close to local amenities.  What a view to wake up to in the morning - thank you :-)

For those who love the outdoors, the nearby Haughton and Murray Country Park offers an abundance of beautiful walks, and the 18-hole Alford Golf Course is ideal for both experienced and novice players. An ideal location for exploring Aberdeenshire, there is something for everyone, including distilleries, walking, fishing, shooting, cycling and copious famous golf courses. It is an easy commute to the city of Aberdeen and surrounding Aberdeenshire areas and Highlands.

Culzean House is an outstanding country property located in the picturesque village of Ardentinny in the Cowal Peninsula, gateway to the Scottish Highlands. The beautifully appointed holiday house radiates elegance and charm. Boasting homely comforts to create a stylish holiday, perfect for family gatherings and celebrations. Inside, beautifully restored and designed to a high standard, Culzean House is warm and welcoming at any time of the year. The inviting living room is filled with comfortable sofas for cosy winter evenings, "a home from home" where family and friends can relax and enjoy this special place. The adjacent formal dining room is perfect for an evening of celebrations. The generous fully equipped kitchen is complete with all the modern appliances, a superb space for cooking up a feast. In-house catering can be arranged prior to arrival. There is a separate utility room with washer and dryer for guests’ convenience. Seven spacious bedrooms are spread over three levels and each boast individually styled interiors and lovely views out over the gardens and hills beyond. The ground floor features a twin bedroom with an en-suite shower room. The first floor has two elegantly designed double bedrooms, both en-suite, a further double bedroom and a children’s bunk room. This floor also features a designer bathroom, complete with a bath/shower. The second floor has two spacious double bedrooms, both beautifully furnished with stunning views. The house is suitable for 14 guests. For children cots can be arranged and stairgates for safety.
Outside, Culzean House has a magnificent, secluded garden, beautifully manicured with a large area of decking where you can relax in your own private hot tub and Finnish sauna. The views from the south-facing decking area are spectacular, giving stunning uninterrupted views of the glorious Argyll Forest Park beyond. The large, enclosed gardens have pathways and outdoor seating to soak up the breathtaking views. A wonderful area for children to play and explore. Explore Culzean House is conveniently situated at the gateway to the Scottish Highlands and within Loch Lomond & The Trossachs National Park. A perfect base to explore. The surrounding area offers picturesque scenery, forest walks, beach walks and activities such as quad biking, horse riding, river and sea fishing.

This spacious semi-detached village property has been transformed into a retreat offering an outdoor hot tub and sauna, indoor turkish steam room and lounge with a 75" TV. Fully catered packages can be booked in advance direct with the owner, including buffets and dinners, as well as spa treatments.
Tarbolton, close to the town of Ayr, is perhaps best known for its strong connections with Robert Burns, Scotland’s National Bard. In 1780, Burns set up a debating society at a cottage called the Bachelors’ Club. This authentically restored house, now a museum owned by the National Trust for Scotland, is open to the public and visitors can explore the venue where Burns would once debate with other members of the Tarbolton parish.
Ayrshire is home to the Ayrshire Coastal Path, a 100-mile long coastal walk with a fantastic panoramic coastline with views over the sea to the mountains of Arran. The River Ayr Way, a 40-mile source to sea walk is also easily accessed, making this an ideal location for the outdoor enthusiast. The Galloway Forest Park is a short drive away, and is Britain’s largest forest park with 300 square miles of wild beauty waiting to be explored. The park boasts tranquil valleys, rugged rock faces, forest, moorland, lochs and ancient woodland, and a huge diversity of wildlife, including red and roe deer, wild goats and many birds of prey. The park has also been awarded the status of one of only four Dark Sky Parks in the western world and when the sun sets, enthusiasts come to wonder at the universe revealed above. Dalmellington is home to the Scottish Dark Observatory and is only a short drive from the property.
Ayrshire offers many gardens and castles to visit, and activities such as horse riding, racing and golf, and the world famous Royal Troon and Turnberry courses are both close to hand. Culzean Castle and Dumfries House are both spectacular and well worth booking a tour. The islands of Cumbrae, Arran and Bute are all easily reached for a day out, while day trips to Ireland can be taken from Cairnryan. The pretty towns of Troon, Prestwick and Ayr are only a short drive with very good rail links for a trip to the cosmopolitan city of Glasgow and also historic Edinburgh. Loch Lomond and the Trossachs National Park is an hour’s drive. Beach 8 miles. Shop and pub 250 yards, restaurant 2 miles.

Dalgarven House is an exclusive use spa venue. The property can accommodate up to 27, features nine en-suite bedrooms, a private bar area, and function suite/party room, as well as an outdoor 10 seater commercial hot tub and indoor thermal suite exclusively for your use. The hot tub area has mood lighting and additional seating, and is fully fenced off, guaranteeing complete privacy for your group.
Surrounded by the beautiful Ayrshire countryside, the area is known for its gently rolling landscape and is a hugely popular area with walkers and cyclists of all abilities. Ayrshire is home to the Ayrshire coastal path, a 100-mile long coastal walk with one of the finest panoramic coastlines in the British Isles. Crowned with a superb backdrop of the ever-changing profile of the mountains of Arran across the Firth of Clyde, this coastline is steeped in history and teeming with wildlife, including red squirrels, deer, otters and seals, and is a haven for bird watchers.

Culzean Castle, owned by the National Trust for Scotland, is spectacular and is Ayrshire’s most popular tourist attraction. Ayrshire is the heart of ’Burns Country’, steeped in tradition and history. Visit Burns Cottage, The Burns Memorial Museum and the Brig o’ Doon, the bridge from the famous poem Tam o’ Shanter, all of which are a must for Burns fans. Day trips to Ireland can be taken from Cairnryan, whilst a short drive leads to Ayr, a traditional seaside town. Glasgow, Stirling and Edinburgh are perfect for a day out, as is Loch Lomond and The Trossachs National Park, with ferry links to the islands of Arran, Bute and Cumbrae all within easy reach. Beach 7 miles. Shop, pub and restaurant 2 miles.

name: Glendaruel House
short_description: Grand West Coast country house for very large groups, set in extensive grounds with a hot tub, sauna, tennis and games rooms, plus dark skies and easy access to lochs, ferries and coastal scenery.
long_description:
Just 90 minutes from Glasgow, yet set amid the breathtaking scenery of Scotland’s West Coast, this grand estate accommodates up to 36 guests across 13 bedrooms, six spacious reception rooms, and ten bathrooms. Elegantly furnished with antiques and carefully chosen collectables, the property offers a welcoming, relaxed atmosphere where guests of all ages can unwind without worry.
Perfect for family gatherings, corporate retreats, milestone celebrations, weddings, or large reunions, the house can also be combined with neighbouring properties for even bigger groups, providing accommodation for up to 31 bedrooms across the estate.
The estate is packed with entertainment and leisure options. Guests can enjoy a private sauna, seven-seater hot tub, full-size billiard room with snooker table, table football, air hockey, chess, and darts. Outdoors, there is a tennis court, croquet lawn, sunken trampoline, football pitch, two table tennis tables, and acres of grounds for cycling, exploring, or simply relaxing. A dozen shared bicycles and six sets of golf clubs are available, while wildlife enthusiasts may spot deer and red squirrels. With minimal light pollution, the night skies here are truly spectacular.
The property warmly welcomes children and pets. The dining hall, drawing room with baby grand piano and open fire, and billiard room provide elegant spaces for shared meals and classic country living. The drawing room comfortably seats at least twenty, and the dining table accommodates up to twenty-four guests. Two TV rooms with full Sky TV and a playroom featuring a massive dollhouse ensure fun for all ages.
Upstairs, the bedrooms offer flexible sleeping arrangements. Three king-size doubles, a quadruple bunk room, a triple room, and a family bunk room for six cater to larger groups. The remaining seven bedrooms can be configured as super-king doubles, twins, or even triples in some cases. All bedrooms—except the two bunk rooms—have an en-suite or wash-hand basin, complemented by four additional bathrooms and two separate WCs.
The estate’s 22 acres provide endless opportunities for activity and relaxation. Guests can enjoy walking, cycling, swimming, sailing, fishing, riding, stalking, or golf, all within minutes of the property. Situated less than a mile from the top of Loch Riddon in the Kyles of Bute, the location offers year-round natural beauty and abundant wildlife.
Set in Glendaruel on the Cowal peninsula, the surrounding area boasts wooded hills, beaches, lochs, islands, and open countryside. Outdoor enthusiasts will find endless adventures, while historic towns like Dunoon, Rothesay, and Inverary are easily accessible.
Loch Lomond is just 35 minutes away, and nearby Colintraive provides ferry access to the Isle of Bute, with additional ferries from Portavadie connecting to Tarbert, the Mull of Kintyre, Campbeltown, and the islands beyond.

long_description:
Edderton Hall is perfectly situated in the beautiful Montgomeryshire countryside and commands panoramic views across the Severn Valley towards Powis Castle and beyond. An outstanding country house perfect for a family get together.
The property consists of a sweeping driveway and as you go through the front door, you have a large living room with a wood burning stove and Smart TV leading to a games room with bar area and a separate children’s playroom. There is a second living room with wood burner and Smart TV leading to a formal dining room, large open plan kitchen with a second dining table and garden room. There is alsoa utility room with a washing machine and tumble dryer. The ground floor bedroom has level access and may be suitable for less mobile guests and the dining room has a large dining table.
There are many local attractions all within a short car journey, including National Trust properties such as Powis Castle, Attingham Park estate in the medieval town of Shrewsbury and Chirk Castle. Offas Dyke, Glyndwr Way and the River Severn are also close by. The market towns of Oswestry and Welshpool are within a short drive. Chester is a 1½ hours away and Shrewsbury is just 30 minutes’ away by car. All offer a large array of shops and restaurants for guests to enjoy. For the more active guests, there is a great selection of walks, such as the Llanymynech Rocks nature reserve, or for those looking for longer walks, the Shropshire Hills is an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty all well worth a visit. Please do not charge Electric Vehicles at the property - there is Tesco’s within a couple miles which has charging points, alongside the main car park which has charging points for you to use.

reviews.comment: Thank you Mike for welcoming us.  I always think it’s a nice thing when the owner/host is able to do that in person. Lovely place and facilities. The separate hot tub with stunning views was enjoyed as was the bbq area. The pool table was a win (cues a little worse for wear but we bought some new tips for you!).  We were lucky as the weather was fab. Walked to local village, some of us swam by the waterfall and plunge pool and also had time to canoe in Shrewsbury and visit the Castle.  All in all fab

We were a family of 21 (ages 5-76) celebrating different achievements. The house was perfect for what we wanted with great outdoor area that the children enjoyed. Not too far in a car to different amenities and attractions. The house had lots of room for everyone, never under each others feet and plenty of rooms to escape too. Kitchen was well equipped, just needed a few bigger pans, but minor detail. Overall we had a great week away and hosts easy to get hold of. One suggested improvement from the children is to separate the field into 2 sections: one for dogs and one for children to play on.

A lovely house in a beautiful setting was our “home” for a week, more than enough bedrooms for our whole family of 17. Just to sit outside and enjoy the wonderful views, to me, was all that was needed for a relaxing time. The weather was gorgeous, so what more could we ask for. ***

long_description:
In a rural setting, but less than 5 miles east of the seaside town of Aberystwyth, and with beautiful views of the Rheidol Valley, Maesbangor Farmhouse is a large property with lots of room to spread out. Previously two homes, but now combined into one, this spacious semi-detached house offers seven bedrooms sleeping up to 14 guests.
The imposing front of the house looks across the valley, and the front garden even boasts a hot tub where you can relax and take in the view. As you enter inside you will appreciate how ideal the farmhouse is for families or friends who want that extra space, or perhaps a quiet corner. There is a large beamed dining room with a feature wood burner. Leading off is a conservatory overlooking the enclosed terrace with benches and tables as well as a small lawn. The kitchen, complete with a breakfast area, is well-equipped with everything you need to cook up a tasty treat.
On the other side of the house there is a living room with 50" Freeview TV and wood burner, as well as an additional living room. Also on this side of the house you’ll find kitchen number two; smaller than the first but still well-equipped. There are two staircases that lead to the first floor, one leading to four bedrooms, all en-suite, and the other leading to three further bedrooms, one of which is en-suite, and a family bathroom. This is the perfect location for a family holiday, or a break with a group of friends.
Imagine yourself sitting on the the sandy beach overlooking Cardigan Bay, watching dolphins, or perhaps exploring one of the many market towns in the surrounding area. The Victorian resort of Aberystwyth, with its electric cliff railway, promenade and pier, is close by, as is the compelling Cambrian Mountains, dotted with hill sheep farms, forest and lakeland. Take a meandering train ride on what was once a working link between the local lead mines and the harbour; the Vale of Rheidol Railway now runs a steam train service through the Rheidol Valley to Devil’s Bridge, where you can see the famous Mynach Falls, Devil’s Punch Bowl and Jacob’s Ladder. When you’re done with exploring for the day, come back and relax at Maesbangor Farmhouse or visit the gastro pub, situated within half a mile of the house. Beach 6 miles. Shop, pub and restaurant ½ mile.

long_description:
Immerse yourself in the magnificence of this stunning former farmhouse of Fountain Hill Farm which is set on its own in the ‘picture-postcard’ Pembrokeshire countryside. It has fabulous views of the Preseli Hills, while a tributary of the River Nevern meanders at the bottom of the orchard. This grand farmhouse is teeming with character and offers a very high level of comfort throughout, with solid oak floors, beams and an original inglenook fireplace, which really do complement this property. A natural stone porch opens into a large reception area which features a wood burner set in a Welsh stone inglenook fireplace with a slate hearth, and oak stairs to the first floor. A dining room adds to the character and charm, with exposed stonework and a bespoke dining table. Here you can enjoy formal dining with family and friends, or maybe enjoy a barbecue al fresco on the patio, where there are uninterrupted views over the beautiful Preseli Hills, or just relax in your private hot tub. In the evening, you can retire to one of the two living rooms complete with a cosy wood burner - this property really does offer everything for that perfect getaway. The large master suite offers fantastic views, with even your very own observatory making the most of the magnificent views here at Fountain Hill.
Positioned at the foothills of the Preseli Hills, it lies close to the quaint hamlet of Eglwyswrw, and is conveniently on the doorstep of the Pembrokeshire Coast National Park, which offers fantastic walks through the hills and on the coastal paths, as well as horse riding, fishing on the Rivers Teifi and Nevern, and even sea fishing and wildlife spotting. There is also golf within 8 miles, as well as kayaking nearby. The historic market town of Cardigan is only a 15-minute drive away, and nearby are a host of beautiful beaches such as Poppit and Newport Sands or Cwm-Yr-Eglwys and Pwllgwaelod. This rugged and sublime Pembrokeshire coastline really is worth a visit. The historic market town of Cardigan has a bustling high street featuring the famous Cardigan Castle, many antique and craft shops, together with an abundance of restaurants and cafés. Travelling south, you can discover the famous walled town of Tenby with its award-winning beach, or take a trip to Caldey Island or Oakwood (Wales’ largest theme park) or the award-winning Folly Farm Adventure Park and Zoo, all of which will make the perfect day out. Beach 9 miles. Shop 2 miles, pub and restaurant 3½ miles.

long_description:
Welcome to Llwyncelyn Farmhouse. This charming holiday retreat is nestled in the picturesque Pembrokeshire countryside near the village of Clynderwen. This spacious seven-bedroom farmhouse is the perfect escape for families and groups comfortably accommodating up to fourteen guests (plus two infants in cots). One of the highlights of Llwyncelyn Farmhouse is the luxurious, fast-heating Finnish hot tub where you can indulge in a soothing soak while gazing out at the breathtaking countryside vistas across to the Preseli Hills.
As you step inside Llwyncelyn Farmhouse, you’ll be greeted by the inviting ambience of this lovingly restored farmhouse. The centrepiece of the home is the large open plan kitchen-dining room, complete with modern appliances and ample seating around the farmhouse table, perfect for socialising and enjoying delicious meals together. French doors lead from the dining area onto a patio, where you can dine al fresco and soak up the tranquillity of the surrounding landscape. The spacious living room offers a cosy retreat, featuring a flame-effect electric stove and a Smart TV for relaxing evenings with loved ones.
A well-stocked bookcase including local interest books plus numerous board and other games complete your evening entertainment. Patio doors open onto the large gardens, where you can unwind amidst stunning views across to the Preseli Hills. The ground floor also boasts a convenient twin bedroom with adjustable beds and an en-suite shower room, ideal for guests seeking ease of access. Upstairs, you will find six further beautifully appointed bedrooms, providing comfortable accommodation for everyone in your party.
Llywncelyn Farmhouse is perfectly located for a plethora of activities for the whole family. Those who enjoy walking and outdoor life can find the Preseli Hills half an hour’s drive away heading north; the Pembrokeshire coastal path can be found to the south and west and can be easily reached by car. Narberth, with its quirky shops, restaurants and quaint cafes, is a short 12-minute drive away. Further south, the bustling seaside resort of Tenby, also renowned for its medieval walls, can be reached in half an hour.
For young families, a visit to the area would not be complete without a trip to the county’s premier theme parks including Heatherton World of Activities and Folly Farm among many others. Those wishing to venture further afield will find the city of St David’s, with its magnificent cathedral; Pembroke Castle; boat trips to the islands of Skomer and Skokholm; the National Botanic Gardens of Wales and Laugharne, of Dylan Thomas fame, all within an hour’s drive. National Trust and Cadw members should not forget their membership cards as they take advantage of castles, gardens woodlands and car parking in the area.

reviews.comment: We had fantastic weekend at Llwyncelyn Farmhouse and a really warm welcome from our host Madeline. The house was spotlessly clean and was stocked with absolutely everything we needed for a self catering break. There was so much space that even with a large group, you don’t feel like you’re on top of each other. The toys, cots, plates and cutlery for the children were a really welcome surprise. The views are spectacular and the hot tub is perfect for relaxing in. Thank you so much for your hospitality Madeline. We hope to be back soon.

Absolutely stunning farmhouse had everything you needed in it. Well thought out. Madeline and Marc are the most amazing hosts and they were there for any communication that was needed and from start to finish were always happy to help. The views were incredible. The hot tub was very spacious and relaxing. Would highly recommend staying here there was only one downside and that was that we had to leave 🥹 Also there’s Hugo who fast became the love of my life he is part of the farmhouse we were told he could be kept out if didn’t want any animals around but honestly he’s the best part of the stay he’s the friendliest dog in the world.

A beautifully presented and well equipped house perfect for us as a large intergenerational family. We were made to feel very welcome on arrival by the hosts and the welcome box and homemade cake was a lovely treat after our long journey. The hosts were available during our stay should we have needed anything. The kitchen, lounge and outside spaces all had ample comfortable seating for the number of guests enabling us to relax together as a family and everyone enjoyed the hot tub. Two ovens in the kitchen and plenty of crockery and cutlery meant catering was easy and there was ample fridge and freezer space. Our little ones were delighted with the indoor and outdoor toys and there was plenty of space for the dogs in the secure garden. The dogs appreciated the dog treats too! Llwyncelyn Farmhouse is the best place we have stayed with our family in recent years and we would definitely highly recommend.

long_description:
Meusydd is a stunning holiday cottage set on the beautiful west Wales coast, offering the perfect base for a memorable staycation with family or friends. With unspoilt sea views and a private, covered swim spa, it comfortably sleeps up to 14 guests across seven spacious bedrooms—including six kingsize rooms (four with en-suites) and one twin room. Ideal for large groups or multi-generational holidays, the bedrooms are thoughtfully arranged over both the ground and first floors for easy access. The property also features two additional family bathrooms, including a modern ground-floor wet room—perfect for rinsing off after a day at the beach, just a short walk away.
Inside, the open-plan kitchen, living and dining area is bright, social, and beautifully designed to make the most of the coastal setting, with large doors leading out to the sea-facing terrace. It’s a fantastic space for entertaining, whether you’re preparing a meal in the well-equipped kitchen (complete with two ovens), sharing a family breakfast, or enjoying drinks as the sun sets over the water. Additional features include a utility room with a washing machine, dryer, iron, ironing board, and extra fridge/freezer to help you feel right at home. There is also private parking for up to three vehicles and a payable electric vehicle charging point for added convenience.
Step outside to a private, enclosed garden and terrace, where you can dine al fresco with breathtaking views of the coastline, unwind in the luxury swim spa, or simply relax under the veranda—perfect in any weather. Half of the kingsize bedrooms enjoy views over the Cardigan coast, allowing you to wake each morning to the sound and scent of the sea. Renovated at the beginning of 2020, Meusydd combines the comfort of a boutique hotel with the freedom and privacy of your own seaside retreat. Please note that the hot tub is available for use until 10pm daily, and we kindly ask guests to respect the peace and privacy of our neighbours.
Ideally located just across the road from Cardigan Golf Club and within walking distance of local beaches, Meusydd offers easy access to all the highlights of Cardigan and Gwbert. Whether you’re walking the coastal path, visiting local eateries, or simply soaking up the views, this well-appointed cottage is the perfect setting for your Welsh coastal escape. These properties can also be booked together to accommodate up to 120 people, making it ideal for larger gatherings. For security and peace of mind, please note that external areas of the property are monitored by CCTV.

reviews.comment: The house is beautiful, in a stunning location, with magnificent views of the sea, and sunsets. We had a wonderful stay and visited the local beaches, walks, and enjoyed a meal at the Gwbert Hotel and drinks at The Cliff Hotel. We would highly recommend and would definitely book again. It was a first time for myself staying in the beautiful Cardigan Bay because I usually holiday in Pembrokeshire. I was not disappointed and would love to return. The house was perfect for our families and dog.

For the last 14 years we have been using holiday homes around the country as venues for our family, up to 10 adults and 2 children, pre-Christmas get together. Meusydd ranks very highly among the best we’ve used.The 7 bedrooms are good sized bright and comfortable. The social accommodation combining a large lounge with ample sofa space for all the family, dining area with big table and a very well appointed kitchen is great. Outside there is also a large covered hot tub and an outdoor eating area with views of the coast. Meusydd, part of the Gwbert Holiday group, sits close to the coast path, has fabulous views over the Teifi estuary and is a short drive from Cardigan. We also had a very good meal at the Flatrock Bistro in the Gwbert Hotel just a short walk away. The property was very well maintained and the provision of kitchen equipment and tableware is the best I’ve seen in 14 yearsIn summary a very comfortable well appointed holiday home for families and friends

It was an ideal venue for a family gathering of 14 with all we needed for a thoroughly enjoyable and comfortable stay. Spacious, luxurious and relaxing. We definitely recommend it and would love to return.

long_description:
Enjoying a fabulous rural location close to the banks of the Llangollen canal, on the owners’ working sheep and cattle farm, this charming complex of four cottages, Y Stabl (ref UK12742), Cor Tarw (ref UK12743), Ty Felin (ref UK12744) and Ty Godro (ref UK12745) have been skilfully converted from a range of former farm buildings to offer truly delightful, modern and spacious holiday accommodation. Each lovely barn enjoys its own private enclosed garden and each boasts a fabulous hot tub, perfect for relaxing after a busy day exploring this wonderful corner of Wales. These adjoining cottages would make a fabulous location for large groups and families holidaying together.
The location is perfect for exploring the very best of North Wales and the border lands, outdoor enthusiasts will certainly delight in the myriad of activities on offer nearby. These include white water rafting, mountain bike trails, canoeing, golf and excellent walking and birdwatching. Close by lies the lovely town of Llangollen where visitors will find an abundance of interesting shops, inns and restaurants and great attractions including horse drawn canal boat trips and historic steam train journeys. From here, there are narrowboat trips across the famous Pontcysyllte aqueduct, the highest and longest on the whole canal system, and the surrounding Dee Valley is a breathtakingly beautiful backdrop for climbing, abseiling and gorge walking. Sitting high above Llangollen are the mysterious ruins of Dinas Bran Castle, the legendary hiding place of the Holy Grail, and well worth the walk to take in the fabulous views, whilst Chirk with its lovely National Trust castle is also close by. Other attraction include Zip World, Chester Zoo, Snowdonia Nation Park and the city of Wrexham to name but a few.
The cottages are located within easy access to road and rail links, with three railway stations within 10 miles. Manchester and Liverpool airports are just an hour’s drive away. Also within easy reach is the pretty market town of Shrewsbury, as well as the cities of Chester and Birmingham. Shop 2 miles and pub 1 mile.
The properties can be booked together to accommodate up to 32 guests.

long_description:
Perfect for a large family gathering or celebration, Oswald House offers spacious and stylish accommodation for a splendid holiday. The vast kitchen and dining space is the social hub of the home and large bi-fold doors open up onto the outside space with a superb hot tub and barbecue; the ideal spot for relaxing in after a busy day sightseeing. Situated in the village of Llanon with a pub and shops within walking distance, this holiday home is the perfect base for immersing yourself in all that the area has to offer. With a superb mix of coast and countryside, Ceredigion is a large and beautiful place to visit. Award-winning beaches, perfect coves, iconic castles and pretty harbours make days out by car or on foot along the 60 miles of Heritage coastline a must. This region inspired Dylan Thomas to write some of his finest poetry. It is framed by the Cambrian Mountains, known as the backbone of Wales, and is so rich in wildlife, legends and fascinating landscapes. Look out for birds of prey such as red kites and buzzards soaring high above, and dolphins or seals in the waters. Drive along the Plynlimon Mountains, through the Tywi Forest or visit the impressive Abergwesyn Pass, and marvel at the solitude.
For a truly authentic Welsh family holiday experience, this is the area to be. The locals are justifiably proud of this region with its rich local folklore which tells of tricking the devil, mermaids, shipwrecked kings and princesses, and even an explanation of why gulls sound as if they’re crying. The little gems of Georgian Aberaeron, historic Cardigan, salty New Quay, traditional Tregaron and Lampeter are waiting to be explored. To the south, the coves of Mwnt, Cwmtydu, Penbryn, Tresaith – which resemble illustrations from books about pirates, are all within easy reach. To the north, around Aberystwyth and Borth, there are vast stretches of sand. Food plays a big part in the experience of Ceredigion, and a wide choice is to be found in the shops, restaurants and cafés offering regional products and ingredients such as the world beating Teifi Valley cheeses, the ubiquitous Welsh cakes, bara brith and of course, some spectacularly good seafood from the coast.
No visit to the area would be complete without a ride on the steam railway. From the coast at Aberystwyth, watch the scenery change whilst travelling through ancient woodland and rugged mountain scenery, with the line clinging to the hillside to reach Devil’s Bridge, home of the famous Mynach Falls and Devil’s Punchbowl. Come and escape to this magnificent area and let Oswald House be your home for a holiday to remember!
Beach ½ mile. Shop, pub and restaurant 600 yards. This property can be booked together with Ty Fynnon (HW7601) and Oswald Lodge (HW7804) to accommodate larger groups.

long_description:
The Anchorage is one of the finest Georgian houses nestled within the historic market town of Pembroke and only a 10 minute walk to Pembroke Castle, the scenic Millponds, restaurants, cafés and shops. This spacious luxury holiday home has been meticulously restored back to its former glory with many original features retained, including decorative coving, wide staircase, feature fireplaces and shutters. It offers the perfect place for family and friends to come together for a wonderful holiday or to celebrate that special occasion. The Anchorage has been stylishly furnished throughout, with comfort being a priority.
This delightful property is spread over four floors and boasts five en-suite bathrooms, a separate family bathroom and a wet room, an elegant living room with high ceilings and a butler’s pantry to prepare a relaxed drink or two in the evenings after a busy day on the beach or a long walk along the beautiful Pembrokeshire Coastal Path.
On the lower ground floor, the open plan kitchen/dining area is perfect for entertaining, and is well equipped with a large focal island including breakfast bar, two dishwashers and two fridges to make your stay as relaxing as possible. Children will enjoy the cosy cinema room, and there is a fabulous hot tub for all to enjoy and unwind in. Outside is ’The Wash House’, where you will find the washing machine, tumble dryer, iron and ironing board, as well as a wet room with shower, toilet, wash hand basin and extra space for walking boots and coats. For those bringing bikes, there is an outdoor, floor-mounted cycle rack for three bicycles.
The bustling coastal resort of Tenby is within easy reach and is renowned for its picturesque harbour, narrow cobbled streets and pastel painted Georgian houses. It has a variety of boutique gift shops, traditional pubs and highly acclaimed restaurants. Take a boat trip to the historic island of Caldey, with its Celtic monastery and Cistercian monks, who have made it a holy island for hundreds of years. Away from the coast, explore the rolling hills of Preseli and discover its ancient sites dotted along its rugged terrain. For keen walkers the Pembrokeshire Coast National Park offering 186 miles of truly sublime walks is close by. Folly Farm Zoo, and Heatherton World of Activites are within a 30-minute drive. Pembroke Railway Station is just a 5-minute walk from the property. Stunning beaches just 4 miles away!

long_description:
Delve into Y Dorlan, as you arrive you will sweep down a private driveway surrounded by paddocks to approach this architect-designed, truly unique lodge, nestled on the banks of the River Teifi. The encompassing gardens reach down to the river banks. Y Dorlan really is the perfect base from which to explore the local charms of the bustling, historic market town of Cardigan, on the edge of the dramatic Ceredigion coastline.
This beautiful lodge is full of character and features a large, spiral, open-tread staircase in the grand hallway with some rooms focusing on the views of the meandering river. You may prefer to get a closer view of the Teifi from the sun terrace, relaxing with a glass of wine in your private hot tub, or star gazing into the clear night sky. Al fresco dining is sublime, with a large built in barbecue to cook your catch of the day. Imagine waking up and heading for the sauna followed by swim in your indoor swimming pool - truly magnificent! The garden also boasts a giant draughts set and there is even a helicopter landing pad, for those who want to arrive in style!
This lodge is perfect for families and larger groups who want to explore the three counties of Ceredigion, Pembrokeshire and Carmarthenshire. Just a stone’s throw across the River Teifi is the Welsh Wildlife Centre which is one of the best wetland reserves in Wales, where a huge diversity of wildlife is waiting to be discovered. You may prefer to explore the Cardigan Bay Marine Wildlife Centre where you can learn how to spot dolphins, porpoise and Atlantic grey seals.
Cardigan Castle has undergone a major renovation project, and with over 900 years of history is well worth a visit. For those keen to explore the area on foot, the coastal footpath is truly wonderful, or inland, explore the Preseli Hills.
Please note: There are open, steep, spiral or narrow stairs at the property.

Oil central heating (underfloor on ground floor), electricity, bed linen, towels and Wi-Fi included. Travel cot available on request. Highchair and stairgate. Welcome pack. External utility room with washing machine and tumble dryer (shared with other properties on-site). Lawned garden with decked sitting-out area, garden furniture and gas BBQ. Courtyard with bar area, gas BBQ, pizza oven, table tennis and gas firepits (shared). Swim spa. hot tub (private). Fishing on-site (licence required). Bike store. Electric vehicle charging point. Private parking for 3 cars. 2 small dogs welcome. No smoking. Please note: There is a step in the garden, and unfenced ponds in the grounds, 80 yards away.

Perched on the Dale Peninsula, high above the crashing waves and just 300 yards from the Pembrokeshire Coastal Path, Musselwick Farm Luxury Cottages enjoy truly sublime sea views, nestled within the owners 232-acre arable farm. The Millhouse is one of five superbly finished and unique cottages that have been individually designed and styled to offer the perfect luxurious stay. Situated between the coastal village of Marloes and the picture-postcard hamlet of St Brides, this wonderful collection of exquisite cottages have been meticulously transformed from the original farm buildings to offer the perfect stay for family and friends.
This large detached cottage offers a spacious open plan living, dining and kitchen area, with a focal island with solid oak worktops and Belfast sinks. There is a decked terrace just off the living room, and the master suite on the ground floor provides a lovely four poster bed. All bedrooms have been lovingly furnished and enjoy their own en-suite facilities. Outside, guests can enjoy the shared courtyard area, where you can have a go at making pizzas, or perhaps light the BBQ and dine alresco whilst enjoying the fresh sea air sat around the fire pit. For the children, there’s table tennis and five-a-side football, and for those who enjoy fishing, there are trout and course fishing ponds.
Nearby, enjoy the golden sands of Marloes or take a boat trip to Skomer Island to discover a host of wildlife and sealife. Surrounded by rolling countryside and a plethora of walks from the doorstep, you won’t be short on things to see and do. The coastal resort of Little Haven provides a selection of highly acclaimed restaurants and traditional Welsh pubs. A visit to the area would not be complete without a memorable trip to the small city of St David’s, where a plethora of eclectic gift shops, stylish cafés, tasteful restaurants and the iconic 12th century cathedral can be discovered. Alternatively, for those looking for an adrenaline adventure, head east and visit the award-winning theme parks of Heatherton, Oakwood or Folly Farm, famed for its roller coasters, fascinating wildlife and family entertainment.
The Millhouse can be booked together with The Cornstore (UK32513), The Stables (UK32514), The Cart House (UK32515) and The Cowshed (UK32570) to accommodate upto 30 guests.

long_description:
These ten wonderful, detached holiday homes offer ample space for larger families or groups, in lovingly furnished accommodation designed with guest comfort in mind. Each charming home has its own private garden and hot tub, perfect for al fresco dining followed by a dip in the bubbles!
The accommodation offers a light and airy space in which to unwind or entertain after a busy day of exploration. The well-equipped kitchens are sure to please the chef in the family, complete with a fridge/freezer and dishwasher.
Riversmouth (17809) accommodates up to 12 guests and is set across three floors, offering ample space in which to unwind. On the ground floor are two twin bedrooms and a shower room, ideal for the less mobile. The first floor houses one kingsize room and a family bathroom, while on the second floor, there is a double room with ensuite, a kingsize room with ensuite, and one twin room. Outside is a small garden, private parking for three cars and a private hot tub, ensuring you are well catered for.
With breath-taking views over Cardigan Bay, the properties are located just 100 yards from the cliff top. Gwbert-on-Sea is a small, quiet hamlet on the shore of the mouth of the Teifi Estuary, just a couple of miles outside Cardigan. The settlement takes its name from the wandering St Gwbert, said to have landed here and taken shelter in a cave. The shoreline is marked by rugged cliffs and small shingle bays, with large stretches of sandbank exposed at low tide, and the area gives superb views over a diverse and scenic landscape. The ancient oak woodland of the Teifi Valley, the tidal marshes of the estuary, and the boundary of the Pembrokeshire Coast National Park can all be appreciated from here.
The 18-hole golf course at Cardigan Golf Club also offers fine views of the estuary and sea, and from the headland, you can look across to Cardigan Island. The mud and sand flats of the estuary attract a great variety of birds, and in the autumn waders such as the redshank, oystercatcher and curlew can be seen feeding here, along with several species of migrating duck. The headland of Craig y Gwbert is the site of an Iron Age Fort, with pieces of pottery found near Gwbert, now on display in Cardigan Museum. All the outside areas are covered by CCTV. Beach 7 miles. Shop 3½ miles, pub and restaurant 500 yards.
These properties can be booked together to accommodate 120 people.
Please kindly note that outside areas are covered by CCTV.
One pet dog is welcome to join you on your holiday, please state upon booking as additional charges apply. Guests who arrive at the with their dog without prior arrangement may not be accommodated. Whilst we are able to accommodate pet dogs, all other animals are not permitted.

We loved the en-suite bathrooms and the supplied toiletries were very nice too. The hot tub and swim spa were a great feature but seemed a little tired - headrests were damaged or missing.  The kitchen was well equipped but could have perhaps benefited from having a supply of salt/pepper/oil.  We experienced an issue with one of the appliances which was immediately dealt with by the maintenance team at Gwbert Holidays.  We were a multi generation family group, and the house facilities were exceptionally good if you have a baby with you. the location near the Cliff Hotel was brilliant for meals and drinks, and we had a couple of rounds of golf too. Overall a fantastic experience - we are coming back next year and hopefully stayi by at the same house.

We had a wonderful stay at this cottage. The sea views were absolutely amazing and one of the highlights of our trip. The cottage was spacious, comfortable, and had plenty of room to relax. A lovely place to stay and enjoy the surroundings.

Tŷ Môr is perfectly situated on the Cardigan Bay coast with truly enviable uninterrupted sea views and boasts your very own Swimspa to make the most of those magnificent views. Newly constructed in 2023 to a very high standard this spacious holiday cottage is modern and beautifully finished with everything you could need for a relaxing break by the sea. Here, family and friends can get together for the ultimate breakaway. Nestled within Gwbert-on-Sea a small coastal hamlet on the shore of the mouth of the Teifi Estuary and just a couple of miles from the historic market town of Cardigan where you will find a host of shops, galleries, theatre, restaurants, and Cardigan Castle. Offering five spacious kingsize bedrooms plus a family room and one super king/twin, you receive the pleasures of a hotel stay with the convenience of having everyone under the same roof.

The luxurious bedrooms will make you feel like you’re waking up in a 5* hotel and most bedrooms deliver a spectacular sea view, so you can wake up to watch the waves crashing against Cardigan Island.
Tŷ Môr is kitted out with all the mod cons and luxury features that you don’t come across very often. Enjoy complimentary FabFour coffee in your bean-to-cup coffee machine to kick start your morning whilst taking in the sunrise over the Ceredigion coast. Ease those aching muscles in your private hot tub or start your day off with a gentle swim in the swim spa. Come evening, enjoy a barbecue whilst watching the sun go down, and sit around the firepit reminiscing on the day’s activities. Conveniently, Gwbert Hotel and The Cliff Hotel and Spa are a short walk away so you’re never too far from a member of staff, delicious meals should you not feel like cooking or wish to make use of the excellent spa facilities, available at an additional charge, pre-booking is essential.

long_description:
Discover Willington Lodge, a truly luxurious Grade II listed Georgian country home set in the north Wales and Cheshire border. This incredible property has that all important wow factor that sets your holiday apart from all others. Sleeping up to eighten guests, you and your loved ones will be living life to the highest levels of splendid! Upon arrival, you are greeted by the classic Georgian architecture with beautiful white detailing and elegant hedgerows. This wonderfully grand holiday home is the definition of luxury. Throughout, you will find period features that are quintessential to English sophistication that makes Willington Lodge a truly magnificent place to make memories that last a lifetime.
The grounds are as impressive as the property itself. With grand lawns, walled garden, court yards, and quiet ponds, you will find something special everywhere you discover. With gardens and facilities like the ones on offer at Willington Lodge, you will appreciate why it is regarded as one of the area’s top rural wedding venues. For wedding services, please contact the venue directly.
Ideally located for a rural retreat, far enough away from civilisation but close enough to not feel isolated. Willington Lodge is only 10 minutes from the popular market town of Whitchurch and the picturesque town of Ellesmere you will find a perfect country hideaway. Whitchurch offers a wealth of independent shops, cafés, bars and restaurants to suit all tastes. Add the weekly country market, monthly farmers’ market, a wide range of independent specialist shops, lovely coffee shops, the many traditional pubs and inns which offer good food and beers, the interesting mix of buildings and you have the ideal place to discover on your holiday. Ellesmere, only 10 minutes away has developed into a vibrant market town with numerous of Georgian and half-timbered buildings. Ellesmere prides itself on its individual and independent shops – some have been in the same family for generations. Chester and Shrewsbury are both only half an hour away.
With Shrewsbury approximately 30 minutes’ drive away, there’s a variety of things to do making it a great day out. Shrewsbury is full of finds to be discovered by foot or by boat, the River Severn is a must, as is the café culture, the castle and the churches that dominate Shrewsbury’s famous skyline.
In the other direction and approximately 30 minutes’ drive away again, is the historical city of Chester with its excellent shopping and famous races, with the Blue Planet Aquarium close by and of course Chester Zoo, there are so many options.
Throughout the year there are numerous food festivals and regattas. It’s a great place to visit. For the more adventurous travel seekers there are various walks and outdoor activities nearby including The Mercian Way which is part of the award-winning National Cycle Network. Overton-on-Dee which is surrounded by a forty-mile network of interconnecting public footpaths and bridleways, all of them readily accessible from the village. From taking a stroll around the beautiful gardens to exploring the woodlands and countryside, even just sitting back relaxing and taking in the tranquillity of the house. Willington Lodge promises an idyllic holiday retreat.
Please note: There are open, steep, spiral or narrow stairs at the property.

reviews.comment: Fantastic house! Everything about the house is immaculate. Highly recommend to anyone wanting to stay as a family, lots of space to socialise as a group but plenty of space to hang out to get your own space too. The house is well equipped with everything you need, the bedrooms are all large and tastefully decorated. We particularly enjoyed the gardens and garden room as a family. Hope to return in the future! :)

Just returned after our week long stay at Willington Lodge and the only word that can describe this place is SPLENDID! There was 18 of us and the house was the perfect size - big enough to spread out yet not so big that you felt you didn’t see anyone! The outside space is utterly beautiful, the walled garden with the sun loungers and hot tub were a huge hit with everyone. The paddock was the perfect place for cricket, badminton and croquet - which we spent many hours doing. We used the bbq almost every night as we were so lucky with the weather and ate in the covered outdoor space which comfortably seated all of us together. The local area has lots to do - we went paddle boarding at Ellesmere, karting at Rednal Karting and had a great adventure at Hawkstone Park Follies. We had great meals at The Boat House (Ellesmere) and Cross Foxes (Erbistock right on the river). Overall we had the most incredible stay, comfortable rooms, great bathrooms with hot showers and most importantly, memories made with family. Thank you to Willington Lodge for being such great hosts, the detailed tour on arrival from the owner was so helpful. We absolutely cannot wait to come back again to make more memories!

long_description:
Occupying an elevated position amid the beautiful Denbighshire countryside, Clwyd Gate Manor is an extraordinary luxury retreat with panoramic views across the Vale of Clwyd and Clwydian Range. Sleeping up to twenty four guests across eleven bedrooms, this award-winning property provides an unforgettable setting for large family holidays, group escapes and corporate stays.
Designed with both relaxation and entertainment in mind, the manor’s spectacular facilities include a heated indoor swimming pool, separate children’s pool and sauna. Outside, guests can unwind in the hillside hot tub while admiring the surrounding countryside or gather around the large firepit beneath the stars.
The stylish living spaces offer plenty of room for everyone. A state-of-the-art kitchen with a central island makes group catering straightforward, while the elegant dining room seats thirty guests together. The adjoining lounge features comfortable seating, a log burner and doors opening onto a glass-fronted balcony with far-reaching views.
Entertainment continues on the second floor, where an impressive games room contains a pool table, table football, bar, board games and a large Smart television. The medieval-style sandstone cave bar provides a wonderfully distinctive place to enjoy evening drinks.
Each of the eleven bedrooms is located on the ground floor and has its own Smart television. Flexible arrangements include king-size, super king-size, twin beds, while the four-poster Celebration Suite features an en-suite bathroom and freestanding bath. Several bedrooms open directly onto the extensive enclosed veranda, allowing guests to wake up to spectacular countryside scenery. Entry to the main house facilities is located on a private pathway in.
Clwyd Gate Manor is situated near Ruthin, a historic market town known for its attractive architecture, independent shops and excellent food. Visitors can explore Ruthin Castle, discover the town’s darker history at Ruthin Gaol or visit Nantclwyd y Dre, one of Wales’ oldest dated timber-framed houses. Ruthin Craft Centre also showcases contemporary applied arts.
The surrounding Clwydian Range and Dee Valley National Landscape offers outstanding opportunities for walking, cycling and outdoor adventures. Follow scenic routes across rolling hills, climb Moel Famau for impressive views or explore the woodland trails and limestone cliffs of Loggerheads Country Park.
The charming town of Llangollen is another rewarding destination, offering riverside walks, independent shops and journeys aboard its heritage railway. Historic Mold and the cathedral city of Chester are also within driving distance, providing further choices for shopping, dining and sightseeing.
For a coastal day out, guests can visit the beaches of Prestatyn and Rhyl or travel farther west to Llandudno and Conwy. The mountains, lakes and forests of Eryri National Park are equally accessible for memorable days in the Welsh landscape. Combining exceptional accommodation, private spa facilities and magnificent views, Clwyd Gate Manor promises a truly remarkable North Wales escape.

long_description:
Oil central heating (underfloor on lower ground and ground floor), electricity, bed linen, towels and Wi-Fi included. Initial logs for wood burners included. Travel cot and highchair available on request. Stairgate. Welcome pack. Lawned garden with patio, garden furniture and BBQ. Balcony. 2-acre natural grounds with children’s play area (shared with other property on-site). Hot tub for 6 (private). 2 dogs welcome, to be kept on a lead at all times (sheep country). Private parking for 4 cars. Wheelchair access. No smoking. Please note: Sorry, no hen or stag parties. The patio is raised (with ramp access) and the property has a natural water supply from a borehole. This property has a security deposit of £150.

This stunning, detached, barn conversion has been lovingly crafted to provide a beautiful holiday home for all the family. Spread over four levels, there’s a central ‘atrium’ with views out over the peaceful countryside, with a glass-sided lift connecting all levels – ideal if a member of your party is less mobile or uses a wheelchair. There are wonderful A frame joists throughout this light and airy property, with the main living room, dining room and kitchen being in the central part of the house. On the ground floor there’s also a lovely sun room opening out onto a balcony overlooking the surrounding countryside, a games and media room with PlayStation 4, table football, electric organ, and a curved 65" Smart TV with Blu-ray player – ideal for the full cinema experience! There’s also a playroom packed with toys, games and jigsaw puzzles for the younger members of your party. Two of the bedrooms are on this floor, whilst there are four upstairs on the first floor, from where a minstrel’s gallery overlooks the staircase. On the lower ground floor you’ll find a further double bedroom and living room, together with a niftily concealed kitchenette – ideal for grandparents staying with family but who like their own space!
No such holiday property would be complete without a hot tub, and you’ll find the one at Y Beudy has some of the finest views from any hot tub as you while away the evenings watching the sun go down. There’s also a fabulous elevated patio area, with ramped access, giving further fantastic views, and an exciting children’s play area which is shared with the owner’s other holiday property. Ruthin is just 4 miles away, home to the Ruthin Craft Centre, and the former Ruthin Gaol, here you will find a great selection of eateries and individual shops in the streets radiating down the hill from the centre of town. A little further afield is Llandegla Forest with its mountain bike centre and great walks, whilst the historic city of Chester with its famous city walls, cathedral and unique shops in the Rows is well worth a visit. Betws-y-Coed, the ’Gateway to the Snowdonia National Park’, is also within easy reach and offers outdoor clothing shops and the amazing Zip World Fforest. Beach 22 miles. Shop and pub 1½ mile, restaurant 4 miles.

reviews.comment: A good property for a large family celebration

We had the perfect family stay here, everything we needed for a family of 12 ranging from 4 years to 77 years. Although the location isn't the easiest to get to the views when you do are absolutely worth it. The hosts were so helpful from check in to any questions we had and even left us a little welcome pack. Would 100% recommend.

We were a family group of 13 plus one dog, ages ranging from 19 - 80.  The house accommodated us well, with space for us to spread out. It was very well equipped and we enjoyed the hot tub and outside space - the views are incredible. The lower ground has access to outside and is fairly self-contained with a bedroom, kitchenette area (hidden behind cupboard doors), a lounge and wet room (this could do with a bit of tlc and it’s trial and error to suss out the shower to stop the whole room flooding!). The upper ground floor has two bedrooms (one with en-suite), a separate toilet, the main lounge, utility room, children’s playroom plus two other reception rooms. The first floor is a large kitchen and a dining room with plenty of space to seat 14 around the large table.  Finally on the second floor there are four bedrooms, one with en-suite and two with a jack and jill bathroom. For our particular family group we felt that we would have benefited from another bathroom but that was mainly because we were all adult couples bar one. On the whole the property was clean and tidy albeit lots of cobwebs in places and a few dead flies. It seemed that the cleaners had been in straight after the last people left (a few weeks earlier?) but hadn’t been back just to give it a quick once over before we arrived. With large gaps between bookings this is something the owners may wish to consider. Also we hadn’t been left any tea towels, bin liners or gas for the BBQ and had to contact the owner who, to his credit, made a 2 1/2 round trip on the Saturday afternoon to sort out supplies. Unfortunately though, it being a Saturday afternoon, we couldn’t source any BBQ gas in Ruthin so had to make do with a disposable one for our planned BBQ that afternoon. Despite those few niggles we had a great time and don’t think that anyone would be disappointed with this property as it is ideal for large groups of all ages. The location is great (you soon get used to the lane leading to the house) being nearby to Ruthin. Other places we visited were Snowdonia (11 of us managed to climb Snowdon), Ffestiniogg Railway, Anglesey and Puffin Island, white water rafting at Canolfan Tryweryn and the Mach Loop so a good time was had by us all.

long_description: Situated in a picturesque, coastal position with spectacular views over Carmarthen Bay, this large, detached barn has been sympathetically converted to retain its original charm and character, making it an unforgettable experience for a family or groups looking to explore West Wales. This holiday property, adjacent to the owner’s home, is bursting with original character including original stone walls and beams, whilst lots of welcoming touches have been added for that homely feel throughout. For children and family entertainment, the barn boasts a spacious games room equipped with a pool and football table, a great distraction during inclement weather. Outside, guests can enjoy their large, lawned garden with a patio area, where they can sit, relax and unwind whilst watching the sun set over the idyllic bay. Carmarthenshire itself has lots on offer, including fantastic walks along the Millennium Coastal Path, which leads through scenic Pembrey Country Park, which is renowned for its dry ski slope, horse riding trails and 7 miles of beaches. For sports enthusiasts, visitors can enjoy a round of golf at the Jack Nicklaus course or watch live sport at the Llanelli Scartlets Rugby stadium and nearby Ffos Las racecourse. Away from the coast, the Carmarthenshire countryside is just as promising with its array of charming market towns and medieval castles including Kidwelly and Laugharne, or guests can visit the National Botanical Garden of Wales. Just a 60-minute drive away is the popular tourist resort of Tenby, with its cobbled streets, traditional Welsh pubs and thrilling leisure parks which are waiting to be explored. Beach ½ mile. Shop and pub 1 mile.

long_description:
Just a three-minute walk from the golden sands of Rhos-on-Sea, Rhos Sea Manor is an extraordinary luxury retreat sleeping up to twenty eight guests across thirteen bedrooms. Beautifully renovated and exquisitely presented throughout, this magnificent home is ideal for large family gatherings, milestone celebrations and memorable group holidays on the North Wales coast.
The extensive accommodation has been thoughtfully designed to combine elegance with flexibility. Most bedrooms can be arranged with either super-king-size beds or twin beds, making the property suitable for different generations and group arrangements. Several rooms also include sofa beds, while the impressive four-poster master bedroom provides a particularly luxurious retreat. Eleven bathrooms, including en-suite and Jack-and-Jill facilities, ensure guests have plenty of space and privacy.
Rhos Sea Manor’s exceptional leisure facilities make every stay feel like a private resort experience. Swim in the heated indoor pool while younger guests enjoy the separate children’s pool, then unwind in the sauna or sink into the bubbling hot tub. The private cinema is perfect for relaxed film nights, while the games room offers further entertainment for guests of all ages.
One of the home’s most distinctive features is its atmospheric cave bar, providing an unforgettable setting for drinks and conversation. Outside, the beautiful grounds offer space for children to play and adults to relax. Gather around the firepit as evening falls, cook together using the barbecue or pizza oven, and enjoy quality time in the fresh coastal air. Excellent private parking, Wi-Fi and a dedicated workspace add further convenience.
Rhos-on-Sea is a welcoming seaside town with an attractive promenade, independent shops and a varied selection of cafés, pubs and restaurants. Its broad sandy beach is perfect for paddling, picnics and family days beside the sea, while the small harbour and breakwater provide a pleasant destination for a gentle stroll.
The Wales Coast Path passes through the area, offering scenic walks towards Colwyn Bay and Llandudno. Visitors can also discover the tiny St Trillo’s Chapel beside the shore or explore Bryn Euryn Nature Reserve, where woodland trails lead to an ancient hillfort and far-reaching coastal views.
Families can visit the Welsh Mountain Zoo or enjoy the open spaces and leisure facilities at nearby Eirias Park. The Victorian resort of Llandudno is within easy reach, offering two beaches, a traditional pier and the magnificent Great Orme, which can be explored on foot, by historic tramway or aboard the seasonal cable car.
Historic Conwy provides another rewarding day out, with its imposing medieval castle, ancient town walls and picturesque harbour. Farther inland, Bodnant Garden and the mountains, lakes and forests of Eryri National Park offer endless opportunities for sightseeing and outdoor adventure. Combining outstanding facilities, luxurious accommodation and a superb coastal setting, Rhos Sea Manor promises an unforgettable North Wales escape.

The Wendover is a generous, stylish holiday home designed for big get-togethers, whether that’s family celebrations, milestone birthdays or a long overdue friends’ escape. Sleeping up to 16 guests across six comfortable bedrooms, it offers plenty of space to spread out without ever feeling disconnected.
The heart of the house is the large open-plan kitchen, dining and living area – a bright, sociable space made for shared meals, long chats and relaxed evenings together. The kitchen is well equipped for cooking for a crowd, while the living area invites everyone to kick back after a day out. Step outside and you’ll find the private hot tub, perfect for winding down under the stars with a drink in hand. Located above a friendly pub, The Wendover has a lively yet welcoming atmosphere, ideal for groups who enjoy being close to the action while still having their own private retreat.
Set in Towyn, the location puts you right in the middle of some of the region’s best scenery and attractions. Golden sandy beaches are just a short drive away, ideal for coastal walks, paddling or bracing sea swims. The surrounding countryside offers rolling hills, quiet lanes and scenic trails for walking and cycling, with Snowdonia within easy reach for more adventurous days out.
Nearby towns and villages provide local shops, cafés and traditional markets, while historic castles, coastal paths and family-friendly attractions are all close by. In the evenings, having a pub right below means you can enjoy a relaxed drink and good food without needing to travel, before heading back upstairs to your own space. The Wendover combines space, comfort and a brilliant North Wales location for a memorable group stay.

long_description:
Set in the peaceful Monmouthshire village of Llandevaud, High View House is a striking modern home designed for relaxing getaways, family gatherings and special occasions. Spread over three spacious floors, this detached six-bedroom property offers contemporary comfort, luxury touches and stunning rural views.
On the first floor, you’ll find two beautiful super king bedrooms, both with private ensuite facilities. The master suite features a free-standing bath, a double walk-in shower and elegant finishes throughout — the perfect space to unwind. The second super king bedroom also includes its own ensuite and a luxurious free-standing bath in the room, offering a boutique-hotel feel.
The ground floor is the heart of the home, featuring an impressive dining room with piano and doors opening onto a spacious balcony overlooking the countryside. There’s a gym for active guests and a games room equipped with a Wii and Xbox for family fun.
On the lower ground floor, there are four stylish king bedrooms, each with its own En-suite bathroom and TV — ideal for guests wanting comfort and privacy. This level also includes a laundry room, a pool and darts room, and a bar room – perfect for social evenings in.
Step outside to discover a large patio area with a hot tub, perfect for soaking up the views or relaxing under the stars. Beyond lies a spacious lawned garden, ideal for outdoor games or simply enjoying the fresh Welsh air.
Conveniently located near Newport and within easy reach of Cardiff and the Wye Valley, High View House combines rural tranquillity with modern luxury. Whether you’re celebrating, exploring, or simply unwinding, this exceptional home offers the space and style for an unforgettable stay.

long_description:
Set in the heart of the Anglesey countryside near Llanerchymedd, this stunning five star holiday let is an exceptional farmhouse retreat offering space, luxury and character in equal measure. Surrounded by rolling rural views and complete with a private hot tub, it provides the perfect setting for memorable group getaways, celebrations and family holidays.
Sleeping up to eighteen guests across six beautifully appointed bedrooms, this impressive property combines traditional charm with modern comfort. Five of the bedrooms benefit from stylish en-suite bathrooms, ensuring privacy and convenience for larger groups. Throughout the farmhouse, original character features have been carefully retained, adding warmth and authenticity. Highlights include the striking stained-glass feature window in the hall, original, and the beautiful Victorian tiled floor in the entrance porch, which offers an elegant first impression.
The main sitting room is both inviting and spacious, featuring comfortable seating, a Smart TV and a cosy log burner, ideal for relaxing evenings after a day exploring the island. A separate kitchen diner forms the social heart of the home, offering ample space and excellent facilities to cater for all guests. Well equipped for group dining, it is perfect for shared meals, celebrations and leisurely breakfasts overlooking the countryside.
Outside, the hot tub is perfectly positioned to take in uninterrupted rural views, offering a peaceful spot to unwind under the stars. The surrounding landscape provides a true sense of escape while remaining within easy reach of Anglesey’s most popular destinations.
The farmhouse is ideally located for exploring the island’s diverse attractions. The golden sands and water sports haven of Rhosneigr are just a short drive away, as are other stunning beaches including Trearddur Bay, Red Wharf Bay and Newborough Beach with its famous forest walks and views towards Llanddwyn Island. Guests can also enjoy visiting Beaumaris with its historic castle, and the dramatic coastal scenery along the Anglesey Coastal Path.
With its luxurious accommodation, retained historic features and superb location, this exceptional farmhouse in Llanerchymedd offers an unforgettable Anglesey escape for large groups seeking comfort, character and countryside tranquillity.
